## Job Cost & Reserves
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 11*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Job Cost & Reserves 

The Job Cost & Reserves application allows you to track and manage your company’s job costs and replacement 

reserves. 

If your company has a subscription for Replacement Reserves but not Job Cost, then you will not have access to 
any job cost-related items. A separate user guide is available for the standalone Replacement Reserves 
application. 

Job Cost 

Job costs are expenses associated with property improvements and new developments, from capital improvement 

projects to renovations to new construction. With the application’s job cost features, you can manage every phase 

of a project through completion. When your project is underway, you can manage all project documents to 

reduce errors, provide visibility, and enable efficient project management. 

Additionally, you can: 

• 
Customize cost codes to support work breakdown structures (WBS). 

• 
Track for unit-level costs in multifamily assets. 

• 
Track budget estimates, revisions, and final costs. 

• 
Track documents and permits. 

• 
Process draws with one or more funding sources. 

• 
Integrate draw requests with Corporate A/R and approval processes. 

• 
Customize views and reports. 

Replacement Reserves 

Replacement reserves are funds that are set aside to periodically replace or repair building components during the 

building’s economic life, such as roofs, parking lots, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems. 

With the application’s replacement reserves features, you can track replacement and repair expenses and then 

organize and package them as reimbursement requests to your lender(s). 

Additionally, you can: 

• 
Generate draw request packages with supporting documents to present to the lender for reimbursement 

• 
Maintain lender information in corporate Accounts Receivable 

• 
Apply receipts after funds are received 

• 
View a status inquiry report for reserve accounts.

#### Job Cost & Reserves Overview
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

Introduction to Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Job Cost & Reserves Overview 

Job Cost functions are split into configuration, setup, tasks, and reporting. 

Configuration 

Use the Configure Job Cost & Reserves (on page 487) page to manage your company’s job cost, 

journal, and draw posting settings. 

Setup 

Before you can add a job, you must set up the job framework. You must set up at least one cost 

structure, job type, draw model, and funding source to add and manage a job. The image below 

shows the order in which you must set up the job framework. 

• 
Cost structure definition: (on page 515) Use this page to manage and define the cost code 

structure. The structure definition dictates the structure tiers (levels) and defines the number 

of characters for each part of the structure detail. This page also allows you to access the 

Cost structure information page. 

You must set up at least one cost structure per set of cost codes that use different levels. For 

example, if you will track one job at the division level and another job at the sub-phase 

level, you must set up two cost structures. 

• 
Job types: (on page 522) Use this page to manage job types, which provide the cost codes 

for all jobs that use that job type. Job types inherit cost code structure from the cost 

structure definition assigned to the job type. This page also allows you to access the Job 

type information, Cost codes, and Cost code information pages. 

You must set up at least one job type per set of cost codes that you use on your jobs. 

• 
Draw models: (on page 554) Use this page to manage job cost draw models, which 

organize cost codes into draw model details or lender categories. These are typically budget 

---


<!-- Page 15 -->
Chapter 1: Introduction to Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

categories provided by your funding sources. This page also allows you to access the Draw 

model, Draw model details, and Assign cost code pages. 

• 
Funding sources: (on page 592) Use this page to manage funding sources, which are 

lenders for your jobs. This page also allows you to access the Funding source information 

page. 

• 
Permits: (on page 498) Use this page to manage permit categories, which group permit or 

document attachments by type or function. This page also allows you to access the Permit 

information page. 

Tasks 

The image below shows the typical workflow of a job. 

• 
Jobs: (on page 17) Use this page to manage jobs, which organize the costs, budgets, 

activities, and draws associated with an entity job. This page also allows you to access the 

Job information page. 

Each job is assigned to an entity, the site where construction takes place. The job’s costs 

apply to the entity’s balance sheet or income statement. Typically, job costs are assigned to 

a Work in Process account on the entity’s balance sheet. 

• 
Budgets: (on page 344) Use this page to manage budgets, which record the spending limits 

of each cost code for the job. This page also allows you to access the Budget page. 

• 
Job segment budgets: (on page 94) Use this page to manage job segment budgets, which 

track budgets and costs at the segment level. This page also allows you to access the Job 

segment budget page. 

In Job Cost & Reserves, segments are units within a multi-family building. Typically, unit 

renovation jobs track at the segment level. 

• 
Draws: Use this page to manage draws, which arrange job costs for funding source 

approval. This page also allows you to access the Draw information page. 

• 
Activity: (on page 90) Use this page to view the Job Cost activity list, which lists all Job Cost 

A/P invoices and journal entries.

Reporting 

The pages that allow you to review job budget and cost code information include: 

• 
Job status inquiry: (on page 166) Use this page to view a summary of the job, including the 

job’s budgets, costs, and commitments. This page also allows you to access the Budget 

details, Pending commitments, Approved commitments, Open commitments, and Cost 

details pages. 

• 
Segments: (on page 503) Use this page to view job segments, which track budgets and 

costs at the segment (unit) level. This page also allows you to access the Job segment 

information page. 

In Job Cost & Reserves, segments are units within a multi-family building. Typically, unit 

renovation jobs track at the segment level. 

• 
Cost code structure: (on page 444) Use this page to filter and view the Cost Code Structure 

report. 

• 
Job setup summary: (on page 435) Use this page to filter and view the Job Setup Summary 

report.

Job Cost & Reserves Permissions 

In RealPage Financial Suite, your access is determined by your company’s subscriptions and 

permissions, and by your user permissions. Your account has both a user type and unique 

permissions that grant access throughout the system. 

If you do not see an option on the menu, ask your system administrator to check your 

permissions and user type. 

For more information about permissions, roles, and user types, see User Types and Permissions or 

ask your system administrator for assistance.

#### Jobs List

##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 27*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Jobs List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs`


Use the Jobs list to view and manage jobs, job budgets, and job status inquiries. From this page, 

you can: 

• 
Add, view, edit, and delete jobs. 

• 
Import and export job records. 

• 
View job status inquiries. 

• 
Manage job budgets. 

• 
Enter or import monthly budgets for a job. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Before you can add a job, you must first configure Job Cost & Reserves settings for your 

company, and then set up cost structures (on page 515), job types (on page 522), cost codes (on 

page 528), draw models (on page 554), draw model details (on page 561), funding sources (on 

page 592), and permits (on page 498). 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage jobs: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Job Cost 
Job 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete, Close 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

---



##### Adding a Job
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 28*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding a Job 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
 Jobs`


To add a job, complete the following tabs on the Job information page: 

• 
Job information 

• 
Dates 

• 
Billing 

• 
Permits and attachments 

• 
Reporting codes 

• 
Authorized users 

To add funding sources or units to the job, you must edit the job, and then enter your changes. 

Adding Job Information 

The Job information tab contains general information about the job. 

1. 
If the job is a child of a parent job, select the Has parent check box, and then select the 

parent job from the Parent job drop-down list. The Job type field automatically populates 

with the job type (on page 522) assigned to the parent job. 

Otherwise, use the Property drop-down list to select which property the job is for. 

2. 
In the Job name field, type a name for the job.  

3. 
Optionally, in the Job name abbr. field, type an abbreviation for the job name.  

4. 
Use the Job type drop-down list to select the job type.  

If this is a child job, the Job type field pre-populates with the job type assigned to the 
parent job. 

5. 
In the Job description field, type a brief description for the job.  

6. 
In the Job status drop-down list, select the job’s current status: 

• 
Pending: The job has not started. In this status, the system does not track budget 

changes. 

• 
Active: The job is in progress. In this status, the system does not track budget changes. 

• 
Active (budget locked): The job is in progress. In this status, you must submit change 

order requests to update budgets for the job. If the change order request is approved, 

then the system tracks that budget change.  

• 
Closed: The job is completed and has been closed. In this status, budgets are locked. 

• 
Complete (not closed): The job is completed but has not been closed. In this status, 

budgets are locked. 

---


<!-- Page 29 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

• 
Canceled: The job was canceled and is no longer in progress. You cannot create a 

transaction, A/P invoice, journal entry, or purchase order for a canceled job. 

• 
Inactive: The job is inactive. You cannot create a transaction, A/P invoice, journal entry, 

or purchase order for an inactivated job. 

7. 
In the Ship to contact drop-down list, assign a shipping contact to the job. 

8. 
If you have integrated Job Cost with Procore (on page 489), then an additional check box 

labeled Include this job when syncing to Procore appears. Typically, you would use this 

field to flag existing job records before exporting them to Procore; however, if you are 

adding a new job record and you plan to sync it with Procore at a later time, then you can 

select it now.  

9. 
If the job will be billed to a specific tenant, fill in the Lease information section: 

• 
Select the tenant from the Tenant drop-down list. 

• 
Select the associated lease from the Lease drop-down list. 

Adding Dates 

The fields on Dates tab are for informational purposes only and do not affect any job cost 

functions. However, they do appear on the Job Status Summary and Job Setup Summary reports. 

1. 
In the Begin date field, type or select the date that the job began.  

2. 
In the Completion date – Estimated field, type or select the date estimated for completing 

the job. 

3. 
In the Completion date – Required field, type or select the date by which the job must be 

completed. 

4. 
In the Completion date – Actual field, type or select the date on which the job was actually 

completed. If the job is still in progress, leave this field blank. 

Adding Billing Information 

The Billing tab appears only when you select a job type (on page 522) that is billable (the Billable 

check box must be selected for that job type). On this tab, you can add either customer billing 

information or internal billing information. 

To add customer billing information: 

1. 
Fill in the Billing information section. 

• 
In the Billing type drop-down list, select “Customer billing”. 

• 
In the Billing account (credit) drop-down list, select the account to bill. 

• 
In the Construction allowance field, type the amount that the tenant is allowed for 

build-out expenses. 

• 
In the Cost of goods sold (debit) drop-down list, select the G/L account to debit. 

---


<!-- Page 30 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
In the Markup percent field, type the percent markup on the tenant cost. 

2. 
Fill in the Construction fee section: 

• 
In the Customer drop-down list, select the customer or property paying the fee. 

• 
In the A/R account (debit) drop-down list, select the G/L account for the A/R portion 

of the construction fee. 

• 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select the vendor receiving the construction fee. 

• 
In the Percent field, type the vendor fee percentage for the service. 

• 
In the Cost code drop-down list, select the cost code for the job to which the 

construction fee is booked. 

The system applies the construction fee when closing the job. 

To add internal billing information: 

1. 
In the Billing type drop-down list, select “Internal billing”. 

2. 
In the Bill to option drop-down list, select whether you want to “Bill to job” or “Bill to 

property”. 

3. 
If you selected the “Bill to job” option: 

• 
Use the Job to bill drop-down list to select the job to bill. 

• 
Use the Job to bill cost code drop-down list to select the billing cost code. 

• 
Use the Account to credit on (property name)’s books drop-down list to select the 

account to credit. 

4. 
If you selected the “Bill to property” option: 

• 
Use the Property to bill drop-down list to select the property to bill. 

• 
Use the Account to credit on (property name)’s books drop-down list to select the 

account to credit. 

This field name references the job property you selected from the Property 
drop-down list on the Job information tab. 

• 
Use the Account to debit on (property to bill)’s books drop-down list to select the 

account to debit. 

This field name references the property you selected as the Property to bill on the 

Billing tab. 

5. 
In the Markup percent field, type the percent markup, if any. 

You can receive the funds in the Billing batches section after generating a tenant invoice (on page 

385) for internal billing: 

---


<!-- Page 31 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

1. 
Click the Receive funds button. 

2. 
In the Date received field, select the fund receipt date. 

3. 
In the Amount received field, enter the fund amount received. 

4. 
In the Document number field, enter the billing transaction number. 

5. 
In the Cash account drop-down list, select the G/L account to use when posting receipts. 

6. 
In the Loans payable account drop-down list, select the G/L account to use when 

generating the invoice. 

Adding Permits and Attachments 

1. 
In the General section, to add a general attachment to the job, select the attachment from 

the Attachments drop-down list.  

You can only add one general attachment per job. To view the attachment, click the  
icon. 

2. 
In the Permits section, to add a permit attachment to the job, select the permit type from 

the Permit drop-down list, and then select an attachment from the Attachment drop-down 

list.  

• 
To add a permit row to the job, click 
 Add.  

• 
To remove a permit row from the job, click 
 Remove.  

• 
To re-order a permit row, click 
 Sort for that row, and then drag and drop the 

permit to the desired spot. 

Adding Job Reporting Codes 

Use this tab to assign job reporting codes (on page 547) to the job. 

• 
The Code description column lists all job reporting codes defined in your system. Use the 

corresponding Code value drop-down list to assign a code value to the job reporting code. 

Adding Authorized Users 

Use this tab to restrict the users who can view and manage the job. The pages that only these 

users are authorized to access include: 

• 
Reports 

• 
Setup 

• 
Job Status Inquiry 

• 
Draws 

• 
Close Job 

---


<!-- Page 32 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

To add an authorized user: 

1. 
Click the Add authorized users button. 

The Select authorized users box opens with a list of users that have Job Cost permissions. 

2. 
Select the check box(es) next to the user(s) who you want to authorize for this job. 

3. 
Click the Add selected users button at the bottom of the list. 

The Users authorized to this job section updates with a list of selected users.  

If there are no users listed on a job, then all users with appropriate role permissions can 
access the job. 

If you authorize a single user for a job, then the system automatically assigns all full 
administrators to the job, limited to the permissions configured for their specific user ID. 
Authorizing a single user for a job also triggers a function that says, “No other users can 
access, unless they are listed as well. ” This access is job -specific, so you do not need to 
add authorized users to other jobs if no single user has been added. 

Saving the Job Record 

When you have finished filling in the fields on each tab, click Save. Alternatively, click More 

actions, and then click Save and new to save the job and open a new, blank job record. 

When you add a new job, the system automatically creates empty budgets for each job cost code. 

You can export the list of budgets to a CSV file and then re-import the file with the budget details 

instead of entering each cost code budget manually. See Importing a Job Budget (on page 34) for 

more information.

##### Editing a Job
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 33*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Editing a Job 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Edit`


Some tabs and features on the Job information page are available only when you edit a job. This 

includes: 

• 
The Units tab 

• 
The Funding sources tab 

• 
The Owner history tab (if the job has been transferred from a different property) 

• 
The Recalculate job totals, Transfer job, and Sync to Procore buttons on the Job 

information tab 

To edit a job: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Search & find section, click the Jobs menu option. 

The Jobs list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the job that you want to edit.  

4. 
Edit the fields on each tab as needed.  

• 
See Adding a Job (on page 18) for instructions on filling in job information, dates, 

billing, permits and attachments, reporting codes, and authorized users. 

• 
See Recalculating Job Totals (on page 26) for instructions on updating the job’s 

budget and cost totals. 

• 
See Transferring a Job to Another Property (on page 26) for instructions on 

transferring the ownership of the job to another property. 

• 
See Adding Units to a Job (on page 29) for instructions on assigning units to the job. 

• 
See Adding Funding Sources to a Job (on page 31) for instructions on adding funding 

sources to the job. 

• 
See Syncing a Job to Procore (on page 33) for instructions on exporting the job to 

Procore. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save.

#### Job Information Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 35*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Job Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
 Jobs`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > View/Edit`


Use the Job information page to create and manage jobs in RealPage Financial Suite. 

Page Overview 

From this page, you can: 

• 
Add, view, edit, duplicate, or delete jobs. 

• 
Add billing information for a job. 

• 
Add units to a job to track job segment budgets, unit renovation dates, and unit rent 

changes. 

• 
Configure funding sources for a job. 

• 
Upload permits or attachments for a job. 

• 
Assign reporting codes to a job. 

• 
Restrict the users authorized for a job. 

• 
Recalculate job totals. 

• 
Transfer a job to a different property. 

• 
Reopen all closed cost codes. 

• 
Sync job information to Procore (integration required). 

Conditional Tabs 

Some tabs and buttons on the Job information page are dependent on other settings or 

conditions: 

• 
The Billing tab appears only when the job type is billable (the Billable check box must be 

selected for that job type). 

• 
The Units tab appears only if you enable segments in the job type and only if you are in Edit 

or View mode. 

• 
The Funding sources tab appears only if you are in Edit or View mode. 

• 
The Owner history tab appears only if you are in Edit or View mode, and only if the job has 

been transferred from a different property. 

Conditional Actions 

The buttons on the Job information tab are dependent on other settings or conditions: 

• 
The Recalculate job totals button appears only if you are in Edit mode. 

• 
The Transfer job button appears only if you are in Edit mode. 

---

• 
The Reopen closed cost codes button appears only if there are any closed cost codes 

associated with the job. 

• 
The Sync to Procore button appears only if you configure the Procore integration (on page 

489) on the Configure Job Cost & Reserves page. 

Recalculating Job Totals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Edit > Job 
Information > Recalculate Job Totals`


Use the Recalculate job totals button in the job record to update the job’s budgeted amounts 

and costs. These totals are included next to the job in the Jobs list. 

To recalculate totals for a job: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, click the Edit link next to the job record. 

2. 
On the Job information tab, click the Recalculate job totals button. 

The system updates the budget and cost totals, taking into consideration any changes made 

to the job’s budget and any new invoices created for the job. 

Transferring a Job to Another Property 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Edit`


You can transfer the ownership of a job to a different property using the Transfer job button on 

the Job information tab of the job record. After you transfer a job, you can view its transfer 

history on the Owner history tab. 

To transfer a job: 

1. 
On the Job information tab, click the Transfer job button. 

---


<!-- Page 37 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

The Transfer job box opens. 

2. 
In the New property drop-down list, select the property to which you want to transfer the 

job. 

This links the job to the new property such that all future costs will update the new owning 
entity ’s balance sheet. You will need to create a journal entry moving the WIP balance from 
one entity to the other. 

3. 
In the Change date field, type or select the effective date of transfer. 

4. 
Optionally, in the Comment field, type a reason or memo for the job transfer. 

5. 
Click the Transfer button.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 38*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

A new tab labeled Owner history appears on the Job information page containing a history 

of properties that have owned the job and the transfer date. 

Reopening a Job’s Closed Cost Codes 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Edit`


You can reopen closed cost codes associated with a job so that users can continue posting job 

activity to cost categories that were previously locked; for example, to make changes after a cost 

category was prematurely or mistakenly finalized.  

Common reasons for reopening cost codes include: 

• 
Missed or late transactions: An invoice, expense, or adjustment comes in after the cost 

code was closed. 

• 
Corrections or reclassifications: Costs need to be fixed, moved, or adjusted for accuracy. 

• 
Budget updates: Additional work is approved, requiring new costs to be tracked under the 

same code. 

• 
Job not actually complete: The work tied to that cost code wasn’t finished, and more 

activity is expected. 

• 
Audit or reconciliation findings: Finance identifies discrepancies that require updates to 

historical costs. 

When a cost code is reopened, you can post new transactions, adjust or correct existing costs, or 

update budgets and actuals.  

Before You Begin 

Before completing these steps, keep the following in mind: 

• 
The Reopen closed cost codes button appears only if there are closed cost codes linked to 

the job. 

• 
Clicking this button reopens all of the job’s closed cost codes. 

---

• 
Reopening a cost code allows changes to finalized data, which may affect reporting, audit 

trails, and budget control. 

Procedures 

To reopen a job’s cost codes: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application. 

2. 
On the All tab, go to the Search & Find section, and then select the Jobs menu option. 

The Open jobs list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the desired job. 

The Job information page opens on the Job information tab. 

4. 
Click the Reopen closed cost codes button. 

5. 
Click OK to confirm.

Tracking Job Expenses for a Unit 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Edit > Units`


In the Job Cost & Reserves application, segments—also known as units—are used to track 

budgets and costs for each multi-family apartment unit in a building renovation. You can also 

track the cost of rent for each unit before and after the renovation is completed. The system 

automatically calculates and displays the change in rent. 

To track job expenses for a unit: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Search & find section, click the Jobs menu option. 

The Jobs list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the job where the unit is located. 

The Job information page opens. 

4. 
Click the Units tab. 

5. 
If there aren’t any units assigned to the job yet, add them now. See Adding Units to a Job 

(on page 29) for more information. 

6. 
Use the fields in the Expenses may be tracked for the following units section to keep track of 

expenses for each unit: 

• 
Estimated start date: Type or select the estimated start date for the unit renovation. 

• 
Estimated completion date: Type or select the estimated completion date for the unit 

renovation. 

• 
Actual start date: Type or select the date that the unit renovation began. 

• 
Actual completion date: Type or select the date that the unit renovation was 

completed. 

• 
Rent before: Type the unit’s rent before the renovation.  

• 
Rent after: Type the unit’s rent after the renovation. 

• 
Rent change: This is the amount that the rent changed after the renovation. 

7. 
Click the Save button to save any changes you make while tracking unit expenses.

Syncing a Job to Procore 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Edit > Job 
Information > Sync to Procore`


Use the Sync to Procore button in the job record to manually sync an individual job to Procore. 

This button appears only under the following conditions: 

• 
You are licensed to integrate with Procore’s construction management software. 

• 
You have enabled the Procore integration feature on the Configure Job Cost & Reserves 

page. 

• 
You have opened the Job information page in Edit mode. 

For instructions on syncing multiple jobs to Procore, see Integrating Job Cost with Procore (on 
page 489 ). 

To sync a job to Procore: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, click the Edit link next to the job record. 

2. 
On the Job information tab, click the Sync to Procore button. 

The system adds the export to the offline queue for processing and sends you a 

confirmation email when processing is complete. If there are any errors while syncing, then 

an entry will appear in the External queue exceptions log with a description of the error.

##### Importing a Job Budget

Importing a Job Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Budgets by Job`


When you add a new job, the system automatically creates empty budgets for each job cost code. 

You can export the list of budgets to a CSV file and then re-import the file with the budget details 

instead of entering each cost code budget manually. 

You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 
status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 
information, see Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354 ). 

To import a cost code budget: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, select the Budgets by job link next to the desired job. 

The (Job Name) - Budgets page opens with a list of budget details for each of the job’s cost 

codes. 

2. 
On the Budgets page, click Export budgets template. 

• 
If the job type includes segments, click Budget to start the download process. 

• 
If the job type does not include segments, the system immediately starts the 

download process. 

The system either downloads the chartexport-(job name).csv or prompts you to open or 

save the chartexport-(job name).csv file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the chartexport-(job name).csv file. 

The file automatically provides information for some fields: 

• 
JOB NAME: This is the name of the job. 

• 
COST CODE: This is the code of the cost code. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: This is a description of the cost code. 

4. 
In the BUDGET column for each budgeted cost code, enter the budget amount of that cost 

code. 

For all cost codes that do not have a budget for the job, leave the BUDGET column as “0”. 

The example below shows a cost code budget import list. 

---


<!-- Page 46 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as.  

6. 
In the Save as box, use the Save as type drop-down list to select “CSV (comma delimited) 

(*.csv).” 

7. 
Change the File name or location as needed, and then click Save. 

8. 
On the (Job Name) - Budgets page, click Import. The system opens the Import budget 

information box. 

9. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

10. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

11. 
Click Done. 

12. 
If you are adding unit- or segment-level budgets, you must add those budgets separately. 

For more information, see Importing a Job Segment Budget (on page 96). If you are not 

tracking segment-level budgets for the job, you can skip this step. 

For more information about importing data, see Importing in RealPage Accounting.

##### Importing Job Budgets by Month
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 48*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Importing Job Budgets by Month 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Budgets by Month`


Use this process to import job budgets on a monthly basis to provide more granular reporting. 

You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 
status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 
information, see Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354 ). 

To import a monthly job budget: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, select the Budgets by month link next to the desired job. 

The Budget by month page opens. 

2. 
In the Select job drop-down list, select the job for which you are importing a budget. 

The Begin date and Completion date - required fields must be defined for the job before 
you can continue. 

3. 
Click the Download budgets by month template link. 

The system either downloads the CSV file or prompts you to open or save the CSV file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

4. 
Open the (Job Name) Monthly Budget.csv file. 

The template automatically populates data for some of the fields based on the job you 

selected: 

• 
Cost code: This is the cost code number and description. 

• 
CO#: This is the change order number for the corresponding cost code. If a budget 

change order was submitted, then an additional row appears for the cost code with 

the budget changes. Change orders are listed sequentially under the cost code’s 

original budget. For example, if you have three change orders, then three rows will 

appear under the original budget as CO# 1, 2, and 3. 

You do not need to make changes to this column in the template. 

• 
BUDGET: This is either the total amount originally budgeted for the cost code or the 

budget change amount. 

A positive amount in the BUDGET column is added to the original budget. A negative 
amount is subtracted from the original budget. 

5. 
In the monthly reporting period columns, fill in the monthly budget amounts for each cost 

code as needed. 

---

The columns correspond with the Begin date and Completion date - required fields in the 
job record. For example, if the job begins on 2/15 and ends on 5/31, then a column appears 
for each month during that time period (February, March, April, May). 

6. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

7. 
On the Budget by month page, click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file to 

import it back into the system. 

A table appears with the imported budget information. Header accounts (cost codes that 

did not have a WIP account) do not appear in the table. 

8. 
Click Done. 

After you’ve imported a job’s budget, you can return to the Budget by month page to 

manually edit or update budget amounts. If the budget is locked, then you have to submit a 

change order to edit the budget. 

What’s Next? 

Set up budgets for each job. For more information, see Job Budgets (on page 344).

#### Draw Workbench Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 60*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Draw Workbench Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench`


Use the Draw workbench page to manage draws for job cost construction lending and for 

replacement reserve escrow requests. A draw summarizes invoiced costs by combining job activity 

into predetermined categories. When it’s summarized, you can provide the draw to the funding 

sources of the job. Draws include invoices as proof of service and material costs from vendors and 

subcontractors.  

From this page, you can: 

• 
Filter draws. 

• 
Add draws. 

• 
View and edit draws. 

• 
Add and reverse draw activities. 

• 
Export the draws list. 

• 
Create and save a custom workbench view. 

If you subscribed to the standalone Replacement Reserves application without Job Cost, then 
the Draw workbench will include only replacement reserve draws.

##### Filtering the Draw Workbench
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 62*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Filtering the Draw Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench`


You can filter the Draw workbench list to display specific job cost draws or replacement reserve 

draws and then save the filtered view for future use. Filters are retained even after you view or 

edit a draw so that you don’t have to reapply the same filters when you return to the workbench. 

If you subscribed to the standalone Replacement Reserves application without Job Cost, then 
the Draw workbench will include only replacement reserve draws. 

Filtering the Draw Workbench 

To filter by job cost draws: 

1. 
Select the Job cost option. 

2. 
If you want to filter draws for a particular property, select the property from the Property 

name drop-down list. 

3. 
If you want to filter draws for a particular job, select the job from the Job name drop-down 

list.  

4. 
Use the Status drop-down list to filter for open or posted draws. 

The list of draws automatically refreshes with your filter selections. 

To filter by replacement reserve draws: 

1. 
Select the Replacement reserves option. 

2. 
If you want to filter draws for a particular reserve, select the reserve from the Reserve name 

drop-down list. 

3. 
Use the Status drop-down list to filter for open or posted draws. 

The list of draws automatically refreshes with your filter selections. 

Saving and Applying a Custom View 

You can save your filter settings to reapply the same workbench view in the future. 

To save a custom view: 

1. 
After you apply your filters, click the Save view as button in the upper-right corner. 

The Save view as box opens. 

2. 
In the View name field, type a name for the custom view. 

3. 
Select the Default view check box if you want to set the view as your default view. 

4. 
Select the Make public check box if you want to share the view with other users. 

---


<!-- Page 63 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

5. 
Click Save. 

The view is added to the Apply view drop-down list.  

To apply a custom view: 

1. 
Select the view from the Apply view drop-down list. 

2. 
Click the Apply button. 

Updating a Custom View 

To update a custom view: 

1. 
First, select the view that you want to update from the Apply view drop-down list. 

2. 
Update the view’s filter selections as needed. 

3. 
Click the Update view button in the upper-right corner. 

The Save view as box opens. 

4. 
Edit the view settings as needed. 

You cannot change the View name. 

5. 
Click Save.

##### Importing Job Cost or Replacement Reserve Draws
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 66*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing Job Cost or Replacement Reserve Draws 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > Import Draws`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the import template for job cost and replacement reserve draws: 

1. 
In the Company application, click the All tab, and then click the Import data menu option. 

The Company setup checklist page opens. 

2. 
In the Set up Job Cost section, click the Template link next to Draw. 

The system either downloads the Draw.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the Draw.xls file and populate the draw information: 

• 
Job/Reserve name: Type the name of the job or replacement reserve to which the 

draw applies. Make sure it matches the name of the job or reserve as it appears in the 

Jobs list (on page 17) or Reserves list (on page 362), respectively. 

• 
Funding source: This field applies only to job cost draws. Type the primary funding 

source of the draw. Make sure it matches the name of the funding source as it appears 

in the Funding source list (on page 592) for job cost. 

This also determines the draw model of the draw.  

• 
Funding source option: This field applies only to job cost draws. Type one of the 

following values: 

• 
Single source: This option allocates the full draw to one funding source. 

• 
Multiple sources: This option allocates the draw to funding sources by line item 

or applies individual line items to multiple funding sources. 

• 
Multiple sources allocated by percent: This option allocates the draw to funding 

sources based on the percentages entered on the Job information page. 

• 
Multiple sources allocated by amount: This option allocates the draw to funding 

sources based on specific amounts. 

---


<!-- Page 67 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

• 
Draw name: Type the draw name. 

• 
Draw number: Type the draw number. 

• 
Draw date: Type the date of the draw. 

• 
Additional jobs: This field applies only to job cost draws. Type the names of any 

additional jobs in the draw, separated by commas. Make sure each job matches the 

name of the job as it appears in the Jobs list (on page 17). 

4. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

Importing Data From the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
On the Company setup checklist page, find the Set up Job Cost section, and then click the 

Import link next to Draw. 

You can also click the Import draws button on the Draw workbench page. 

The Import box opens. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button.

##### Adding Single Source Job Cost Draw Activity
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 69*

Managing Draw Activity and Allocations 

The Funding source option selected in the draw determines how you attach activity to the draw. 

For more information, see the related topics: 

• 
Adding Single Source Draw Activity (on page 59) 

• 
Adding Multiple Source Draw Activity (on page 60) 

• 
Adding Allocated by Percent Draw Activity (on page 61) 

• 
Adding Allocated by Amount Draw Activity (on page 62) 

• 
Reversing Draw Activity (on page 63) 

Replacement reserve draws are always allocated to a single funding source.  

Adding Single Source Job Cost Draw Activity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > Add Activity`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > View > Activity > Add Activity`


To add activity to a single source type draw:  

1. 
In the Draw workbench list, find the desired draw, and then click the Add activity link in the 

Actions column. 

The Draw information page opens with two lists: 

• 
Items included in this draw: This lists all transaction line items included in the draw. 

• 
Items not yet included on a draw: This lists all of the job’s transaction line items that 

are not included in any draw. 

You can also access this page by clicking the View link next to the draw, and then selecting 
the Add activity link on the Activity tab. 

2. 
To add a single line item to the draw, click the Include link for the desired line item. 

Alternatively, to add all open items to the draw, click the Include all items link.  

To remove a line item from the draw, click the Exclude link for the desired line item. 

3. 
When your changes are complete, click Save. 

---



##### Adding Multiple Source Job Cost Draw Activity
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 70*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding Multiple Source Job Cost Draw Activity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > Add Activity`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > View > Activity > Add Activity`


To add activity to a multiple funding sources type draw:  

1. 
In the Draw workbench list, find the desired draw, and then click the Add activity link in the 

Actions column. 

The Draw information page opens with two lists: 

• 
Items included in this draw: This lists all transaction line items included in the draw. 

• 
Items not yet included on a draw: This lists all of the job’s transaction line items that 

are not included in any draw. 

You can also access this page by clicking the View link next to the draw, and then selecting 
the Add activity link on the Activity tab. 

2. 
To add a single line item to the draw, click the Include link for the desired line item. 

Alternatively, to add all open items to the draw, click the Include all items link.  

To remove a line item from the draw, click the Exclude link for the desired line item. 

3. 
Click the Allocate link for a line item in the draw. 

The Allocate item to multiple funding sources box opens. 

4. 
On the first funding row:  

• 
Use the Funding source drop-down list to select a funding source that is paying the 

line item. 

• 
In the Amount field, enter the amount that this funding source is paying the line item. 

If the line item is being paid by multiple funding sources, complete a funding row for each 
funding source that is paying the line item. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Apply allocation. 

6. 
Repeat steps 4 through 7 for each line item you want to add to the draw.  

7. 
When your changes are complete, click Save. 

If you print the draw schedule, the allocation split shows at the top of the schedule.

##### Adding Job Cost Draw Activity Allocated by Percent
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 71*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Adding Job Cost Draw Activity Allocated by Percent 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > Add/Reverse Activity`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > View > Activity > Add Activity`


To add activity to multiple funding sources allocated by percent type draw: 

1. 
In the Draw workbench list, find the desired draw, and then click the Add activity link in the 

Actions column. 

The Draw information page opens with two lists: 

• 
Items included in this draw: This lists all transaction line items included in the draw. 

• 
Items not yet included on a draw: This lists all of the job’s transaction line items that 

are not included in any draw. 

You can also access this page by clicking the View link next to the draw, and then selecting 
the Add activity link on the Activity tab. 

2. 
To add a single line item to the draw, click the Include link for the desired line item. 

Alternatively, to add all open items to the draw, click the Include all items link.  

To remove a line item from the draw, click the Exclude link for the desired line item. 

3. 
Click the Allocate link for a line item on the draw. 

The Allocate item to multiple funding sources box opens. Each line item is automatically 

allocated to the funding sources assigned to the job, based on the percentages entered on 

the Funding sources tab. 

For example, assume you are allocating a $500.00 line item that is 75% funded by Hartford 

Savings and 25% funded by F&D Trust. When you view the Allocate item to multiple 

funding sources box, the system automatically allocates $375.00 to Hartford Savings and 

$125.00 to F&D Trust. 

4. 
To manually change any funding allocation, in the Amount field, enter the amount that this 

funding source is paying the line item. 

You must also update any additional line items so that the total allocation equals the line 

item amount. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Apply allocation. 

6. 
Repeat steps 5 – 7 for each line item included on the draw.  

7. 
When your changes are complete, click Save. 

If you print the draw schedule, the allocation split shows at the top of the schedule.

##### Posting a Draw Schedule

##### Printing or Exporting a Draw Schedule Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 76*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Posting a Draw Schedule 

As a best practice, before you post a draw schedule, print the draw schedule and verify that it is 

accurate. For more information, see Printing a Draw Schedule (on page 66). 

Posting a draw schedule moves the draw amounts from the current draw column of the view and 

the report to the previously drawn column.  

You can no longer make adjustments to a draw after posting. We recommend waiting to post the 
draw until after you receive funding.  

To post a draw schedule: 

1. 
Locate the draw you want to post, and then click the View link. 

2. 
Click Post draw schedule. 

A confirmation message shows when the draw posts.  

If you selected the Balance sheet A/R account (debit) check box during Job Cost 

configuration (on page 487), the system generates an A/R invoice for each applicable 

funding source that has a customer assigned to it in Job Cost setup. 

Printing or Exporting a Draw Schedule Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Draw Workbench > View 
> Print/Export Draw Schedule`


To print or export a Draw Schedule report: 

1. 
In the Draw workbench list, click the View link next to the draw whose draw schedule you 

want to print or export. 

The Draw information page opens on the Draw schedule tab. 

2. 
In the Draw schedule section, click the Show reporting and packaging options link. 

A series of reporting and packaging options appears. 

3. 
In the Draw schedule report options section, select which funding sources to include in the 

report: 

• 
Include all sources: Includes all funding sources in the report.  

• 
Include used sources: Includes used funding sources in the report. 

• 
Include no sources: Excludes all funding sources from the report. 

4. 
Click the Print draw schedule or Export draw schedule button. 

• 
If you are printing, a new window opens with the Draw Schedule report in a printable 

format. 

• 
If you are exporting, the Draw Schedule report exports to an Excel file.

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Printing or Exporting a Draw Schedule Detail Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Draw Workbench > View 
> Print/Export Draw Schedule Details`


To print or export the Draw Schedule Detail report for a draw: 

1. 
Locate the draw you want to print or export in the Draw workbench list, and then click the 

View link. 

The Draw information page opens on the Draw schedule tab. 

2. 
In the Draw schedule section, click the Show reporting and packaging options link. 

A series of reporting and packaging options appears. 

3. 
In the Draw schedule report options section, select which funding sources to include in the 

report: 

• 
Include all sources: Includes all funding sources in the report. 

• 
Include used sources: Includes used funding sources in the report. 

• 
Include no sources: Excludes all funding sources from the report. 

4. 
In the Draw schedule detail report options section, select whether to include cost codes in 

the report: 

• 
Include cost code column: Displays the Cost code column in the report. 

• 
Exclude cost code column: Hides the Cost code column from the report. 

5. 
In the same section, select whether to include or exclude invoice totals: 

• 
Include invoice totals: Displays additional rows in the report showing the total amount 

paid for each invoice.  

• 
Exclude invoice totals: Hides rows from the report showing the total amount paid for 

each invoice. 

6. 
If you want to split the columns in the report for A/P invoices and journal entries, then select 

the Split AP/GL information check box. 

• 
If you don’t select this option, then by default the report includes two 

columns—Vendor name and Invoice number—for both A/P invoices and journal 

entries. For journal entries, the Vendor name represents the G/L account name and 

the Invoice number represents the journal entry number. 

• 
If you do select this option, then the report includes four columns—Vendor name, 

Invoice number, G/L account, and G/L batch—to display the A/P invoice and journal 

entry information separately. For journal entries, the Vendor name represents the G/L 

account name, the Account number represents the G/L account number, and the G/L 

batch represents the journal entry number.

Click the Print draw schedule details or Export draw schedule details button.

Assign reserve accounts to draw model lines so that activity is included in the appropriate 

categories on a draw. 

Changes to reserve account assignments apply only to draws that have not yet been posted. 

Before You Begin 

Before you get started, review the Reserve accounts list. This list includes all available reserve 

accounts, even ones that are not currently assigned to a draw model line. The Assign reserve 

accounts page displays only reserve accounts that haven’t been mapped to a lender category.

Procedures 

To assign reserve accounts: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the 

Setup tab. 

If you do not have a Job Cost subscription, select the standalone Replacement Reserves 
application instead. 

2. 
In the Draw models section, select the Replacement reserves menu option. 

The Draw models list opens. 

3. 
Click the Draw model details link next to the desired draw model. 

The Draw model details list opens. 

4. 
Click the Assign reserve accounts button at the top of the page. 

The Assign reserve accounts page opens. 

5. 
Drag a reserve account to the appropriate line in the Draw model details list. 

• 
Repeat as needed. Each reserve account can be assigned to only one line. 

• 
To remove an assignment, drag the reserve account back to the Reserve accounts list. 

6. 
Click Save.

##### Receiving and Posting Draw Receipts
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 84*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Receiving and Posting Draw Receipts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > View > Receive Draw`


After you receive funds for a draw, you can post your draw receipt(s) to the General Ledger. 

To post your draw receipt(s): 

1. 
On the Draw information page, go to the Draw schedule tab, and then click the Receive 

draw button in the Draw schedule section. 

This button appears only after you have posted the draw schedule. 

2. 
In the Draw receipts box, fill in the draw source receipt details: 

• 
In the Amount received field, type the amount received from the funding source. 

Select the Receive all check box to receive the full amount. 

• 
In the Date received field, type or select the date on which you received the funds. 

• 
Select a payment method from the drop-down list. See Payment Methods Overview 

for more information. 

• 
In the Document number field, type the number on the draw receipt. 

3. 
When finished, click the Post receipts button. 

The system creates a deposit in A/R and records the details in the G/L. 

If you receive an error message that the cash account for draws is not defined, then this 
means that you have not defined a Cash account on the Configure Job Cost & Reserves 
page (on page 487 ). For multi-entity shared companies, this setting applies to the top 
level; however, you can override it at the entity level.

Viewing and Editing Excluded Items on Draws 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > Edit/View`


You can populate a list of items that have been excluded from a draw when you view an open 

draw. If you want to add an excluded item back to the draw, you can edit the draw to remove 

items from the excluded list. 

Viewing Excluded Items on a Draw 

To view excluded items on a draw: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves 

application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click the Draw workbench menu option. 

The Draw workbench page opens. 

3. 
Click the Job Cost or Replacement Reserve option to view job cost or replacement reserve 

draws. 

4. 
Click the View link next to the draw. 

The Draw information page opens. 

5. 
Click the Excluded items tab. 

6. 
Click the Show excluded items button to populate a list of items that have been marked to 

be excluded from the job or replacement reserve. 

A list of excluded items appears. 

---

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding Excluded Items Back to a Draw 

To add excluded items back to a draw: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves 

application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click the Draw workbench menu option. 

The Draw workbench page opens. 

3. 
Click the Job Cost or Replacement Reserve option to view job cost or replacement reserve 

draws. 

4. 
Click the Edit link next to the draw. 

The Draw information page opens. 

5. 
Click the Excluded items tab. 

6. 
Select the excluded items that you want to add back to the draw. 

7. 
Click the Make selected items available link. 

8. 
Click Save. 

The items that you selected are removed from the list of excluded items and will be 

available to be added to the draw (assuming they still qualify to be included on a draw).

Job Segment Budgets 

This section describes how to manage segment-level (or unit-level) budgets. 

---



#### Job Segment Budgets List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 104*

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Job Segment Budgets List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Job Segment Budgets`


In Job Cost & Reserves, segments are units within a multi-family building. Typically, unit 

renovation jobs track at the segment level.  

Use the Job segment budgets list to manage segment-level budgets and segment budget 

change order requests. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add, edit, view, and delete job segment budgets. 

• 
Import and export job segment budgets. 

• 
Add and view job segment budget change orders. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 105*



##### Adding a Job Segment Budget
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 105*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Before you can add and manage job segment budgets, you must first: 

• 
Set up the affected cost codes to allow segment budgets. For more information, see Adding 

a Cost Code (on page 530). 

• 
Set up the job cost code budgets. For more information, see Importing a Cost Code Budget 

(on page 34). 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage job segment budgets: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Job Cost & Reserves 
Job Segment 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

Job Cost & Reserves 
Segment Definition 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Adding a Job Segment Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
 Job Segment Budgets`


Before you can import or add segment budgets: 

• 
The job type of the job must use a cost structure with at least four levels of definition. For 

more information, see Adding, Duplicating, or Editing a Cost Structure (on page 516). 

• 
The cost code(s) must allow segment-level tracking. For more information, see Adding a 

Cost Code (on page 530). 

• 
You must assign units to the job. For more information, see Editing a Job (on page 22). 

• 
You must add cost code budgets. For more information, see Importing a Cost Code Budget 

(on page 34). 

• 
You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 

status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 

information, see Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354). 

• 
On the import spreadsheet and Job segment budget page, the system provides the cost 

code levels, but not cost code descriptions. As a reference, you can export the cost code list 

for the job type of the job whose budgets you plan to enter. 

---



##### Importing a Job Segment Budget
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 106*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

To add a job segment budget: 

1. 
In the Job segment budgets list, click the Add button. 

The Job segment budget page opens. 

2. 
In the Job name drop-down list, select the job to which the segment budget applies. 

You must select a job whose job type uses segments. 

The Job type field automatically populates with the job type of the selected job.  

3. 
In the Cost code drop-down list, select the cost code to which the segment budget applies. 

You must select a cost code that has segment -level tracking enabled. 

4. 
In the Segment or Unit drop-down list, select the segment or unit to which the segment 

budget applies. 

5. 
In the Amount field, type the budget amount for this cost code and segment (or unit).  

6. 
When your changes are complete: 

• 
Click Save to save the segment budget and close the Job segment budget page.  

• 
Alternatively, click More actions, and then click Save and new to save the segment 

budget and open a new Job segment budget page. 

Importing a Job Segment Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Job Segment Budgets > 
Import Job Segment Budgets`


Before you can import or add segment budgets: 

• 
The job type of the job must use a cost structure with at least four levels of definition. For 

more information, see Adding, Duplicating, or Editing a Cost Structure (on page 516). 

• 
The cost code(s) must allow segment-level tracking. For more information, see Adding a 

Cost Code (on page 530). 

• 
You must assign units to the job. For more information, see Editing a Job (on page 22). 

• 
You must add cost code budgets. For more information, see Importing a Cost Code Budget 

(on page 34). 

• 
You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 

status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 

information, see Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354). 

• 
On the import spreadsheet and Job segment budget page, the system provides the cost 

code levels, but not cost code descriptions. As a reference, you can export the cost code list 

for the job type of the job whose budgets you plan to enter. 

---


<!-- Page 107 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

To import a segment budget: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, select the Budgets link next to the desired job. 

The (Job Name) - Budgets page opens with a list of budget details for each of the job’s cost 

codes. 

2. 
Click the Export budgets template button, and then select the Units budget link.  

The system either downloads the chartexport-(job name)-segment.csv or prompts you to 

open or save the chartexport-(job name)-segment.csv file, depending on your browser’s 

settings. 

The Units budget template allows you to upload budgets for individual job segments or 
units. However, we recommend that you use the Budgets template to import a job budget 
(on page 34 ) first, and then when you add units to the job, the system will automatically 
create a budget per cost code per unit in the Job segment budgets list. 

3. 
Open the chartexport-(job name)-segment.csv file. 

The file automatically provides information for some fields: 

• 
JOB NAME: This is the name of the job. 

• 
COST CODE: This is the code of the cost code.  

The file provides one set of all cost codes available for the job. To import cost codes 

for multiple units at a time, copy this list for each unit you are entering budgets for. 

4. 
For each segment-level budget, enter the required information: 

• 
UNIT: Enter the unit Number. 

• 
BUDGET: Enter the budget amount of that cost code for that specific unit. You can 

enter one budget per cost code for each unit. 

For all cost codes that do not have a budget for the job, enter a budget of “0”. 

The example below shows a segment budget import list. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as.

Click Save.

##### What’s Next?
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 111*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves

Adding a Segment Budget Change Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Job Segment Budgets > 
Change Order > Add`


You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job status 

is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more information, see 

Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354). 

To add a change order: 

1. 
Click Add. 

2. 
In the Effective date field, type or select the date on which the change order takes effect. 

3. 
In the Amount field, type the amount of the change order. 

4. 
In the Comment field, type a comment about the source of the change order. 

5. 
Use the Attachments drop-down list to add an existing attachment, or click the Add link at 

the drop of the drop-down list to upload a new supporting document for the change order. 

6. 
When your changes are complete: 

• 
Click Save to save the change order and close the Job segment change order page.  

• 
Alternatively, click More actions, and then click Save and new to save the change 

order and open a new Job segment change order page. 

What’s Next? 

All segment budget change orders are automatically approved, regardless of the amount or if the 

associated job is subject to approval.

orders that contain a Job Cost specific table in the Available Budget box, See Available 
Budget box for more information.

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing the Purchase orders page. You may have 

additional options based on your permission settings. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Spend Management. 

2. 
Under the All tab, click the Workbench link. 

3. 
Select Purchase order. 

Spend Management Home > Purchase Orders 

From the Spend Management Home page, click Purchase orders. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Purchase Order`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Job Cost & Reserves. 

2. 
Click the All tab. 

3. 
Under Search and find, select Purchase order. 

Adding a New Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order > Add`


Use the Purchase order information page to add a new purchase order. To create a new purchase 

order, complete the following required fields. See Fields (on page 114) for more information 

about the additional fields on this page. 

1. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the date of the purchase 

order. 

2. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Encumbrance date field, and then select the date of the 

encumbrance. 

3. 
Select a vendor from the Vendor drop-down list.  

If the vendor is not available in the drop-down list, see Adding a New Vendor. 

4. 
Optionally, after you select the vendor, click the Saved items link to view an offline 

shopping list of frequently used items saved for that vendor. See Applying a Saved Item to a 

Purchase Order (on page 113) for more information. 

5. 
If you want to bill to the company address, select the Use company address for bill to 

check box. Otherwise, select the property that is being billed for the purchase from the Bill 

to drop-down list. 

---


<!-- Page 119 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

If the purchase order is for a property that is not in the Bill to list, click the Add link at the 

top of the list, and then complete the Contact Information box. 

The Bill to drop-down list is not selectable if you are billing to the company. However, you 
can opt to bill to the company and ship to a property. 

6. 
If this is a blanket purchase order, select the Blanket check box. Otherwise, clear the Blanket 

check box. 

• 
Select either the Blanket PO on item quantities or Blanket PO on dollar value only 

option. 

• 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Expiry date field to select the date the blanket 

purchase order expires. 

7. 
Select the line entry type. If you implement the Job Cost application and this purchase order 

should be entered as a Job Cost, select Job cost. Otherwise, select Standard. The system 

updates the table layout based on your selection. 

8. 
Type a description of the purchase in the Description field. 

9. 
In the Documents section, select an existing attachment from the drop-down list in the 

Attachments field. See Attachments for more information. 

Depending on your RealPage Accounting configuration, you may also have an option to scan 
A/P invoices into the system. See Scanning for more information. 

10. 
Alternatively, from the drop-down list, click Add to create a new attachment. 

11. 
Click the Spend control button to view the monthly and year-to-date available budget for 

the vendor and property on the purchase order. See Available Budget Page for more 

information. 

12. 
Click the Apply template button to apply an allocation template when adding a purchase 

order. The Apply template box opens. 

This causes all line-item entries to inherit the defined allocation. 

13. 
Select the allocation template to use from the Template drop-down list. 

If an allocation template is not listed, click Find to search for the template and apply it. 

14. 
Type an amount in the Amount field. 

15. 
Select the G/L account to use from the G/L account drop-down list.

21.

The default entry is SKU1 for the first line, SKU2 for the second line, and so on. You can 

replace this entry with a valid SKU to help auto-match invoices to purchase orders when

 Action menu button (first column) in the Standard line entry type table to

entry row opens with the Dimensions and Segments fields open. Enter all information. 

• 
If there are no more line-item entries, the <<Previous row button is activated. Click

populates based on the total of the purchase order multiplied by the tax percentage.

table. 

33.

36. 
After completing all fields, complete one of the following actions: 

• 
Click the Draft button. The system saves your progress on the purchase order, 

allowing you to review and submit it at a later date. 

• 
Click the Submit button. The system submits the purchase order for processing. 

• 
Click the Done button. The system cancels any changes made and returns to the

• 
Click the More actions button. The system gives you the Submit, Edit entries layout,

##### Applying a Saved Item to a Purchase Order
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 124*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Applying a Saved Item to a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Search & Find > 
 Purchase Order > Saved 
Items`


When you create a new purchase order, you can select a vendor for the purchase order and then 

open a list of saved items for that vendor. If any items have been stored for that vendor, then you 

can quickly select them from the list and populate them as line entries in the purchase order.  

To select and apply one or more saved items and then apply them to a purchase order: 

1. 
On the Purchase order information page, click the Saved items link under the Vendor 

drop-down list. 

The Saved items box opens with a list of frequently used items saved for that vendor. 

You must select a vendor for the purchase order before you can access the Saved items 
list. 

2. 
In the Saved items table list, select the Select check box next to the desired item(s), and 

then click the Apply button. 

If you do not see the item that you are looking for in the list, you can add a new saved item 
for that vendor. See Adding a Saved Item for instructions. 

The Saved items box closes and the selected items populate as line entries in the purchase 

order. 

---

Editing a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order > Edit`


You can edit only purchase orders that have a status of Draft, Submitted, Partially Approved, or 

Declined. To update a purchase order that has already been approved, see Adding a Change 

Order for a Purchase Order (on page 136). 

To edit a purchase order: 

1. 
From either the Spend management workbench page or the Purchase orders page, click 

the Edit link next to the purchase order you want to edit. The Purchase order information 

page opens. 

To create an exact duplicate instead of editing the current purchase order, click the 

Duplicate button. 

2. 
If you choose to send a manually entered purchase order directly to an online vendor, select 

the Send purchase order to vendor check box. 

3. 
In the Documents section, click one of the following options: 

• 
Click the Choose file button to open a box, locate a file, and then click Open to add it 

to the purchase order. Click the Attach button to upload it to the purchase order. 

• 
Type a name for the attachment in the File name field, and then click Scan to upload it 

to the purchase order. 

4. 
In the eSign Documents section, view the information of any documents listed. 

5. 
Click the Spend control button to view the monthly and year-to-date available budget for 

the vendor and property on the purchase order. 

6. 
Click the Apply template button to apply an allocation when editing a purchase order. The 

Apply Template box opens. 

This causes all line-item entries to inherit the defined allocation. 

• 
Select the allocation template to use from the Template drop-down list. 

If an allocation template is not listed, click Find to search for the template and apply 
it. 

• 
Type an amount in the Amount field. 

• 
Select the G/L account to use from the G/L account drop-down list.
