##### Adding a Change Order for a Purchase Order
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 147*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Adding a Change Order for a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order`


To add a change order for a purchase order: 

1. 
In the Purchase orders list, find the purchase order you want to change, and then click the 

Change order link in the Actions column next to the transaction. The Change purchase 

order page loads. 

2. 
To add a line entry to the table, click the CO link for the item you want to adjust. A new line 

opens with a version number added. 

Alternatively, if you want to delete items from the purchase order after an item has been 
invoiced or paid, you must edit the purchase order. See Editing a Purchase Order (on page 
122 ) for more information. 

3. 
Type a description of the account code/item in the Account code desc. field. This field can 

include the description and a short memo. 

4. 
Type the quantity in the Qty field. 

5. 
Type the adjustment to the price of the line item in the Price field. 

6. 
Optionally, type a brief note regarding the purpose of the change order in the Notes field 

for future reference. 

7. 
Click Save. 

---



##### Receiving Goods for a Purchase Order
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 148*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Receiving Goods for a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order`


If you configured Spend Management to account for the receipt of goods, you can log receipt of 

goods for a purchase order. 

To log the receipt of goods for a purchase order: 

1. 
From the Purchase Orders page, find the purchase order for which you want to log receipt 

of goods, and then click the Receive link next to the transaction. The Receipt of Goods page 

loads for the purchase order. 

2. 
For each line item, type the number of items received in the Qty rec’d field. 

3. 
Click Save. The Purchase Orders page loads with the purchase order displayed as follows: 

• 
If all goods on the purchase order have been received, the purchase order appears 

with a Received status, and the Create invoice option is available. Also, the Received 

amount reflects the Total amount of the purchase order and the Open amount is 

0.00. 

• 
If only some of the goods on the purchase order have been received, the purchase 

order appears with a Partially Received status, and the Create invoice option is 

available. Also, the Received amount reflects the total amount of received goods, and 

the Open amount reflects the Total amount of the purchase order minus the 

Received amount. 

After a purchase order has been partially or fully received, you cannot delete it, even if the 
purchase order has not been matched to any invoices yet. 

After you log received goods for a purchase order, you can create an A/P invoice. To create an 

invoice for the received goods, see Creating an Invoice from a Purchase Order (on page 138). 

---

Creating an A/P Invoice for a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order`


To create an invoice from a purchase order: 

1. 
From the Purchase Orders page, find the purchase order for which you want to create an 

invoice and click the Create invoice link in the Actions column next to the transaction. The 

A/P Invoice page loads. 

The Create invoice feature is available for all purchase orders that have been received or 
partially received. For easier searching, filter purchase orders for these statuses. 

2. 
Complete the required fields for the A/P invoice, including the Date, Total invoice amount, 

and Due date. See A/P Invoice Fields for more information. 

3. 
Click the 
 drop-down list next to the Submit & new button, and then select Submit. The 

system creates the A/P invoice, and the Purchase Orders page loads.

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Closing a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order`


To close a purchase order: 

1. 
From the Workbench page, find the purchase order you want to close. 

When the Receipt of Goods function is enabled in the Spend Management application, you 
can close purchase orders with a status of Partially Received, Received, or Partial Invoice 
Match. 

2. 
Click the Close link next to the transaction. The system opens an alert message box that the 

transaction is about to be closed. 

3. 
Click the OK button to close the purchase order. 

• 
Alternatively, click the Cancel button to not close the purchase order and return to the 

previous page. 

Deleting a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order`


Only users with Delete permissions may delete a purchase order. You cannot delete a purchase 

order that is closed, matched with an invoice, or partially or fully received even if the purchase 

order has not been matched to any invoices yet. All other purchases orders can be deleted, 

including drafts. 

To delete a purchase order: 

1. 
Select the Delete link next to the purchase order you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the OK button. The system deletes the purchase order. 

---

orders. 

On purchase orders with a status of Approved or Partial Invoice Matched, you can close or 

cancel purchase orders in bulk by selecting the check box at the beginning of each row. 

1.

appears.

message appears.

Adding a New Subcontract 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend management > All > Workbench > Subcontract > Add`


Use the Subcontract information page to add a new subcontract. 

You must set up a job in the Job Cost application before you can set up a subcontract for the job. 

To create a new subcontract, complete the following required fields. See Fields (on page 156) for 

more information about the additional fields on this page. 

1. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the start date of the 

subcontract. 

2. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Expiration date field, and then select the end date of 

the subcontract. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

3. 
Use the Contractor drop-down list to select a contractor. 

If the contractor is not available in the drop-down list, see Adding a New Contractor. 

4. 
If you want to bill to the company address, select the Use company address for bill to 

check box. Otherwise, select the property that is being billed for the purchase from the Bill 

to drop-down list. 

If the purchase order is for a property that is not in the list, click the Add link at the top of 

the list and complete the Contact Information box.

To add a change order for a subcontract: 

1.

page loads.

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

External Queue Exceptions List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > External Queue Exceptions`


The External queue exceptions list captures and logs any errors that occur when the system 

processes messages from Procore. Each log entry displays the error message and the date and 

time that the error occurred. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The following permissions are available only if your company is licensed to integrate with Procore. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to access the External queue exceptions list: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Job Cost & Reserves 
External Queue 
List 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Retrying an Exception 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > External Queue Exceptions 
> Retry`


After you troubleshoot and fix an error captured in the External queue exceptions list, you can 

click the Retry link to reattempt processing and syncing to Procore. 

For example, if a new purchase order was created in Procore but the vendor associated with the 

purchase order does not exist in RealPage Financial Suite, then an exception would appear in the 

queue with the error message. You would need to set up a matching vendor record in RealPage 

Financial Suite and then click the Retry link to resume processing.

Use the Job status inquiry page to review and compare budgets and commitments for jobs. From

##### Filtering the Job Status Inquiry
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 177*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Before you view the Job status inquiry page: 

• 
You must set up the job. For more information, see Adding a Job (on page 18). 

• 
You must enter the job’s budgets. For more information, see Job Budgets (on page 344). 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage job status inquiries: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Job Cost 
Job Status Inquiry 
List 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Filtering the Job Status Inquiry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Daily Tasks > Job Status Inquiry`


To filter the job status inquiry: 

1. 
In the Filters section, use the As of date calendar to select the date for which you want to 

calculate balances. 

2. 
In the Select view drop-down list, select how you want to view the job status inquiry:  

• 
Default view: Select this option to use the system default view. 

• 
Create custom view: Select this option to create a custom view. See Managing Custom 

Views in the Job Status Inquiry (on page 169). 

3. 
Click the Select report codes button to define one or more report codes filters for the job 

status inquiry.  

4. 
In the Report code filters box:  

• 
Use the drop-down lists to select the report codes that you want to include in the 

report. 

• 
To include all values of a report code, choose the Select all check box. 

• 
To include multiple values of a report code, select the individual check boxes for the 

values you want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific value, type the report code value name in the Search field. 

---


<!-- Page 178 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
When you are done selecting report codes, click the Apply filters button. 

• 
To reset filter values, click the Clear filters button. 

5. 
You can run the job status inquiry for one or more jobs by selecting jobs individually, 

selecting a job type, or selecting a parent job. 

• 
To filter the inquiry by all child jobs under a parent job, select the parent job from the 

Parent job drop-down list. The multi-select box populates with all child jobs 

associated with that parent job. 

• 
To filter the inquiry by a single job or multiple jobs, select the job(s) from the Job 

drop-down list. To view multiple jobs, click the Select link under Multiple jobs, and 

then select the jobs for which you want to view budget details. See Using the 

Multi-Select Box for instructions. 

• 
To filter the inquiry by all jobs with a specific job type, select the job type from the Job 

type drop-down list. The multi-select box populates with all jobs associated with that 

job type.  

6. 
If you selected only one job with segment-level budgets, then select the Display by unit 

check box to separate the Job status inquiry information by unit, and then use the Unit 

drop-down list to select the units that you want to include. If you do not select this check 

box, this information is summarized for all units associated with the job. 

7. 
In the Cost structure drop-down list, select the cost structure level for which you want to 

view budgets. 

• 
To view specific cost codes within this cost structure, click the Select link, and then 

select the cost codes you want to view budgets for. See Using the Multi-Select Box for 

instructions. 

8. 
In the Level of detail drop-down list, select how many cost structure levels to show in the 

inquiry. Available options include: 

• 
1: The budget collapses to the job level. 

• 
2: The budget collapses to the division level. 

• 
3: The budget collapses to the phase level. 

• 
4: The budget collapses to the subphase level. 

• 
5: The budget collapses to the custom segment 1 level. 

• 
6: The budget collapses to the custom segment 2 level. 

This affects how the budgets show only when the page first loads. You can still manually 

expand and collapse sections as needed. 

9. 
If you selected multiple jobs, you can select the Consolidated check box to consolidate 

budget and cost information for each job into one group labeled “Consolidated jobs”. 

---



##### Managing Custom Views in the Job Status Inquiry
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 179*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

10. 
Select the Hide cost code check box to hide the cost code numbers and display only the 

cost code descriptions. 

11. 
Select the Include job description check box to include the job description in the job status 

inquiry. The job description will appear in parentheses next to the job name. 

12. 
If you have not entered a budget or your budget is less than the Cost to date, then the 

report will display a negative value in the Cost to complete column. However, you can 

select the Prevent negative cost to complete check box to display “0.00” instead of the 

negative value.  

13. 
When your changes are complete: 

• 
To apply your filters to the job status inquiry, click the Apply filters button. If you did 

not select any filters, click the All jobs button to review all jobs in the inquiry. 

• 
To reset all filters to the default settings, click the Clear filters button. 

Managing Custom Views in the Job Status Inquiry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Daily Tasks > Job Status Inquiry`


You can create custom views to define which columns appear in a job status inquiry. These views 

can be modified or deleted at any time. 

Adding a Custom View 

To add a custom view: 

1. 
In the Select view drop-down list, select the “Create custom view” option. 

The Custom view box opens.

Select view drop-down list. 

3. 
Click the Select link under Select columns to open a multi-select box where you can select 

what columns are included in the view. See Using the Multi-Select Box for more information. 

4. 
When your changes are complete, click Save.

Using the Comparison View 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Daily Tasks > Job Status Inquiry > 
Comparison View`


Click the Comparison view button to compare job segments (units) (on page 502) across all or 

multiple cost codes. By default, the comparison view displays units as rows and cost codes as 

columns; however, you can click the Flip view button to display cost codes as rows and units as 

columns instead. 

To use the comparison view: 

1. 
In the Filters section: 

• 
Select a Job with units enabled. 

• 
Select the Display by unit check box. 

• 
Click the Apply filters button. 

---


<!-- Page 181 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

2. 
In the Job status inquiry list, click the Comparison view button. 

The list refreshes to display each unit as a row and each cost code as a column. 

3. 
In the Compare drop-down list, select the parameter by which you want to compare the 

units: 

• 
Cost to date: This is the total amount of costs entered for the cost code. 

• 
Budget: This is the original cost code budget plus approved budget changes (Original 

budget ± Budget changes). 

• 
Cost to complete: This is the amount of estimated costs remaining for the cost code 

(Projected revised budget – Costs). 

• 
Remaining budget: This is the amount of budget remaining for the cost code (Revised 

budget – Approved commitments – Costs). 

---


<!-- Page 182 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

By default, the comparison is based on the Cost to date.  

4. 
In the Level drop-down list, select the cost structure levels you want to include in the 

comparison. You can compare up to the subphase level: Division, Division-Phase, or 

Division-Phase-Subphase. 

5. 
Select the Show dates check box if you want to include the start dates and completion 

dates for each unit renovation. The following columns are added to the report: 

• 
Start date: This column displays the projected and actual start dates for the unit 

renovation. 

• 
Completion date: This column displays the projected and actual completion dates for 

the unit renovation. 

These dates are pulled from the Units tab in the job record. See Tracking Unit Rent Changes 
(on page 30 ) for more information. 

6. 
Select the Show rent check box if you want to include the change in rent for each unit. The 

following columns are added to the report: 

• 
Rent Before: This is the unit’s rent before the renovation. 

• 
Rent After: This is the unit’s rent after the renovation. 

• 
Rent Change: This is the amount by which the rent changed after the renovation. 

7. 
To invert the columns and rows, click the Flip view button. 

The system refreshes the list to display each cost code as a row and each unit as a column. 

8. 
Click the Job status view button to return to the original view.

Job name

Property 
This is the abbreviation and name of the property the job is assigned to. 

Click this link to view the property. 

Project 
If the job is a child job, this is the name of the parent job. 

Job status 
This is the status of the job: 

• 
Pending: The job has not started. In this status, budget changes are 

not tracked. 

• 
Active: The job is in progress. In this status, budget changes are not 

tracked. 

• 
Active (budget locked): The job is in progress. In this status, you 

must use change order requests to update budgets. If the change 

order request is approved, then that change is tracked. 

• 
Closed: The job is complete and closed. In this status, budgets are 

locked. 

• 
Complete (not closed): The job is complete but not closed. In this 

status, budgets are locked. 

• 
Canceled: The job was canceled and is no longer in progress. You 

cannot create a transaction, A/P invoice, journal entry, or purchase 

order for a canceled job. 

• 
Inactive: The job is inactive. You cannot create a transaction, A/P 

invoice, journal entry, or purchase order for an inactivated job.

Job description

This is the tenant assigned to the job. 

Lease

Begin date 
This is the date the job began. 

Completion date – 

actual 

This is the date the job was completed. 

This does not show for open jobs.

Job Status Inquiry Page - Job Status View 

These fields appear when you click the Job status view button. This is the default view. 

Job / Cost code 
This is the name of the job or cost code level and description. 

Each level of cost codes is nested below the previous level. For example, if 

the job’s cost codes use divisions, phases, and subphases, you would have to 

expand the division and phase levels to see the subphase budgets and costs. 

Original budget 
This amount varies depending on the job status: 

• 
If the job status is Pending or Active, then this is the current amount 

of the cost code budget. 

• 
If the job status is Active (budget locked), Complete (not closed), or 

Closed, this is the amount of the cost code budget when the job 

status changed to Active (budget locked). 

Budget changes 
This is the total amount of changes to the cost code budget from approved 

change orders. 

The system only includes change orders whose Effective date is on or 
before the As of date. 

Revised budget 
This is the original cost code budget plus approved budget changes. This 

calculation is: 

Original Budget ± Budget Changes  

Budget changes 

pending 

This is the total amount of change orders awaiting approval for the cost 

code. 

The system only includes change orders whose Effective date is on or 
before the As of date. 

Projected revised 

budget 

This is the original cost code budget plus approved and pending budget 

changes. This calculation is: 

Original budget ± Budget changes ± Budget changes pending 

Commitments 

pending approval 

This is the total amount of commitments awaiting approval for the cost 

code. Click this link to open the Pending commitments page. 

Approved 

commitments 

This is the total amount of approved commitments for the cost code. Click 

this link to open the Approved commitments page. 

---

Open 

commitments 

This is the total amount of open commitments for the cost code. Click this 

link to open the Cost details page. 

If you entered a Prior commitments offset amount when adding a budget 
for a cost code, then the Prior commitments offset amount reduces the 

Open commitments amount for that cost code. 

External 

commitments 

This is the total amount of external commitments for the cost code. Click this 

link to open the External commitments page. 

External commitments are commitments that come from external 
sources, such as OpsTechnology. OpsTechnology can send invoices to 
RealPage Financial Suite with job cost information. You can receive and 
update external commitments through the API or directly add, import, and 
update them through the Job cost external commitments list. 

Cost to date 
This is the total amount of costs entered for the cost code. 

Remaining 

budget 

This is the amount of budget remaining for the cost code. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Approved commitments – Costs 

Cost to complete This is the amount of estimated costs remaining for the cost code. This 

calculation is: 

Projected revised budget – Costs 

Cost to complete 

override 

This is the cost to complete entered by a user, which overrides the 

system-generated value shown in Cost to complete. 

This column only appears when you click the Show override button. 

Override reason 
This is the reason for the override. 

This column only appears when you click the Show override button. 

Cost at 

completion 

This amount varies depending on the job status: 

• 
If the job is closed, this is the total amount of costs entered for 

applicable cost codes in the division when the job was closed. 

• 
If the job is still open, this is the Cost to date amount. 

Variance to 

revised budget 

This is the difference between the revised budget amount and the final cost 

for the cost code. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Cost at completion 

Variance to 

original budget 

This is the difference between the original budget amount and the final cost 

for the cost code. This calculation is: 

Original budget – Cost at completion

Reclassifying a Budget

Budget`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Status > Original 
Budget`


To reclassify a budget: 

1. 
On the Budget details page, use the Reclass to drop-down list to select the cost code you 

want to reclassify the budget to.  

2. 
In the Amount to reclass field, enter the amount you want to reclassify.  

If this is not the full amount of the budget, the remaining amount stays budgeted to the 

current cost code. 

3. 
In the Reclass description field, type any additional details to record with the reclass. 

4. 
When your changes are complete, click Reclass.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 202*

Matching Job Cost Invoices to Purchase Orders 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Daily Tasks > Job Status Inquiry > Cost to 
Date`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Status > Cost to 
Date`


Use the Match order button on the Cost to date page to match A/P invoices with purchase 

orders, subcontracts, and service contract orders. Clicking this button opens a box with all of the 

open transactions associated with the vendor and job cost code on the A/P invoice. When you 

match line items, information on the purchase order overrides the information on the A/P line 

item. 

To match line items: 

1. 
Click the Show order number column button in the upper-right corner of the Cost to date 

page. 

The Order number column appears. 

2. 
Click the Match order button in the Order number column. 

A box opens with a list of open transactions associated with the same vendor and cost code 

on the A/P invoice. 

3. 
Select the check box next to each line item you want to match to the A/P invoice. 

4. 
Type the Amount to apply for each line item, and then press the TAB key. The Remaining 

to apply field is updated to reflect the total amount on the invoice remaining to be 

matched. 

5. 
Click the Match selected item(s) button to match the line item(s). 

The order number you matched the invoice to appears in the Order number column.

Funding Source Inquiry Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Daily Tasks > Funding Source Inquiry`


The Funding source inquiry page lets you compare budgeted totals to total drawn amounts by 

funding source across multiple properties and jobs.  

By default, the system displays the funding sources for each job across the property. Funding 

Source Inquiry columns include: 

• 
Job name: Lists the jobs across the property 

• 
Funding source: Lists the funding sources for each job 

• 
Budget: Lists the budget entered for the funding source 

• 
Budget changes: Lists the budget changes entered against the funding source 

• 
Revised budget: Lists the calculated sum of the budget and budget changes 

• 
Total drawn: Lists the total draw amount against that funding source in a job 

• 
Budget remaining: Lists the difference between the revised budget and total draw amount

Create an A/P Invoice 

This section shows you how to add job cost A/P invoices. The Create an A/P invoice link in the 

Job Cost & Reserves application menu takes you to the same A/P Invoice page as the one in the 

Accounts Payable application. From this page, you can add standard invoice line items, job cost 

line items, or both. 

See the A/P Invoices section in Accounts Payable for a comprehensive set of topics related to 
A/P invoices.

#### A/P Invoice Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 215*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

A/P Invoice Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > All > Search & Find > A/P Invoices`


Use the A/P invoice page to add a new A/P invoice and view and edit an existing A/P invoice. 

After creating the invoice, you can: 

• 
Duplicate the invoice. Click the Duplicate button. 

• 
Print the invoice. Click the Print button. 

• 
Pay the invoice. Click the Pay button. 

• 
Reclassify the invoice. Click the Reclassify button.  

If the button does not appear at the top left, then you cannot reclassify this transaction. 

• 
Post the invoice to the General ledger. Click the Post button. 

• 
Create a recurring transaction based on the invoice. Click the More actions button and then 

select Create recurring transaction. 

• 
View the invoice’s audit trail. Click the More actions button and then select View audit trail. 

• 
View a breakdown of the total balance due to the vendor. Click the Vendor ID balance link 

at the top of the page. 

• 
Associate documents with this invoice and view the attached documents. 

• 
In the OPS section, you can view the approval workflow of an invoice when your system is 

integrated with OPSTechnology. 

• 
In the OPS Attachments section, you can click the URL to view the eInvoice and any 

attachments associated with the eInvoice. This section appears when the invoice type is 

eInvoice or oInvoice. 

In the Invoice Entries section, you can: 

• 
View the available budget for the property. Click the Spend control button. 

• 
Add default values for the invoice entries list. Click the Show defaults link. 

• 
Apply A/P allocations to the invoice. Click the Apply A/P allocation button.  

• 
Save the A/P allocations. Click the Save A/P allocation button. 

• 
Define an allocation split. Click Show details. 

• 
Customize the allocation. Click Show details and then click the Customize allocation 

button. 

• 
Select one or more segment type and segment values to associate with the A/P invoice. 

• 
Use fields shared by Spend Management to help you match the A/P invoice to a purchase 

order. The shared fields include Account code description, Qty, UOM, Price, and Extended 

price.  

---


<!-- Page 216 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The A/P Invoice page can have up to eight sections: 

• 
At the top is the vendor name, vendor ID in parentheses, and the vendor’s balance, the total 

amount that you owe to the vendor. This section appears only after you have saved the 

invoice. 

• 
The banner section shows basic information about the A/P invoice so that you can find it 

quickly. This section appears only after you have saved the invoice. 

• 
The Date section (so-called because the first field in the section is the Date field) contains 

most of the important information about the A/P invoice.  

• 
The Term section contains further details about the invoice. 

• 
The next section can contain custom fields requested by your company. Consult your 

System Administrator for details. 

• 
The Documents section contains documents related to this A/P invoice. Use this section to 

attach documents, scan documents and to view the attached documents. 

• 
The Currency section appears if your system is multi-currency enabled.  

• 
The Invoice entries section contains the line items that are covered by this A/P invoice.  

The A/P Invoice record can have up to three tabs: 

• 
A/P invoice: This tab contains the essential components of the invoice,  

• 
Messaging: This tab allows you to send a message about this invoice to another system 

user, to an external email address, or to the vendor associated with the A/P invoice. 

• 
Header: This tab contains any custom fields that the property management company wants 

to track.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Before you can add a job cost A/P invoice: 

• 
You must set up the job. For more information, see Adding a Job (on page 18). 

• 
You must assign at least one funding source to the job. For more information, see Editing a 

Job (on page 22). Additionally, you must assign the job type’s cost codes to the draw model 

details of the funding source’s draw model. 

• 
You must set up the job budgets. For more information, see Importing a Cost Code Budget 

(on page 34). 

• 
If the job is using segment-level tracking, you must assign the affected units to the job and 

set up the job segment budgets. 

• 
You must set up the vendor you will use for the invoice. 

• 
To work with attachments, you must be a Business, Employee, or Approval user type with 

permissions to Attachments and Attachment folders in the Company application. 

• 
To view attachments, you must have the List and View permissions to both Attachments 

and Attachment folders.

Adding an A/P Invoice Manually 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 
 A/P Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > Add`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open 
Invoices and Adjustments > Accounts Payable Invoices > Create`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Search & Find > 
 AP Invoice`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost > Daily Tasks > Create an AP Invoice`


This topic describes how to create an A/P invoice as if every possible feature is enabled. Your 

experience of this page will differ depending on the features that your system has enabled. 

Variations occur due to system configuration, your permissions, and your company’s installation 

of other RealPage Financial Suite applications. 

Applications that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
Spend Management 

• 
Job Cost  

Configuration Differences that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
When your system is configured to use multiple currencies, additional currency fields appear 

in this record. See the multi-currency systems section on the General Ledger configuration 

page. 

• 
When the Intercompany billing option is enabled (Accounts Receivable configuration), the 

A/R Invoice Dimensions section appears. 

• 
When your system is integrated with OpsTechnology, it allows RealPage Accounting to 

receive eInvoices. 

• 
Accounts Payable configuration:  

• 
When the Enable bank account selection in A/P invoice option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Bank account field to appear on the A/P invoice 

record. 

• 
When the Enable invoice entry control validation option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Total invoice amount field to appear on the A/P 

invoice record. 

• 
When Spend management is enabled, then the Match Order button appears, allowing you 

to match a purchase order to the A/P invoice. Additional fields appear on the record such as 

QTY, Price, Extended Price, UOM, and Account code description. 

---


<!-- Page 220 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
When Job Cost is enabled, the Line Entry Type section appears. When you select Include Job 

cost, the system adds Job cost-specific columns in the Invoice Entries list such as Job name, 

Cost code, and Job unit.  

• 
When scanning is enabled, the Attachments field is replaced with the Documents section, 

affecting the way that you attach documents.  

• 
If the Please complete one-time setup scanner prompt appears, follow the 

instructions in Downloading the Scanning Software. If you do not plan to scan 

supporting documents at this time, you can skip the download by clicking the X in 

upper-right corner of the box.  

• 
If you enabled the Single scan upload feature in your preferences and have previously 

downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the 

software when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, 

purchase order, or service contract, or scan a document into the document dashboard. 

When this occurs, download the new software. There is no need to uninstall the 

previous version. 

• 
Clicking the Scan button in the Documents section redisplays the scanner prompt. 

Related Permissions 

• 
Permissions for attachments 

• 
Permissions for adding assets 

To create an A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the Date field, type the date of the invoice, or leave it set to today’s date.

needed; for example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different 

date.

In the G/L posting date field, type the date that you want the A/P invoice to post on the 

general ledger.  

3. 
In the Total invoice amount field, type the amount of the invoice.  

This field appears only when the Enable invoice entry control validation check box is 

selected on the configuration page of Accounts Payable. When enabled, this is a required 

field.

Saving the A/P Invoice 

When entering the transaction information, save it as a draft or post it. The system validates 

transactions only when they are posted. For example, required departments or locations are not 

validated until posting. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction without affecting the 

subledger or G/L. Later, you or another user can review and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the transaction. 

System Checks for Budget Exceeded  

If you try to post an A/P invoice that exceeds the default budget, and your company uses the A/P 

invoice approval process with the budget exceeded feature, the system displays a warning. The 

system may also prevent you from posting the A/P invoice. If you want to be able to bypass this 

budget check, ask your system administrator to grant you the desired bypass permission. Bypass 

permissions are available for A/P invoices and purchase orders. 

When the budget exceeded feature is enabled, the system checks the A/P invoice amount against 

the budgeted number for the G/L account. When the amount exceeds the budget, then the 

system either displays a warning or prevents you from saving the A/P invoice, depending on how 

your company configured the feature. When preventing an A/P invoice from being posted, the 

system also displays a warning to let you know why you cannot post. 

To enable or disable the budget exceeded feature, see Setting a system action when an A/P 

invoice or purchase order exceeds the budget.

System Checks for Attachments 

Your company may require that you attach a document to support the A/P invoice before you can 

save it as a draft, post, or submit it. If you need to save an A/P invoice without an attachment, 

contact your system administrator and ask them to remove the Require attachment permission 

from your role or account. 

What’s Next? 

When your company uses approvals, A/P invoices first go through the payment approval 

workflow. After payments are approved, you can make the payments.  

Go to the Pay A/P invoices page to select the invoice for payment. When you select Add to 

outbox or Pay now: 

• 
The invoice becomes a payment request. 

• 
The system notifies approvers that a payment is waiting for their approval. 

• 
You can view the status of the payment request in the Payment request list. 

• 
When an approver approves the invoice, the system pays the invoice. 

• 
If the payment method is Check, the system allows the payment to be included in a check 

run.

A/P Invoices List

view of the list, you can add a custom view using the Manage views > Create new view.

Columns 

Select (check box) 
Use these check boxes to select invoices that you want to include in an 

invoice package. When you select a check box, the package invoice 

mode begins.  

Edit (link) 
Opens the A/P invoice so that you can change it. 

The Edit option is not available when you do not have access to all 
locations in the invoice. This means that your company has multiple 
entities, and you are not allowed to view activities between entities to 
which you do not have access.  

View (link) 
Opens the A/P invoice so that you can review the details. 

Vendor name 
This column contains the name of the vendor who is the source of the 

A/P invoice. 

Invoice number 
This column contains the record number assigned to the A/P invoice by 

the vendor. This number prints on the check remittance stub, but not on 

the check itself. 

Date 
This column contains the transaction date. 

Hold 
This column contains a check mark when someone has placed the A/P 

invoice on hold. 

Amount 

Base Amount 

Transaction amount 

This column contains the actual amount of the transaction for this item 

in a single-currency company. 

If you’ve enabled multi-currency, the system displays Base Amount and 

Transaction Amount in place of Amount. 

Base Amount is the amount of the item in the base currency of your 

company. 

Transaction amount is the amount of the item in the currency you set 

for the A/P invoice. 

For example, if your base currency is USD and you create a 100 Euro A/P 

invoice, for the A/P invoice Line Item, you see the A/P invoice with 100 

Euro as the Transaction amount and 110 USD as the Base Amount 

(assuming a 1.1 exchange rate from Euro to USD). 

---


<!-- Page 238 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Transaction type 
This column contains the type of invoice: 

• 
A/P invoice: Regular A/P invoices 

• 
eInvoice: A system-generated A/P invoice created by Spend 

Management Storefront. 

• 
oInvoice: A system-generated A/P invoice created by Full 

Service.  

Base currency 
This column indicates what the base currency is for this entity. 

This field appears only when your company is a multi-currency company. 

State 
This column contains the current part of the processing cycle for the A/P 

invoice. How much you can edit an A/P invoice, or delete or reverse it, 

depends on its state. 

• 
Draft: The A/P invoice is created, but not posted. It can be 

changed without consequence. 

• 
Posted: The A/P invoice was posted to the G/L. 

• 
Selected: The A/P invoice is now selected for payment. 

• 
Paid: Vendor payment was made. 

• 
Partially Paid: Only a partial payment was made. There is a 

remaining amount to be paid. 

• 
Reversed: The A/P invoice was reversed by a second transaction, 

which essentially zeroed out the balance in the GL. Your 

company retains a record of the reversed A/P invoice and the 

reversal transaction for audit trail purposes. 

• 
Reversal: This transaction is created when you reverse a 

transaction and causes the balance to zero out. 

• 
No value: This transaction is posted but has not affected the 

General ledger.  

Summary title 
This column contains the name of the summary that include this A/P 

invoice. A summary is a collection of same type transactions, grouped 

together for same-time processing.  

Payment method 
This column contains the payment method used to pay this A/P invoice.  

Payment number 
This column contains the payment number. When there are multiple 

payments, open the A/P invoice and click the Multiple payments link to 

see the list of payments. 

Location name 
This is the location associated with the invoice.

Print (link) 
Click this link to have the system generate the A/P invoice in a printable 

format. 

Entity 
This is the entity associated with the invoice when the invoice is created 

at the entity level. When an invoice is created at the top level, the Entity 

column is blank. 

Delete / Reverse 
This column contains a link that allows you to delete or reverse an 

unpaid A/P invoice. Your system setting of Enable reversal of unpaid 

A/P invoices in Accounts payable configuration determines whether the 

link displays Delete or Reverse.  

Fields 

The presence and order of fields can differ based on how you open a record (Add, Edit, or View) 

and by the kind of invoice it is, A/P invoice, eInvoice, or oInvoice. The first two sections do not 

appear when you are adding an A/P invoice. If you are adding an invoice, skip to the First Section 

Under the Banner section. 

In systems with multi-currency enabled, the Currency section appears. Currency is indicated by 

three-character currency codes, such as USD (US dollars), GBP (British Pound Sterling), and CAD 

(Canadian dollars).  

When you have the scanner enabled, then the Documents section appears on the A/P invoice 

page instead of Attachments fields.  

When adding an A/P invoice in a system that is integrated with OPSTechnology, the OPS section 

appears after the Term section. When you edit and view an invoice, the fields in the OPS section 

move to the Header tab. RealPage consultants create the custom fields that appear in the OPS 

section, and fill them in. These custom OPS fields vary from company to company. Consult your 

system administrator if you have questions about these fields.  

This is a list of fields on the A/P invoice and AI-Invoice Scanning pages: 

(Above the Banner Section) 

Vendor 
This is the vendor associated with the A/P invoice. 

Vendor ID balance 

(link) 

This is the amount that your company owes to the vendor. Click the link 

to open the Vendor totals box to see the total amount due from each 

entity.  

If you are working in a multi-entity company that uses multiple base 
currencies, then you do not see a linked amount. Instead of an amount
a View due link appears.

(Banner Section) 

Invoice date 
This is the transaction’s date. When entering a new A/P invoice, the 

date defaults to the current date. 

Due date 
This is the date that the payment is due. The system calculates the due 

date based on the A/P invoice date and terms. 

Due in/Overdue 
Due in: When an invoice hasn’t reached the due date, then this field 

contains the number of days until the payment is due. 

Overdue: When an invoice passes the due date, then this field contains 

the number of days that the payment is past due. 

Invoice total 
This is the amount that is due on the due date. 

Amount paid 
This is the amount that your company is paying through this A/P 

invoice. 

Amount due 
This is the amount due after this payment is made. 

DRAFT 
The Draft symbol appears when the A/P invoice was created and saved 

as a draft instead of posting it. 

% 
This is the confidence barometer. The system determines how 

confident that you can be that the A/P invoice is valid and should be 

paid. Colors help to show the confidence level. Green indicates that 

confidence is high. 

You can configure the system to approve A/P invoices based on 

confidence level automatically. 

(First Section Under the Banner) 

Date 
Type the date or click the 
 Calendar button to select the date of the 

invoice. 

When entering a new A/P invoice, the date defaults to the current date. 

You can choose to enter a different date such as the date on the A/P 

invoice. This field is required. 

G/L posting date 

Type the date or click the 
 Calendar button to select the date to post 

the A/P invoice to the General Ledger. 

The G/L posting date appears on this page only if enabled in the 

Configure Accounts Payable page. This is the date on which the 

transaction actually posts to the general ledger. Unless you change it, 

this date defaults to the transaction date.

Total invoice amount Type the total amount, the sum of all line items, in this field. This field is 

required. 

This field is controlled by the Enable invoice entry control validation 

check box. When selected, the system validates that the total invoice 

amount equals the total amount defined in the line items and the Total 

invoice amount field appears on the A/P invoice page.  

Vendor (Supplier) 
Select the vendor (supplier) that is the source of the A/P invoice. You can 

either select a vendor from the drop-down list or type the name of the 

vendor for the A/P invoice. For vendors that you use often, it’s best to 

create vendor records for them in the system. This field is required. 

You can use the field controls to add a new vendor, view a vendor’s 

record, or find a vendor’s record.  

To add or import vendors, you must be at the top level. 

Pay to 
Select the vendor contact to whom you want to send the payment.  

The system automatically completes this field from the Pay to contact 

field in the Vendor record. If the Pay to contact is empty, then the 

system uses the contact associated with the vendor record. You can 

override the contact by selecting a different one on this page. As an 

example, a vendor that has multiple offices may request that you send 

the check to an office other than the one on record. 

Return to 
Select the vendor contact to whom you want to send a return of the 

purchase. By default, this is the Return to contact on the Vendor record.  

If it is not filled in, then the system uses the contact associated with the 

vendor that you selected on this page. In most cases, you won’t need to 

override the default, but you can override it as needed. As an example, 

when returning a defective product, the vendor may request that you 

return it to a location other than the one on record.

State 
The state of the invoice: 

• 
Submitted: The invoice is saved and submitted to the approval 

workflow. 

• 
Declined: Approvers declined the invoice. 

• 
Selected: The invoice is selected for payment but not yet paid. 

• 
Draft: The invoice is saved but not yet posted or submitted for 

approval. 

• 
Posted: The invoice is posted to the General Ledger. 

• 
Partially paid: Only part of the invoice is paid. 

• 
Partially approved: A transaction can have more than one 

approver. The invoice is approved by at least one approver in 

the workflow, but more approvals are required. 

• 
Paid: The invoice is paid in full. 

• 
Reversed: The invoice has been reversed. 

• 
Reversal: The listed transaction is the reversal created from the 

reversed invoice. 

This field appears only after you save the invoice. 

Invoice number 
Type a unique number to assign to the invoice. 

To set an alarm for duplicate numbers, or to disallow duplicate numbers 

for this vendor, see Configure Accounts Payable. This number prints on 

the check remittance stub, but not on the check itself. 

This field is required. 

Reference number 
This is the record number assigned to the A/P invoice by the vendor.  

It can also be a number such as a purchase order or account number 

that may be useful in searches or reports on this A/P invoice. This 

number shows in searches and on the G/L Details report, but it does not 

print on the check or check remittance stub. 

When Invoice Processing enters an account number on an A/P invoice 

record, the account number appears in the oInvoice’s Reference number 

field. 

Description  
Enter information that you want stored with this A/P invoice. This 

information prints on the Vendor Ledger report but does not print on the 

check or remittance stub. 

Contact tax group 
Select the contact tax group to associate with this A/P invoice.  

This field appears on the A/P invoice page when VAT is enabled.

Allocation 
Select the allocation template from the drop-down list. 

Allocations in the line item section enable you to override the allocation 

for individual items from what you set in the header of the A/P invoice. 

• 
You can select an allocation template that defines how you want 

the item allocated. The template specifies how to automatically 

distribute the amounts.  

• 
You can also set up a custom allocation by clicking Customize 

Allocation in the Details section. The system displays the 

Allocation Splits box.  

If you change the amounts so that the total is different from what 

you entered in the transaction section, the system updates the 

total when you save the change and return to the transaction 

section of the invoice. It also changes the name of the allocation 

to Custom. 

If your company includes multiple entities and transacts in multiple 

currencies, and if you create allocations at the entity level, then you can 

only use those allocations at the entity level. You cannot access 

entity-level transaction allocations at the top level. 

The Allocation Splits box only displays if you have configured your 

Accounts Payable to enable the ability to create transaction allocations 

when entering A/P invoices in A/P invoice entry. To do this, from the

Create a PO Commitment 

This section shows you how to add job cost purchase order (PO) commitments. The Create a PO 

commitment link in the Job Cost & Reserves application menu takes you to the same Purchase 

order information page as the one in the Spend Management application. From this page, you 

can add standard line items, job cost line items, or both. 

See the Purchase Orders section in Spend Management for a comprehensive set of topics 
related to purchase orders.

Purchase Order Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Daily Tasks > Create a PO Commitment`


Use the Purchase order information page to add, edit, duplicate, print, and email purchase 

orders. 

On purchase orders with a status of Approved or Partial Invoice Matched, you can close or 

cancel purchase orders in bulk by selecting the check box at the beginning of each row. 

1. 
Select the check box for each purchase order to close or cancel. The Close/Cancel button 

appears. 

2. 
When all purchase orders are selected, click the Close/Cancel button. A confirmation 

message appears. 

3. 
Click the OK button to confirm the action.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

##### Adding a New Purchase Order
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 265*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Adding a New Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order > Add`


Use the Purchase order information page to add a new purchase order. To create a new purchase 

order, complete the following required fields. See Fields (on page 114) for more information 

about the additional fields on this page. 

1. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the date of the purchase 

order. 

2. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Encumbrance date field, and then select the date of the 

encumbrance. 

3. 
Select a vendor from the Vendor drop-down list.  

If the vendor is not available in the drop-down list, see Adding a New Vendor. 

4. 
Optionally, after you select the vendor, click the Saved items link to view an offline 

shopping list of frequently used items saved for that vendor. See Applying a Saved Item to a 

Purchase Order (on page 113) for more information. 

5. 
If you want to bill to the company address, select the Use company address for bill to 

check box. Otherwise, select the property that is being billed for the purchase from the Bill 

to drop-down list. 

If the purchase order is for a property that is not in the Bill to list, click the Add link at the 

top of the list, and then complete the Contact Information box. 

The Bill to drop-down list is not selectable if you are billing to the company. However, you 
can opt to bill to the company and ship to a property. 

6. 
If this is a blanket purchase order, select the Blanket check box. Otherwise, clear the Blanket 

check box. 

• 
Select either the Blanket PO on item quantities or Blanket PO on dollar value only 

option. 

• 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Expiry date field to select the date the blanket 

purchase order expires. 

7. 
Select the line entry type. If you implement the Job Cost application and this purchase order 

should be entered as a Job Cost, select Job cost. Otherwise, select Standard. The system 

updates the table layout based on your selection. 

8. 
Type a description of the purchase in the Description field. 

9. 
In the Documents section, select an existing attachment from the drop-down list in the 

Attachments field. See Attachments for more information. 

---


<!-- Page 266 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Depending on your RealPage Accounting configuration, you may also have an option to scan 
A/P invoices into the system. See Scanning for more information. 

10. 
Alternatively, from the drop-down list, click Add to create a new attachment. 

11. 
Click the Spend control button to view the monthly and year-to-date available budget for 

the vendor and property on the purchase order. See Available Budget Page for more 

information. 

12. 
Click the Apply template button to apply an allocation template when adding a purchase 

order. The Apply template box opens. 

This causes all line-item entries to inherit the defined allocation. 

13. 
Select the allocation template to use from the Template drop-down list. 

If an allocation template is not listed, click Find to search for the template and apply it. 

14. 
Type an amount in the Amount field. 

15. 
Select the G/L account to use from the G/L account drop-down list. 

16. 
Click the Apply button. 

17. 
Click the Save template button to add a new allocation template when adding a purchase 

order. The Save template box opens. 

18. 
Type a name for the new allocation template in the Name field. 

19. 
Optionally, type a description of the allocation template in the Description (optional) field. 

20. 
Select the type of allocation template to use from the TemplateType drop-down list. 

21. 
Optionally, type any additional information you want to include in the Memo (optional) 

field. 

---


<!-- Page 267 -->

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

22. 
Click the Save button. 

23. 
Complete the line entry table: 

• 
For standard line entries, refer to Standard Line Entry Table section in Fields (on page 

114) for more information. 

• 
For job cost line entries, refer to Job Cost Line Entry Table section in Fields (on page 

114) for more information. 

24. 
Click the Show defaults link to expand the following additional fields: 

• 
Classification 

• 
Project 

• 
Owner 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Unit 

• 
Account 

25. 
Click the Apply defaults button to use the defined defaults on a purchase order to reduce 

the amount of time spent keying in large orders. 

Click the Hide defaults link to close these additional fields. 

26. 
In the SKU column, verify the information. 

---


<!-- Page 268 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The default entry is SKU1 for the first line, SKU2 for the second line, and so on. You can 

replace this entry with a valid SKU to help auto-match invoices to purchase orders when 

processing invoices, but you cannot leave it blank. 

27. 
Click the 
 Action menu button (first column) in the Standard line entry type table to 

show the Dimensions and Segments fields for the line item. Refer to Standard Line Entry 

Table section in Fields (on page 114) for more information. 

For purchase orders, the quantity can be listed in whole or partial (decimal) number values. 

28. 
If there is more than one line-item entry, click the Next row >> button. The next line-item 

entry row opens with the Dimensions and Segments fields open. Enter all information. 

• 
If there are no more line-item entries, the <<Previous row button is activated. Click 

this button to return to the previous line-item entry. 

• 
If there are more line-item entries, the Next row >> button is activated. Click this 

button to move to the next line-item entry. 

29. 
After the information is entered, click the Hide details link on the tab to minimize the table 

entries. 

• 
To maximize the table, click the Show details link on the tab. 

30. 
Enter a number in the Tax percentage field. 

---


<!-- Page 269 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

If the tax percentage is calculated automatically, the amount in the Tax amount field 
populates based on the total of the purchase order multiplied by the tax percentage. 

31. 
Complete the Shipping amount and Discount amount fields if applicable. 

32. 
Click the Distribute button. This applies the amounts in these fields to each line item in the 

table. 

33. 
Type any notes for the purchase order in the Notes field if needed. 

34. 
If your Spend Management configuration requires you to add an attachment, use the 

Attachments drop-down list to add an attachment. See Attachments for more information. 

35. 
In the Alternate Bids section, enter the following information for tracking purposes: 

• 
Vendor Name 

• 
Amount 

• 
Attachment 

The Alternate Bid details and attachments can be included in a purchase order 
package. 

36. 
After completing all fields, complete one of the following actions: 

• 
Click the Draft button. The system saves your progress on the purchase order, 

allowing you to review and submit it at a later date. 

• 
Click the Submit button. The system submits the purchase order for processing. 

• 
Click the Done button. The system cancels any changes made and returns to the 

previous page. 

• 
Click the More actions button. The system gives you the Submit, Edit entries layout, 

Edit job cost layout, or Table size options. Select an option to complete adding a 

purchase order. 

During the application configuration, if the Enable preventing or warning a user when 

adding an A/P invoice that exceeds the budget check box is selected, either the user is 
prevented or restricted from creating an A/P invoice or a warning message appears that 
the budget has been exceeded. See Configuring Transaction Approvals for more 
information.

##### Adding a New Subcontract
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 281*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Adding a New Subcontract 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend management > All > Workbench > Subcontract > Add`


Use the Subcontract information page to add a new subcontract. 

You must set up a job in the Job Cost application before you can set up a subcontract for the job. 

To create a new subcontract, complete the following required fields. See Fields (on page 156) for 

more information about the additional fields on this page. 

1. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the start date of the 

subcontract. 

2. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Expiration date field, and then select the end date of 

the subcontract. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

3. 
Use the Contractor drop-down list to select a contractor. 

If the contractor is not available in the drop-down list, see Adding a New Contractor. 

4. 
If you want to bill to the company address, select the Use company address for bill to 

check box. Otherwise, select the property that is being billed for the purchase from the Bill 

to drop-down list. 

If the purchase order is for a property that is not in the list, click the Add link at the top of 

the list and complete the Contact Information box. 

5. 
Type a description of the contracted service in the Description field. 

6. 
If your Spend Management configuration requires you to add an attachment, use the 

Attachments drop-down list to add an attachment.  

7. 
Complete the line entry table. See Line Entry Table in Fields (on page 156) for more 

information. 

8. 
Optionally, preview the approval workflow. 

• 
Click the More actions button, and then select Preview workflow. The Preview 

approval workflows box opens. 

• 
Review the approval workflow, and then click the X to close the box. 

9. 
Click the Submit button. The system submits the subcontract for processing. 

---

Create Journal Entry 

This section shows you how to add job cost journal entries. The Create journal entry link in the 

Job Cost & Reserves application menu takes you to the same Journal entries page as the one in 

the General Ledger application. From this page, you can add standard line items, job cost line 

items, or both. 

See the Journal Entries section in General Ledger for a comprehensive set of topics related to 
journal entries. 

---



#### Journal Entries Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 287*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Journal Entries Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > 
 Journal Entry`


Use the Journal entries page to add an entry in a journal or make changes to a journal entry.  

When you add a journal entry, you can either post it right away or save it as a draft. When you’re 

adding a new journal entry, the record has only one page. After you complete the journal entry by 

posting or saving it as a draft, the additional tabs appear.  

If your company uses the approval workflow for journal entries, then you submit the journal entry 
for approval rather than posting it. 

The Journal entries page is composed of three tabs: 

• 
Transactions: Use this tab to create and manage the journal entry. 

• 
History: This tab displays information about the entry. Like an audit entry, this tab tracks the 

entry’s creation, who created it, and when. It also displays the current state of the 

transaction. 

• 
Messaging: Use this tab to create and review messages about this journal entry. 

The Transactions tab contains the following sections: 

• 
The Transaction section 

• 
The Documents section 

• 
The Entries and/or Job cost entries section 

Transaction Section 

In this section, you select the journal to which you are adding the journal entry and add 

descriptive information about the journal entry. You will also: 

• 
Select the source entity. 

• 
Specify whether the line entries will be standard line entries or Job Cost entries. 

• 
Select the approval workflow, if any. 

Documents Section 

Use the Documents section to attach a file to the journal entry. You can either attach a file that 

resides on your computer or scan a document in and attach it, right from the journal entry page. 

You can also view an attached document from the journal entry page by clicking the 

Attachment button. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 288*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Entries Section 

If you are creating a standard journal entry, use the Entries section to classify the journal entry by 

selecting an account, and then assigning the expense or revenue to a specific department, 

location, and unit.  

The Entries list lets you define defaults before you begin to have the system fill in the columns 

that may all have the same value. 

Job Cost Entries Section 

If you are creating a Job Cost journal entry, use the Job cost entries section to record the line items 

of that journal entry, including the job location, job name, cost code, and job unit.  

Line Item Details 

Fill in the details of a line entry by clicking the Show details tab. This tab appears when you click a 

column in a row. The Details section lets you define: 

• 
Journal entry type 

• 
Dimensions 

• 
Segment types and their values. 

You can also customize allocation splits between dimensions in the Entries section’s Details 

section. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Before you can add a Job Cost journal entry: 

• 
You must set up the job. For more information, see Adding a Job (on page 18). 

• 
To work with attachments, you must be a Business, Employee, or Approval user type with 

permissions to Attachments and Attachment folders in the Company application. 

• 
To view attachments, you must have the List and View permissions to both Attachments 

and Attachment folders.

Adding a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find 
 Journal Entry`


When you add a transaction to a journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft or posting it 

right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be complete—you or another 

user can review them later, make changes, and then post them. When you post a journal 

transaction, the entire transaction must balance, and all required information must be entered. 

You can substantiate a transaction by associating it with a supporting attachment. You can also 

use the transaction allocations to automatically distribute amounts across departments and 

locations. 

---


<!-- Page 290 -->
Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

You can add a journal entry directly or add it from the General Ledger workbench. This topic 

describes how to add a journal entry directly. 

This topic describes how to add a standard journal entry. If you want to create a statistical journal 

entry, see Creating statistical journal entries. 

To add a new journal entry: 

Enter general information about the transaction. The top part of the page is where you enter the 

transaction date, description, and other basic information. 

1. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want to add the new journal 

entry. 

Specifying the journal is necessary only when you selected 
 Journal entry rather than 
the Add button from inside of a journal. 

2. 
In the Posting date field, accept the current date or enter a different one. This is the posting 

date for the entry. 

When your system sends journal entries through the approval process, and you make a 

journal entry in a closed period, RealPage Accounting offers a feature to have the system 

advance the posting date of the journal entry to the next open period.  

3. 
In the Automatic reversal date field, if you want to reverse this transaction on a specific 

date, type a date or select a date from the 
 Calendar. 

An automatic reversal date is the same thing as a reverse transaction except that inverts the 

line items and zeros out the transaction. You can enter today’s date or later. 

To reverse a transaction that you have previously posted, select the check box next to the 
journal transaction that you want to reverse, and then click the Reverse button. 

4. 
Type a description of the journal entry in the Description field. When you enter a 

description, the system adds the text in the Description field to the Memo fields of the line 

items. You can change this text. 

5. 
Type a comment to record in the transaction history in the Comment field. For example, 

write a comment to indicate what the change was or why it was made. Comments appear 

on the History tab after you save the record. 

Each time you edit the journal entry, you can add another comment. The system adds the 

comment to the transaction history with the date. The original comment won’t appear in the 

Comment field but appears on the History tab. 

6. 
In the Reference number field, type a reference number for the journal entry.  

7. 
When you do not have scanning enabled on your system, then the Attachments field 

appears.  

---


<!-- Page 291 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

When your system has scanning enabled, then you can attach a document in the Documents 

section. 

Use the Attachments field to associate a document in the system to support the 

transaction. You can also upload a new file into the system by clicking the Choose files 

button. You can attach any type of file to the transaction, including scanned images, 

spreadsheets, and word-processor documents. Attached files are uploaded to the system for 

permanent, safe storage. You can only add attachments if you have the appropriate 

attachment permissions. 

• 
Show all/Show unattached: Click this link to toggle between showing all existing files 

in the system to showing only files that are not attached to any other record in the 

system. 

•

Turning This Journal Entry into a Recurring Journal Entry 

1.

schedule. When you submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a recurring A/P invoice 

based on the current invoice.

the system to start creating the recurring journal entries. 

3. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select: 

• 
Never: To keep the journal entry perpetually running, select Never.  

• 
Number of occurrences: The End after field appears. To have the journal entry run for 

a limited number of times, type the number of times you want the journal entry to 

recur in the End after field.  

• 
End date: To have the journal entry recur until a specific date, select End date and 

then, in the End on field, type the date on which the last journal entry is to recur.  

4. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, select the frequency that you want the system to 

generate the recurring journal entries. The options are:

None 

• 
Days 

• 
Weeks 

• 
Months 

• 
Years

Months, then type the number of months to repeat by, such as 6 to have the system create 

a journal entry every 6 months.

create the journal entry at the end of the month.

Entering Job Cost Line Item Entries 

If you have the Job Cost application installed, then you may see the Job Cost entries list in the 

journal entry record. Enter the line item information in the Job cost entries list. 

1. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location of the job that you are entering a journal 

entry for.  

• 
For Job Cost line items, the location that you select must have at least one job that is 

not in the Closed status.  

• 
If you selected a source entity in the Transaction information section, then the location 

is the target entity. 

• 
This automatically updates the Base currency field to show the base currency of the 

location. 

2. 
In the Job name drop-down list, select the job for which you are creating a journal entry.  

3. 
In the Cost code drop-down list, select the cost code of the line item.  

When you save the journal entry, this line item applies to the WIP account selected for the 
cost code record (on page 530 ). 

4. 
In the Job unit drop-down list, select the unit of the line item.  

The selected cost code must allow segment -level tracking. 

5. 
Use the Txn currency drop-down list to select the currency of the line item.  

This column shows only if your company has multi-currency enabled. 

6. 
In the Debit (or Transaction debit) field, enter the amount that this line item is debiting.  

• 
If you enter a debit amount, you cannot enter a credit amount for the same line item. 

• 
The total of all entered debit amounts shows at the bottom of the section. If the 

journal entry is the Both type, debits and credits are separated between standard and 

Job Cost line items. 

• 
This automatically updates the Base debit field to show the same amount expressed in 

the base currency. 

7. 
In the Credit (or Transaction credit) field, enter the amount that this line item is crediting.  

• 
If you enter a credit amount, you cannot enter a debit amount for the same line item.

Finishing the Journal Entry 

When you finish entering or editing the journal entry: 

• 
If journal entry approvals are disabled, you can either save the transaction as a draft or post 

it. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the entry without posting it. Later, 

you or another user can review the entry and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the journal entry. 

• 
You can also click the More actions button and then select Post and Print to post the 

journal entry and then print the record. 

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled, submit the journal entry for approval. 

• 
Click Submit to send the journal entry to the approval queue.  

• 
Click Submit & new to submit the journal entry to the approval queue, and then open 

a new journal entry. 

After a journal entry transaction has been approved and posted, editing the entry is not 
allowed and the Edit link isn’t available. To make any changes, reverse the transaction or

Fields 

This topic describes the fields that appear when you are working with journal entry records. For 

information about fields when importing journal entries, see Journal Entries Template. 

Journal Entries List 

Title 
This column contains the name of the journal.

This column contains the journal symbol. 

Book 
This column contains the reporting book for which the journal was 

created. For most companies, the reporting book is accrual. If you opted 

for dual-method reporting, the choices are accrual, cash, or accrual and 

cash. 

Transaction Tab 

Transaction number 
The system assigns a transaction number to the journal entry record. 

Transaction numbers cannot be changed. 

Book(s) 
Select Accrual, Cash, or another book where you want to log this 

transaction.  

Journal 
Select the journal to which you want to add the transaction. This field is 

required. 

Posting date 
By default, this field displays today’s date. You can also enter a different 

date for the transaction or select a date from the pop-up calendar. 

Automatic reversal 

date 

If the transaction will reverse at a later date, this is the date on which the 

transaction will reverse. 

Enter a date only if you want to post a reverse transaction to this 

transaction. The reverse transaction is identical, except it is the inverse 

and therefore “zeroes out” the transaction. You cannot enter a date that 

has passed. 

Description 
Type a description of the transaction.

Buttons 

The buttons on the Journal entries page differ depending on whether journal entries require 

approval or not, and whether you are adding or editing a record. 

When journal entry approvals are disabled, these buttons appear: 

Post 
Posts the journal entry to the General Ledger 

This button appears when you are creating, viewing, or editing a new 

journal entry.

Approve Budget Change Orders 

This section shows you how to manage approvals for job cost budget change orders.
