#### Job Cost Approval Process
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 309*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Job Cost Approval Process 

The typical approval process for a budget change order is as follows: 

1. 
A person adds a budget change order for a job in the Active (budget locked) status. The 

change order may or may not be subject to approval. 

• 
If the job or job type is under an approval policy and approval workflow, then the 

change order is submitted for approval.  

• 
If the job and job type is not under an approval policy or approval workflow, then the 

system bypasses approval and posts the change order. 

• 
If the change order amount is negative (decreases the budget), then the system 

bypasses approval and posts the change order. 

• 
If the change order is for a segment budget, then the system bypasses approval and 

posts the change order. 

2. 
If your company enabled approval notifications, then the system sends an email notification 

to approvers.  

The user must enable email notifications on the My preferences page to receive approval 
notifications. 

3. 
The system adds the change order to the Approval workbench. 

4. 
An approver approves or declines the change order in the Approval workbench. 

• 
If the change order is approved, then the change order amount is removed from the 

Budget changes pending calculation and is added to the Budget changes calculation. 

• 
If the change order is declined, then the change order amount is removed from the 

Budget changes pending calculation.

The Approve [transaction type] box opens.

Click the Approve button.

transactions.

##### Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 322*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

•

You also have the option to close and delete declined purchase orders to remove them from your 

Approval Workbench list page. You must have Delete permissions. 

Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices 

See the How to Get Here (on page 303) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

When the Approval workbench is filtered by A/P invoices, an additional button appears in the 

upper-right corner labeled Review & approve. This button allows you to quickly open and review 

invoices in the order they appear in the approval queue.  

To review and approve A/P invoices: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Approval workbench. 

3. 
Select the A/P invoice option. Set any other filters as needed. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. The system filters the list so that it shows only A/P invoices. 

5. 
Click the Review & approve button. The A/P invoice page opens. If the A/P invoice has an 

attachment and you have enabled the image viewer, the attachment displays in a separate 

window. If not, the invoice image will show on the same page as the invoice. 

If the Review & approve button does not appear, there are no A/P invoices in queue to 
approve. 

6. 
Review the A/P invoice. You can also edit the invoice at the same time. 

7. 
Click one of the buttons: 

• 
Approve & next: Approve the current A/P invoice, and then have the system display 

the next A/P invoice to evaluate. If you made any changes to the invoice, your changes 

are saved and the invoice is routed to the next person for approval. 

• 
Approve & next > Next: Skip the current A/P invoice and display the next A/P invoice 

in your queue. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

---



##### Exporting Transactions to Excel
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 323*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

• 
Decline & next: Decline the A/P invoice, and then display the next A/P invoice to 

evaluate. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Add approver: Add someone who you think should approve the A/P invoice. Any 

changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Send back: Send the invoice back to the previous approver. Any changes you made to 

the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Done: Close the approval queue. 

8. 
Click the Done button to exit the review and approval process. 

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through approvals, and then gets posted, 
RealPage Accounting sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status from 

Pending to Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the 
invoice. We also send updates to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along 
with the payment details. 

Exporting Transactions to Excel 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Workbench`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench`


You can export transaction data from the Approval workbench or Spend management 

workbench to an Excel file. The data included in the file depends on the columns that you have 

enabled in the workbench. 

To export data using the Export to Excel button: 

1. 
Click the Export to Excel button in the upper-right corner of the approval queue. 

The Excel file downloads with any column data configured in the workbench. 

2. 
In the Save as box, name the Excel file, and determine a file location for the exported file.

Click Save.

You can save your workbench filters and selections as a view for settings that you use regularly.

drop-down list.

In the workbench, set up the filters that you want to save.

Select a date, property, or vendor that you frequently access.

Click the Save view as button.

If you want the view to be applied whenever you open the workbench, select the Default 

check box. You can also apply the view as needed by selecting it in the Apply view 

drop-down list.

by using the Approval Workbench Views option.

1. 
Find the transaction that you want to review, and then click the View or Edit link. 

When the A/P invoice transaction is first opened, the system automatically opens the 
attachment to view. You can choose to not show attachments automatically on the My 

Preferences page by selecting the Do not show attachments automatically within invoices 
check box. 

2. 
Review the transaction, make changes as needed if you selected Edit, and then click Save. 

When Gasoline is selected in the Expense category field and the tax rate is enabled in 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Setup > Expense Report Configuration, and when you click the`


Amount field, a box opens that allows you to enter the number of miles. When you click 

Save, the system recalculates the amount with the tax rate included. 

3. 
Continue by approving or declining the transaction.  

After the journal entry has gone through the approval process and been approved, it cannot 

be edited.

##### Adding an Approver to a Transaction
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 326*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an Approver to a Transaction 

See the How to Get Here (on page 303) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

As an approver, you can add another approver to a transaction in the Approval workbench. 

To add an approver to a transaction: 

1. 
Click the Add approver link next to the transaction. 

The Add approver box opens. 

2. 
Type any comments explaining why you are adding the approver. 

You can drag the lower-right corner of the Comments text box to resize it as needed. 

3. 
In the Additional approver drop-down list, select the user that you want to add to the 

transaction, and then click the Done button. 

All users in the drop-down list have access to the transaction ’s location.

##### Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 327*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver 

See the How to Get Here (on page 303) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

Some transactions require approvals from multiple levels. If a transaction pending your approval 

was approved by someone else, you can send the transaction back to that approver instead of 

declining the transaction outright. 

To send a transaction back to the previous approver: 

1. 
On the Approval workbench - My approvals page, click the Send back link in the Send 

back column next to the transaction. 

The Send back box opens. 

2. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

3. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transaction no 

longer appears in your queue. 

Sending Back Multiple Transactions 

To send back multiple transactions to the previous approver: 

1. 
From the Approval workbench - My approvals page, select the check box next to each 

transaction that you want to send back to the previous approver. 

2. 
Click the Send back link in the Send back column next to any of the transactions that you 

selected. 

The Send back box opens. 

3. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

4. 
Select the additional approver from the Additional approver drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transactions no 

longer appear in your queue. 

---

Viewing the Available Budget for a Transaction 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

To view the available budget for a transaction in the approval queue: 

• 
Click the $ link in the Actions column next to the transaction. 

The Available budget page opens with budget information for the property and account 

associated with the transaction. See Available Budget Page for more information. 

Viewing the Approval History of a Transaction 

See the How to Get Here (on page 303) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 304) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all link to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction, and then click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history box opens. See Approval history list (on page 339) for more 

information. 

Including Declined Transactions in the Approval Workbench 

See the How to Get Here (on page 303) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Declined transactions are not included in the approval workbench by default. 

To include declined transactions:  

1. 
Filter (on page 304) the Approval workbench as needed. 

2. 
Select the Include declined check box to include declined transactions. 

3. 
If you want to make this the default setting, then you can save a new custom view (on page 

313) in the workbench and set it as the Default view.

#### Approval History List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 349*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Approval History List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 340) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use this page to review a transaction’s approval history. This page displays when you click a status 

in the Approval workbench. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Financial Suite auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver. Default policies and workflows are visible only to admin 
users, including any events or actions logged in the approval history. 

Columns 

• 
Policy type: This column shows the policy type that the system used to approve the item. 

• 
Policy name: This column shows the policy name that the system used to approve the item. 

Click the link to view policy details. 

• 
Workflow name: This column shows the name of the workflow that the system used in the 

transaction. Click the link to view workflow details. 

• 
Approver role/user: This column contains a link to information about the person who 

decided on the approval. Click to view the role assignment details. You can find out who is 

assigned to a particular role with this link. 

• 
Approved/Declined by: This column contains the user name of the person who made the 

approval decisions. 

• 
Event date: This column contains the date that the transaction last underwent an approval 

event. (It was submitted for approval or partially approved.) 

• 
Comments: This column contains the comments the approver made along with his decision. 

• 
State: This column contains the status of the approval. 

• 
Action type: This column contains the approval status of the transaction. 

• 
Action comments: This column contains the comments associated with the action in the 

state. 

• 
Submitted by: This column contains the name of the user who submitted the transaction. 

“Console member” appears when the user accesses RealPage Financial Suite through the 
console rather than by logging in directly.

Viewing Approval Policy Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here (on page 340) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval policy that was used to decide on a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 304) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval History List (on page 339) for more 

information. 

5. 
Click the text in the Policy name column to open the Approval policy manager, allowing 

you to review the policy details. 

6. 
Click the Close button to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to 

print the approval policy details. 

Viewing Workflow Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here (on page 340) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval workflow that was used to route a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 304) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval history list (on page 339) for more 

information. 

5. 
Click the link in the Workflow name column to display the Approval workflow details. 

6. 
Click Close to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to print the

Budgets List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets`


Use the Budgets list to view and manage job budgets for all jobs. From this page, you can: 

• 
Add, view, edit, and delete job budgets. 

• 
Export job budgets. 

• 
Add and view job budget change orders. 

Alternatively, you can view the budgets for an individual job (on page 34 ) by clicking the Budgets 
link next to the job in the Jobs list. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Before you enter job budgets: 

• 
You must set up the job. For more information, see Adding a Job (on page 18). 

• 
The job type’s cost codes must be assigned to draw model details. For more information, 

see Assign Cost Codes (on page 570). 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage job budgets: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Adding a Job Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Budgets > Add`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > 
 Budgets`


When you add a new job, the system automatically creates empty budgets for each job cost code. 

You can export the list of budgets to a CSV file and then re-import the file with the budget details 

instead of entering each cost code budget manually. See Importing a Job Budget (on page 34) for 

more information. 

You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job status 

is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more information, see 

Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354). 

To add a job budget: 

1. 
In the Job drop-down list, select the job to which the budget applies.  

The Job type field automatically updates to show the job type associated with the selected 

job. 

If you accessed the Budgets page from the Jobs list or you are editing an existing budget, 
these fields automatically populate with the corresponding job and job type. 

2. 
In the Cost code drop-down list, select the cost code for which you are entering a budget.  

3. 
In the Description field, type a description for the budget.  

If you do not provide a description, then the system automatically applies the description 

associated with the selected cost code when you save the budget. 

4. 
In the Amount field, type the budget amount for the cost code.  

5. 
In the Prior commitments offset field, type the amount by which to offset the Open 

commitments amount for the cost code. The Prior commitments offset amount reduces 

the Open commitments amount (on page 187) for the cost code on the Job Status Inquiry 

and Job Status Summary reports. 

6. 
To track costs to this budget with A/P invoices, select the Billable check box. 

---

Importing a Job Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Budgets by Job`


When you add a new job, the system automatically creates empty budgets for each job cost code. 

You can export the list of budgets to a CSV file and then re-import the file with the budget details 

instead of entering each cost code budget manually. 

You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 
status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 
information, see Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354 ). 

To import a cost code budget: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, select the Budgets by job link next to the desired job. 

The (Job Name) - Budgets page opens with a list of budget details for each of the job’s cost 

codes. 

2. 
On the Budgets page, click Export budgets template. 

• 
If the job type includes segments, click Budget to start the download process. 

• 
If the job type does not include segments, the system immediately starts the 

download process. 

The system either downloads the chartexport-(job name).csv or prompts you to open or 

save the chartexport-(job name).csv file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the chartexport-(job name).csv file. 

The file automatically provides information for some fields: 

• 
JOB NAME: This is the name of the job. 

• 
COST CODE: This is the code of the cost code. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: This is a description of the cost code. 

---

In the BUDGET column for each budgeted cost code, enter the budget amount of that cost 

code. 

For all cost codes that do not have a budget for the job, leave the BUDGET column as “0”. 

The example below shows a cost code budget import list. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as.  

6. 
In the Save as box, use the Save as type drop-down list to select “CSV (comma delimited) 

(*.csv).” 

7. 
Change the File name or location as needed, and then click Save. 

8. 
On the (Job Name) - Budgets page, click Import. The system opens the Import budget 

information box. 

9. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

10. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

11. 
Click Done. 

12. 
If you are adding unit- or segment-level budgets, you must add those budgets separately. 

For more information, see Importing a Job Segment Budget (on page 96). If you are not 

tracking segment-level budgets for the job, you can skip this step. 

For more information about importing data, see Importing in RealPage Accounting.

Closing or Reopening Cost Codes for Job Budgets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Budgets > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets > Edit`


Use this procedure to close or reopen individual cost codes from the job budget record as work 

progresses or changes. Closing a cost code prevents additional costs from being posted after that 

portion of the job is complete, while reopening it allows you to record late transactions,  adjust 

or correct the budget, or continue work. 

Before You Begin 

Before completing these steps, keep the following in mind: 

• 
The Closed to new activity check box appears only when you edit a job budget. 

• 
Closing a cost code prevents new cost activity from being recorded for that budget’s cost 

code. 

• 
Reopening a cost code allows additional transactions or corrections. 

• 
Changes may affect reporting and audit history. 

Procedures 

To close or reopen cost codes for job budgets:

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application. 

2. 
On the All tab, go to the Periodic Tasks section, and then select the Budgets menu option. 

The Budgets list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the desired budget. 

The Budget page opens. 

4. 
Toggle the Closed to new activity check box as needed: 

• 
Select the check box to close the cost code. 

• 
Clear the check box to reopen the cost code. 

5. 
Click Save. 

What’s Next? 

If you need to add segment-level budgets, see Adding or Editing a Job Segment Budget (on 

page 95). 

If you are done entering budgets for the job, change the job status to Active (budgets locked). 

When the job is in this status, people cannot add new budgets and must use budget change 

orders to update any budget. Budget change orders are different from budget edits in a couple of 

ways: 

• 
If your company uses the approval process, budget change orders are subject to approval. 

• 
The system tracks budget change orders separately from the original budget. This allows 

you to monitor the number and total amount of changes to the job budget.

Adding a Budget Change Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets > Change Order > 
Add`


You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job status 

is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more information, see 

Adding a Budget Change Order (on page 354). 

You cannot add a new change order to a budget that already has a change order pending 

approval. 

To add a change order: 

1. 
Click Add. 

2. 
In the Effective date field, type or select the date on which the change order takes effect. 

3. 
In the Amount field, type the amount of the change order. 

4. 
In the Comment field, type a comment about the source of the change order. 

5. 
Use the Attachments drop-down list to add an existing attachment, or click the Add link at 

the drop of the drop-down list to upload a new supporting document for the change order. 

6. 
When your changes are complete: 

• 
Click Save to save the change order and close the Change order page.  

• 
Alternatively, click More actions, and then click Save and new to save the change 

order and open a new Change order page. 

Viewing a Budget Change Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets > Change Order > 
View`


You can view budget change orders if they are still in the Submitted status. To view an Approved 

or Partially Approved change order, you must have the Edit approved change orders permission 

(on page 100). 

To view a budget change order: 

1. 
On the Budget change orders page, locate the change order you want to view. 

2. 
Click the View link to the left of the change order. 

3. 
When you’re done viewing the change order, click Done.

Editing a Budget Change Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets > Change Order > 
Edit`


You can edit budget change orders if they are still in the Submitted status. To edit an Approved or 

Partially Approved change order, you must have the Edit approved change orders permission (on 

page 100). 

To edit a budget change order: 

1. 
On the Budget change orders page, locate the change order you want to edit. 

2. 
Click the Edit link to the left of the change order. 

3. 
In the Amount field, enter the amount of the change order.  

4. 
In the Comment field, enter a comment about the source of the change order.  

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save. 

Deleting a Budget Change Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets > Change Order > 
Delete`


You can delete only budget change orders in the Submitted status. 

To delete a budget change order: 

1. 
On the Budget change orders page, locate the change order you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete link to the right of the change order. 

3. 
Click OK in the confirmation box. 

The system removes the change order from the Budget change orders page. This also 

removes the change order amount from all budget calculations. 

What’s Next? 

• 
If the budget is attached to a job that is subject to approval and the budget change order is 

for a positive amount (increases the budget), the change order goes to the Approval 

workbench. Until the change order is approved, this amount shows in the Pending budget 

changes field. 

• 
If the budget is attached to a job that is subject to approval and the budget change order is 

for a negative amount (decreases the budget), the change order is automatically approved 

and this amount shows in the Budget changes field. 

• 
If the budget is not attached to a job that is subject to approval, the change order is 

automatically approved and this amount shows in the Budget changes field.

Use the Reserves list to view and manage reserve accounts. Replacement reserves simplify how 

you track replacement or repair expenses and then organize and package them as reimbursement 

requests to the lender.  

You can use replacement reserves to: 

•

• 
Generate draw request packages with supporting documents for presentation to the lender 

for reimbursement. 

• 
Apply receipts after receiving funds. 

• 
Run a Reserve Status Inquiry. 

• 
Integrate with the RealPage Accounting Security model. 

From this page, you can: 

• 
View reserve accounts. 

• 
Add reserve accounts. 

• 
Edit reserve accounts. 

• 
Delete reserve accounts.

Adding a Reserve 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks >`


 Reserves 

To add a reserve: 

1. 
In the Property drop-down list, select the property you want to associate with the reserve. 

The system auto-populates the Reserve name field with the property name. 

2. 
If you want to override the default name, enter your preferred reserve name. 

3. 
In the Funding source drop-down list, select the funding source for this reserve. 

You can no longer change the funding source after saving. 

4. 
In the Minimum reserve balance field, enter a value that you want to maintain for the 

reserve. The system warns you when the value exceeds the minimum when creating draws 

against this reserve. 

5. 
In the Past months activity allowed on draws field, enter a value to limit the A/P invoice 

records available for selection while creating draws. 

The system auto-populates the Reserve accounts list with all of the reserve accounts 

associated with the selected funding source.  

6. 
In the Maximum amount to be drawn column, enter the maximum withdrawal amount that 

you want to set for each reserve account.  

7. 
Click the Save button.

Adding an External Commitment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > 
 External Commitments`


You can add an external commitment manually or import them in bulk (on page 371) using a 

predefined template. 

To add an external commitment manually: 

1. 
In the Job cost external commitments list, click the Add button. 

The Job cost external commitment page opens. 

2. 
Select a job from the Job drop-down list. 

3. 
Select a cost code from the Cost code drop-down list. The cost code options are 

determined by the job you selected. 

4. 
In the Date field, type or select the commitment date for the costs. 

5. 
In the Amount field, type the commitment amount. 

6. 
Optionally, in the Description field, type a brief description of the external commitment. 

7. 
Optionally, in the PO number field, type the purchase order number associated with the 

external commitment. 

8. 
Click Save. 

The external commitment is added to the Job cost external commitments list and will 

appear in the Job Status Inquiry and Job Status Summary reports in the External 

commitment column. 

---

Importing External Commitments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Job Cost > External 
Commitment > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > External Commitments > 
Import External Commitments`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Downloading and Filling In the Template 

To download the import template for external commitments: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Import data menu option. 

The Import data page opens. 

2. 
In the Set up job cost section, click the Template link next to External commitment. 

The system either downloads the External Commitment.xls file or prompts you to open or 

save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the External Commitment.xls file and fill in the required information: 

• 
Job name: Type the name of the job to which the commitment applies. Make sure to 

type the job name exactly as it appears in the Jobs list. 

• 
Cost code: Type the cost code to assign to the external commitment. Make sure to 

type the cost code exactly as it appears in the Cost codes list. 

• 
Commitment date: Type the date on which to commit the costs. 

• 
Amount: Type the amount of the cost commitment. 

4. 
Optionally, fill in the following fields: 

• 
Description: Type a brief description for the external commitment. 

• 
PO number: Type the purchase order number associated with the external 

commitment. 

5. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

Importing Data From the Template 

To import the template back into the system:

Close Job 

This section discusses how to close jobs or cost codes within a job.  

---



#### Close Job Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 388*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Close Job Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Close Job`


Use the Close job page to close jobs or cost codes within a job. Use this option sparingly; closing 

a job creates a credit to the selected cost codes, effectively zeroing them out on the job status 

view.  

If you close a job (or a specific cost code), then the job or cost code is no longer available for any 
transaction. If you want to preserve the job’s information but still close the accounts, you can 
create contra lines for each WIP account on the job (on page 380 ). 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 389*



##### Closing a Job
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 389*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to close jobs: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Job Cost 
Job 
Close 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Closing a Job 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Close Job`


To close a job: 

1. 
Use the Jobs drop-down list to select the job you are closing. 

2. 
Select one of the Close options: 

• 
Completed job: To close an entire job, select this option.  

• 
Selected cost codes: To close specific cost codes, select this option, and then use the 

Cost codes drop-down list to select the cost codes.  

• 
To include all cost codes, choose the Select all check box. 

• 
To include multiple cost codes, select the individual check boxes for the cost 

codes you want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific cost code, type the cost code in the Search field. 

3. 
In the G/L posting date field, type or select the date you want to post the closing journal 

entry to the General Ledger. 

• 
If you want to exclude the job cost history from the journal entry, then select the 

Exclude job cost history check box. 

• 
If you want to create a fixed asset for any cost code whose Close account matches an 

asset account on a fixed asset class, then select the Create fixed assets check box. 

This option appears only if your company has enabled the Fixed Assets application. 

• 
To group cost codes that use the same WIP account and Close account in one closing 

journal entry, select the Summarize by account check box. 

---



##### Preserving Job Information When Closing Accounts
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 390*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

4. 
Select the Allow additional activity check box if you want the job or the selected cost codes 

to remain open so they can still be used in transactions. For example, you could close the 

entire job or specific cost codes each month to zero them out in the job status view while 

leaving them open for future activity. 

5. 
Select the Process construction fees check box if you want to calculate the construction 

fees for the job activity that you are closing even if the job or the selected cost codes will 

remain open for additional activity. 

• 
If you didn’t charge construction fees for a job activity that you previously closed, you 

can select the Include closed transactions check box to process those construction 

fees when you are actually closing the job. 

6. 
Click Preview close. 

7. 
Review the close job preview, and then click Proceed.  

The system shows a confirmation message that indicates if the job or cost codes closed. 

Preserving Job Information When Closing Accounts 

Alternatively, you can preserve the job’s information but still close the accounts.  

To do so: 

1. 
Create contra lines for each work-in-progress (WIP) account on the job.  

Number the contra lines to show at the bottom of the cost code structure. 

2. 
When you are ready to close the job, create a journal entry that credits the contra lines and 

debits the capital asset accounts. 

This preserves the detail of the job but closes the job out of work-in-progress. 

3. 
To ensure that no additional transactions can be entered for the job, edit the job, and then 

change the Job status to Closed.

cost codes for the job, the closed cost codes are not available for selection.

The system creates a journal entry for each selected cost code and closes the amount to the 

cost code’s Close to account.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 395*

Generate Tenant Invoice Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Generate Tenant Invoice`


Use the Generate Tenant Invoice page to generate an invoice for a tenant or customer. 

Generating a Tenant Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Generate Tenant Invoice`


To generate a tenant invoice: 

1. 
Use the Job drop-down list to select the job for which you want to generate an invoice. 

2. 
Use the Cost codes drop-down list to select the cost codes for the jobs for which you want 
to generate an invoice. 

3. 
Select your preferred Print option. 

• 
Detail (include invoice details): Select this option to display the invoice amount details 
by cost code. 

• 
Summary (one line per cost code): Select this option to display the invoice amount 
summarized by cost code. 

4. 
Click the Apply filters button. 

The system displays the list of items matching the filter criteria. 

5. 
In the list of items, select the check box for the vendors for which you want to generate 
invoices. 

6. 
Click the Preview button. 

The system displays a preview of the invoice. 

7. 
Click the Generate button to create the invoice. 

The system adds the transaction to the A/R Invoices list and marks the transaction as Billed 
in the Job Cost Activity list. 

For internal billing, the system creates two journal entries, depending on the selected Bill to 

option.

Lien Releases 

This section explains how to create and package lien releases for job cost payments. 

---



#### Lien Releases List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 398*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Lien Releases List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Lien Releases`


Lien releases are frequently used in construction and real estate development. A lien release is a 

legal document that removes a lien or claim from a property. Liens are commonly filed by 

contractors to ensure that they’re compensated for their work, and they’re removed after they 

receive the payment. 

Use the Lien releases list in RealPage Financial Suite to create and package lien releases for job 

cost payments. You can even customize your own lien release template by uploading it through 

Platform Services.  

The Lien releases list is blank until you enter a time frame for job cost payments or filter 

payments by one of the columns, such as Vendor name or Job name. For payments that are more 

than a year old, use the Payment date column to filter by a specific date. From there, you can 

select which payments you want to include in your lien release package. 

---

user’s permissions. 

Generating a Lien Release Package 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > Lien Releases`


Use the Lien releases list to create lien releases for job cost payments and package them into a 

single document. You can create lien release packages for payments at either the top level or 

entity level. Payments must be posted to the General Ledger to be included in a package; the list 

does not display any payments that are still pending approval. 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, click the Lien releases menu option. 

The Lien releases list opens. 

3. 
Filter the list to search for payments. You have two options: 

• 
Type a specific number of days in the text box at the top of the list to show all job cost 

payments made within that time frame. 

• 
Use the text fields below the column names to filter the list by specific criteria, such as 

a vendor name or job name. 

4. 
Click the Package lien releases button. 

The page name changes to Package lien releases and a series of buttons appear. 

5. 
Select the check box next to each payment that you want to include in the lien release 

package. 

6. 
Click the Generate package button. 

The Select document template box opens.

Creating and Uploading a Lien Release Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > 
 Printed Doc 
Templates`


Use the Printed doc templates list in the Platform Services (Customization Services) application 

to upload a customized lien release template for your lien release packages. The template must 

be created in Microsoft Word using RealPage’s Word Merge Tool. This tool is an add-in program 

that connects to your RealPage database so that you can easily find and insert merge fields 

directly into a Word document to create custom templates. 

Creating a Lien Release Template in Word 

To create a custom lien release template: 

1. 
Download and install (on page 391) RealPage’s Word Merge Tool. 

2. 
Log in (on page 392) to the tool. 

3. 
Open a Word file (on page 393) for your template. 

4. 
If you are working with a blank document, add the static text to the Word document such as 

the title, and your business name and address. If you are working with an existing template, 

change the existing text to reflect your business needs. 

5. 
Use the Word Merge Tool to insert merge fields (on page 394) in your document template. 

Merge fields are used as placeholders for your data; you can pull in information such as the 

job name, property name, property address, vendor name, vendor address, payment 

amount, and more. 

When inserting merge fields, set the Functional area as Job Cost and the Template as Lien 

release documents. 

6. 
Sync the lien release template (on page 396) with RealPage Financial Suite. 

Uploading the Lien Release Template to RealPage Accounting 

After you’ve created your lien release template, you can upload it to the Printed doc templates 

list as the Lien release template type:

other lists. For example, “Lien Releases”.

Downloading and Installing the Word Merge Tool 

The RealPage Word Merge Add-in tool connects to your RealPage database so that you can easily 

find and insert Word merge fields directly into a Word document in order to create custom 

template.  

To download and install the tool: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Configuration section, click the Company menu option. 

3. 
Scroll to the bottom of the Company information page, and then click the Download Word 

Merge tool link.  

The system copies the RPWordMergeTool ZIP file to your Downloads folder. 

4. 
Extract the RPWordMergeTool ZIP file. 

5. 
In the unzipped folder, open the \RPWordMergeTool\WMTBUILD folder, and then 

double-click the setup.exe file to run it.  

6. 
If prompted, click the Install button to allow the application to be installed. 

7. 
Click Close. 

After the tool is installed, a new tab labeled RealPage Word Merge Add-In appears in 

Microsoft Word.  

To verify installation: 

1. 
Open Word. 

2. 
Look for the RealPage Word Merge Add-In option on the Word ribbon.

Choosing a Word File for Your Document Template 

Choosing a Word File for Your Document Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Printed Doc Templates 
> Template`


The first step in creating a document template is to choose a Word file for the template. To do 

this, you can: 

• 
Create a new Word document from scratch. 

• 
Use an existing Word document that you created previously. 

• 
Export an existing document template from the Printed document templates list to use as a 

starting point, and then edit it in Word. 

After you have selected and opened a Word file, you can customize your custom document 

template to suit the needs of your business. 

Exporting a Document Template from the Printed Document Templates List 

To export an existing document template from RealPage Financial Suite: 

1. 
In the Printed document templates list, locate the document template you want to use, and 

then click the Template link next to it. 

The Word document exports to your local drive. 

2. 
Open the file in Word and edit the file as needed to suit your company’s needs. 

Using the Word Merge Tool to Insert Merge Fields 

To use the Word Merge tool: 

1. 
Open your document template in Word.  

You can open a new blank Word document or download an existing template using the 

Platform Services > Printed Document Templates > Template link.  

2. 
In Word, click the RealPage Word Merge Add-in option. If you do not see the option, see 

Downloading and Installing the Word Merge Tool (on page 391). The package that you 

download also contains some troubleshooting information in the Installation Guide. 

3. 
In the Login box, type your company name, user name, and password. 

4. 
Click the Insert Merge Fields option. The Merge Fields box opens. 

5. 
Select the desired functional area.  

The functional areas correspond with the Accounting applications Company, Accounts 

Receivable, Property Management, and Condo and Co-op.  

For the purpose of illustration, this example uses the Property Management application.

Syncing a Document Template with RealPage Accounting 

After you have finished inserting merge fields into your document template, you must sync the 

document with RealPage Accounting. 

You can sync a new document template or one that you downloaded to make changes. 

To sync a template with RealPage Accounting: 

1. 
Click RealPage Word Merge Add-In. 

2. 
Click the Sync to Product option to update the template in the system. 

3. 
Type the name of the template. 

4. 
In the Functional area drop-down list, select the application that the template is associated 

with. 

5. 
In the Template drop-down list, select the template type that you used when you created 

the template. 

6. 
Click Save. The system saves the template. You can now use the template from the 

application that you selected in step 4.  

You can access these templates in the Platform Services (Customization Services) 
application using the Printed document templates menu option.

Reports 

Job Cost & Reserves provides several reports that allow you to review job activity and 

performance at your properties: 

• 
Job Setup Summary: (on page 435) This report shows job type details for all job types 

currently set up. 

• 
Job Cost Activity: (on page 439) This report lists the A/P invoice and journal entries 

associated with job cost codes. 

• 
Code Cost Structure: (on page 444) This report lists the cost codes assigned to a job. 

• 
Job Budget: (on page 447) This report shows budget details per cost code assigned to a 

job. 

• 
Draw Detail: (on page 451) This report lists draw detail information for a job. 

• 
Job Cost Status: (on page 460) This report shows the commitment and A/P invoice 

information for a job. 

• 
Job Status Summary: (on page 465) This report provides job status inquiry (on page 165) 

information summarized by either jobs or report codes. 

• 
WIP Account Reconciliation: (on page 475) This report lists WIP account information for 

selected properties. 

• 
Open Invoices: (on page 478) This report shows open A/P invoices by job for selected 

properties. 

Column headers in Job Cost reports are frozen to help you keep track of information as you scroll 
down the report.

#### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 410*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 401) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

#### Storing Standard Reports and Charts
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 413*



##### Viewing a Stored Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 413*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

You can process and store the report or chart either before or after viewing it. 

Viewing a Stored Report 

After the system runs the report on the date that you selected, you can find the report in either 

the My stored reports list or the Reports center. 

To view a stored report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Open the application where you created the report. 

2. 
Select the My stored reports option located in the Reports column of the menu. 

The My stored reports list opens with a list of reports stored in the application. 

3. 
Find the report that you want to view and then verify the report date in the Run date/time 

column. Verifying the report date helps you avoid missing data. For example, if you 

scheduled the report to run two weeks ago, you would be missing the last two weeks of 

data. 

4. 
Click one of the following links to open your report in the format it was stored:  

• 
HTML: Opens the report in a new browser tab as a web page. 

• 
PDF: Opens a printable PDF version of the report that you can print and download. 

• 
CSV: Downloads a CSV file containing the report data. This is a good format to 

download if you want to import the data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Opens a text version of the report in the web browser. 

• 
View Status: Opens the report in your configured cloud account. If there is no cloud 

link for the report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 410). 

• 
Success: Opens the report in Reporting Portal. If there was an error processing the 

report, then the View status link appears in the column instead. See Viewing a Report 

Error Log for error details. 

If you have not yet processed the report offline, then click the Create offline link to process 
the report.

Storing a Report in My Stored Reports 

You can generate reports on demand and store them in the My stored reports list for later 

access. 

To store a report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime . 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand. 

3. 
In the Delivery options section, select the Store report option. 

4. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 

If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, 
then the Location ID and Name is added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for. 

5. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves a report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Saves reports in an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Saves the report as a text file. 

Only the Printable and Excel options are available for report groups. When storing report 
groups as an Excel file, each report appears on a separate tab. 

6. 
Click OK.

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime . 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand. 

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  

By default, you can choose from cloud-storage targets that either you ’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all cloud 
targets. 

5. 
If you want to override the default path where the report is delivered in the cloud-storage 

target, then type a different path in the Path field. 

6. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 

If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, 
then the Location ID and Name is added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for. 

7. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves a report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

---

Memorized Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 417) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Memorizing a report retains the report parameters so you don’t have to select them each time 

you want to run or display the report. When you memorize a report, you can assign it a unique 

name so you can add the report to dashboards or report groups or schedule it to run on a 

recurring basis. We recommend that you test run the report with the desired parameters to verify 

that the report output is correct before memorizing the report. 

A memorized report can be public or private. Public reports are available to all system users. 
Private reports are available only to the report owner and system administrators. 

Memorized Reports Locations 

Memorized reports appear in the Memorized reports list (on page 419) and in the Reports 

center. 

The Memorized reports list is accessible from most RealPage Financial Suite applications; 

however, it displays only the reports that were memorized in the application you access it from. 

For example, if you click the Memorized reports option in the Cash Management menu, then the 

list will include only reports memorized in Cash Management. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Memorizing a report requires that you have the permissions to do so. You must have permissions 

to access and run a report in order to memorize it. Permissions for users, groups, or roles are 

configured in the Company setup. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

##### Editing a Memorized Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 430*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Editing a Memorized Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 417) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

You can edit a memorized report or chart only if you are the owner or a system administrator, 

even if the report or chart was made public. As the owner, you can change any parameter, 

including who owns it. The only field you cannot change is the report type.  

To edit a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, click the Edit link next to the report or chart that you want to 

change. The Edit memorized report page opens. The fields on this page correspond with 

the report’s type.  

2. 
Update the fields in the General information section as needed: 

• 
In the Report name and Report description fields, type a new name and description 

for the report, respectively. 

• 
In the Report owner drop-down list, select a different user to be the owner of the 

report. If you change the report’s owner, then you will no longer be able to edit this 

memorized report after you save the changes. However, you can continue to run the 

report if it’s still public.  

• 
Select the Public check box to make the report available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to make the report private; that is, 

available only to yourself and system administrators. 

Others can see private memorized reports by selecting the Include private check box 
in their Memorized reports list. 

3. 
Modify the other settings as needed. 

4. 
Click Save.

##### Running a Memorized Report or Chart

Running a Memorized Report or Chart 

See the How to Get Here (on page 417) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

To run a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, find the report or chart you want to view, and then click the 

Run link.  

2. 
In the Select report type drop-down list, select a format for the report or chart output:  

• 
HTML: Saves the report as an HTML file so you can view it in your web browser. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report as a comma-separated value (CSV) file so you can import the 

data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Saves the report as an Excel file so you can manipulate the data further. 

• 
Text: Saves the report as a basic text file.  

Charts are only available in Printable and HTML format. 

3. 
Click OK to run the report. 

• 
If you selected Printable, HTML, or Text, then the report opens in a new window. 

• 
If you selected CSV or Excel, then the system saves the report in your local Downloads 

folder. 

You can also run a memorized report from the Reports center.

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here (on page 417) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 428) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 428) page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

---


<!-- Page 433 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

---


<!-- Page 434 -->

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save. 

Storing and Delivering the Report 

1.

• 
Email: Sends the report in an email.

Store in Reporting Portal: Stores the report in the selected owner portal(s). 

2.

Email

In the To field, type the email address to which you want to send the report.

your inbox. 

3. 
In the Subject field, type the subject of the email message. 

4. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Sends the report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Sends the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Sends the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Sends the report in an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Sends the report in a text file.

includes the report. 

Store Report 

1. 
In the Report description field, type a description of the report to help you remember its 

purpose and content and to distinguish it from other stored reports. The description 

appears in the My stored reports list in the Title column. 

2. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

•

Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file.

In the Send to drop-down list, select a cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the

##### Job Setup Summary Report Options
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 446*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Job Setup Summary Report Options 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Setup Summary`


To run the Job Setup Summary report: 

1. 
Click the Select report codes button to open the Select report codes box. 

• 
Use the report code drop-down lists to select the report codes you want to include in 

the report. 

• 
To include all values of a report code, choose the Select all check box. 

• 
To include multiple values of a report code, select the individual check boxes for the 

values you want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific value, type the report code value name in the Search field. 

• 
When you are done selecting report codes, click the Apply filters button. 

• 
To reset filter values, click the Clear filters button. 

2. 
Use the Job type drop-down list to select the job type of the jobs you want to view. 

3. 
Use the Location drop-down list to select the location of the jobs you want to view. 

4. 
Use the Job drop-down list to select the jobs to include in the report. 

• 
To include all jobs, choose the Select all check box. 

• 
To include multiple jobs, select the individual check boxes for the jobs you want to 

include. 

• 
To search for a specific job, type the job name in the Search field. 

If you do not select any jobs, all jobs of the selected type and location are included in the 
report. 

5. 
To view only inactive jobs in the report, select the Inactive jobs check box. 

Inactive jobs are jobs in the Pending, Complete (not closed), or Closed status. 

6. 
When finished, choose an action: 

• 
To view the report in your browser, click View.  

• 
To view the report in a printable format, click Print. 

• 
To memorize the report, click Memorize. 

• 
To view the report in an Excel spreadsheet, click Export, and then select Excel. 

---

Job Setup Summary Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Setup Summary > 
View/Print/Export`


The report header includes the report name and report codes selected for the report. 

Jobs are listed in alphabetic order by job type, location, and then job name. The columns shown 

from left to right on the page include: 

• 
Job type/Location: This is the job type associated with the job(s) and the location that the 

job is assigned to. The report groups all job locations of the same job type together. The 

location does not show for child jobs. 

• 
Project: This is the project that the job is assigned to. This shows only for child jobs. 

• 
Job name: This is the name of the job. 

• 
Description: This is the description of the job. 

• 
Ship to: This is the shipping contact for the job. 

• 
Dates: This column displays the job start date, estimated completion date, required 

completion date, and actual completion date, if these dates are entered on the Dates tab in 

the job record. 

• 
Report code: These are the report codes (Type, Status, Project owner, Budget year).  

• 
Report code value: These are the report code values associated with each job. 

• 
Tenant: This is the tenant assigned to the job. 

• 
Lease: This is the lease assigned to the job.

##### Job Cost Activity Report Options
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 450*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Job Cost Activity Report Options 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Cost Activity`


To run the Job Cost Activity report: 

1. 
In the Time period section, enter the Start date and End date for the range by which you 

want to filter the report. 

By default, the Start date is empty and the End date is the current date. If you do not enter 

a Start date, the system includes all available transactions associated with a job up to the 

specified End date. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

2. 
In the Filters section, click the Select report codes button to open the Select report codes 

box, and then select the report codes you want to include in the report. The fields in the 

Select report codes box are based on the Job reporting codes (on page 547) set up for 

your company. 

• 
To include all values of a report code, choose the Select all check box. 

• 
To include multiple values of a report code, select the individual check boxes for the 

values you want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific value, type the report code value name in the Search field. 

• 
To reset filter values, click the Clear filters button. 

3. 
After you select the report codes you want to filter the report by, click the Apply filters 

button. 

4. 
In the Job drop-down list, select the jobs to include in the report. 

• 
To include all jobs, choose the Select all check box (or don’t select anything). 

• 
To include multiple jobs, select the check box next to each job you want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific job, type the job name in the Search field. 

5. 
Optionally, select the Group by unit check box to group the report by job segments (units). 

If you have entered renovation dates and rent change amounts for a unit, then the following 

fields will appear next to the unit number in the report: 

• 
Projected start date: This is the estimated start date for the unit renovation. 

• 
Projected completion date: This is the estimated completion date for the unit 

renovation. 

• 
Actual start date: This is the date that the unit renovation began. 

• 
Actual completion date: This is the date that the unit renovation was completed. 

---


<!-- Page 451 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

• 
Rent before: This is the unit’s rent before the renovation. 

• 
Rent after: This is the unit’s rent after the renovation. 

• 
Rent change: This is the amount that the rent changed after the renovation. 

These fields are pulled from the Units tab in the job record. See Tracking Unit Rent Changes 
(on page 30 ) for more information. 

6. 
Optionally, select the Show cost code on every line check box to show the job and cost 

code on each line of the report. This improves reporting capabilities when the report is 

exported, such as using pivot tables in Excel to filter and aggregate data. 

7. 
Optionally, select the Select specific cost codes check box if you want to filter the report by 

one or more cost codes. This field appears only after you select a Job. 

• 
Select a Cost code option: 

• 
Include: Includes the selected cost codes in the report. 

• 
Exclude: Excludes the selected cost codes from the report.  

• 
Select one or more cost codes from the Cost code drop-down list. 

• 
To select all cost codes, select the Select all check box. 

• 
To select multiple cost codes, select the check box next to each cost code you 

want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific cost code, type the cost code in the Search field. 

If you don’t include any cost codes, then the report will show all cost codes by default. 

8. 
In the Columns to hide drop-down list, select any columns you want to exclude from the 

report. 

• 
To select all columns, select the Select all check box. 

• 
To select one or more columns, select individual check boxes. 

• 
To search for specific column, type the column name in the Search field. 

9. 
When finished, choose an action: 

• 
To view the report in your browser, click View.

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

•

Job Cost Activity Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Cost Activity > 
View/Print/Export`


The report header includes the report name, job name, time period, and the report codes selected 

for the report. 

The Job Cost Activity report shows only the cost codes that have activity for the selected job. The 

system sorts transactions first by cost code, from lowest to highest, and then by date, from oldest 

to newest. The columns shown from left to right on the page include: 

• 
Unit: This is the unit number. This column appears only if you selected the Group by unit 

check box. If you are tracking unit renovation dates and rent changes in the job record, then 

you will see additional fields next to the unit number. See Tracking Unit Rent Changes (on 

page 30) for more information. 

• 
Cost code: This is the cost code level. 

• 
Cost code description: This is the description of the cost code. 

• 
Post date: This is the day the activity posted on. 

• 
Vendor ID/G/L account: This depends on the transaction type: 

• 
If this is an A/P invoice, this is the ID of the vendor on the A/P invoice.  

• 
If this is a journal entry, this is the number of the G/L account. 

• 
Vendor name/G/L description: This depends on the transaction type: 

• 
If this is an A/P invoice, this is the name of the vendor on the A/P invoice.  

• 
If this is a journal entry, this is the description of the G/L account. 

• 
A/P invoice/JE no.: This depends on the transaction source: 

• 
If the transaction is an A/P invoice, then this is the number of the A/P invoice. Click the 

link to open the invoice.  

• 
If the transaction is a journal entry, then this is the number of the journal. Click the link 

to open the journal entry. 

• 
Description: This is the description entered on the line item for the transaction. 

• 
Amount invoiced: This is the amount of the line item for the transaction. Negative numbers 

show in parentheses. 

• 
Amount paid: This is the total amount paid for the transaction. 

• 
Remaining to pay: This is the remaining amount owed to the vendor. 

• 
Retention held: This is the amount held back until a job is completed. 

---
