RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Any columns that you selected in the Columns to hide drop-down list before running the report 
are excluded from the report. See Job Cost Activity Report Options (on page 440 ) for more 
information. 

The total rows shown in the report include: 

• 
A total row that summarizes activity for each cost code.  

• 
A total row that summarizes activity for each cost code heading. The number of total rows 

provided correspond to the cost code structure. For example: 

• 
If you are viewing activity for a job that only tracks to divisions and phases, you will 

see a total row for each phase and division that has activity.  

• 
If you are viewing activity for a job that only tracks to the segment level, you will see a 

total row for each segment, subphase, phase, and division that has activity.  

• 
A total row that summarizes all activity. 

Division total rows show highlighted blue, all other total rows show highlighted gray.

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Job Budget Report Options 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Budget`


To run the Job Budget report: 

1. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which to filter the report. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

2. 
In the Job drop-down list, select the job for which to view budget information. 

3. 
In the Level of detail drop-down list, select how many cost structure levels to show in the 

report: 

• 
All: The report includes all cost structure levels. 

• 
1: The budget collapses to the division level. 

• 
2: The budget collapses to the phase level. 

• 
3: The budget collapses to the subphase level. 

• 
4: The budget collapses to the custom segment 1 level. 

• 
5: The budget collapses to the custom segment 2 level. 

4. 
Optionally, select the Select specific cost codes check box if you want to filter the report by 

one or more cost codes. This field appears only after you select a Job. 

• 
Select a Cost code option: 

• 
Include: Includes the selected cost codes in the report. 

• 
Exclude: Excludes the selected cost codes from the report.  

• 
Select one or more cost codes from the Cost code drop-down list. 

• 
To select all cost codes, select the Select all check box. 

• 
To select multiple cost codes, select the check box next to each cost code you 

want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific cost code, type the cost code in the Search field. 

If you don’t include any cost codes, then the report will show all cost codes by 
default. 

5. 
Optionally, select the Show change order detail check box to display additional details 

about each change order in the report. Two additional columns will appear in the report: the 

Change order comment and the Effective date entered for the change order. 

6. 
Optionally, select the Include zero budgets check box to display items with zero budgets.

Job Budget Report Columns

The report header includes the report name, job name, and filter date. 

The columns shown from left to right on the page include: 

• 
Cost code: This is the job cost code. Rows that represent the top level of the cost code 

structure are highlighted in blue. If you enabled the Display unit budget and Group by unit 

options when customizing the report, then the cost codes in this column will be grouped by 

unit. 

• 
Description: This is the description of the cost code. 

• 
Unit: This is the building unit number.

• 
Change orders: These are the budget change orders requested for the activity. A separate 

row appears for each change order.

Change order comment: This is the comment entered for the change order, if any. This 

column appears only if you selected the Show change order detail check box when

• 
Effective date: This is the date on which the change order took effect. This column appears 

only if you selected the Show change order detail check box when customizing the report. 

• 
Budget changes: These are the approved budget change amounts. The system only 

includes change orders whose Effective date is on or before the As of date. 

• 
Revised budget: This is the amount of the original budget with the approved budget 

change. 

• 
Pending budget changes: This is the amount of budget change orders that are pending 

approval. The system only includes change orders whose Effective date is on or before the 

As of date. 

• 
Projected revised budget: This is the budget amount including the budget change orders 

that are pending approval. 

The total rows shown in the report include: 

• 
A total row that summarizes budget for each cost code.  

• 
A total row that summarizes all budgets.

##### Customizing and Running the Replacement Reserves Draw Detail Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 467*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Customizing and Running the Replacement Reserves Draw Detail Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Reports > Draw 
Detail (RR)`


To customize and run the Replacement Reserves Draw Detail report: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves 

application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Draw Detail (RR) menu option. If you’re using the 

standalone Replacement Reserves application, the menu option is labeled Draw Detail. 

The report configuration page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

In the Filters section, select one or more filter options: 

• 
Reserve name: Select the replacement reserve to generate the report for. This is a required 

field. 

• 
Include option: Select whether to include all transactions, only transactions included in a 

draw, or only transactions not yet included in a draw. 

• 
Funding source: Select one or more funding sources. 

• 
Draw number: Select one or more replacement reserve draw numbers. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.  

• 
Print: Exports the report to a printable PDF file. 

• 
Process & store: Allows you to process and store the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Add to dashboard: Adds the report to one of your custom dashboards. 

• 
Memorize: Memorizes the report and stores it in the Memorized reports list. 

• 
Export: Exports the report to a Word, CSV, Excel, or Text file. 

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can email the report to others. Use trial and error to get the precise 

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you 

want to refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 

process as needed.

Job Cost Status Report Options 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Cost Status`


To run the Job Cost Status report: 

1. 
Optionally, in the Start date and End date fields, select a date range for the report based on 

the job cost invoice date. Any purchase orders created after the end date will not be 

included in the report.  

By default, the End date is set to today ’s date. 

2. 
In the Job drop-down list, select the job for which to view cost codes. 

3. 
Use the Vendor name drop-down list if you want to filter the report by transactions related 

to a specific vendor.  

• 
If you want to include all jobs associated with that vendor in the report, then select the 

Include other jobs for this vendor check box. 

4. 
Use the Subcontract/purchase order drop-down list if you want to filter the report by a 

specific subcontract or purchase order. 

5. 
Optionally, select the Select specific cost codes check box if you want to filter the report by 

one or more cost codes. This field appears only after you select a Job. 

• 
Select a Cost code option: 

• 
Include: Includes the selected cost codes in the report. 

• 
Exclude: Excludes the selected cost codes from the report.  

• 
Select one or more cost codes from the Cost code drop-down list. 

• 
To select all cost codes, select the Select all check box. 

• 
To select multiple cost codes, select the check box next to each cost code you 

want to include. 

• 
To search for a specific cost code, type the cost code in the Search field. 

If you don’t include any cost codes, then the report will show all cost codes by default. 

6. 
Optionally, select the Show detail check box to include purchase order, subcontract, and 

invoice transaction activity on the report. This also displays additional total rows as 

described in Job Cost Status Report Columns (on page 462). 

7. 
Optionally, select the Sort by vendor check box to sort the information in the report by 

vendor instead of by cost code. If this option is selected, the Vendor column will appear in 

the report instead of the Cost code column. 

This option is not available if you selected to filter the report by a specific vendor.

transactions in the report. 

9. 
Optionally, if you selected the Show detail check box, you can select the Show cost code 

and vendor on every line check box to show the job, cost code, and vendor on each line of 

the report. This improves reporting capabilities when the report is exported, such as using 

pivot tables in Excel to filter and aggregate data. 

10. 
When you are finished, choose how you want to deliver the report:

To view the report in your browser, click View.

The Job Cost Status report shows only the cost codes that have activity for the selected job. The

to newest.

•

•

• 
Vendor: This is the name of vendor for the transaction.  

• 
This column appears only if you selected the Show detail or Sort by vendor check box. 

• 
Order number: This is the number of the commitment. Click this link to open the 

commitment.  

• 
This column is left blank for A/P invoices.

This column appears only if you selected the Show detail check box.

##### Job Status Summary Report Columns
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 478*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Job Status Summary Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Cost Summary > View, Print, 
or Export`


The Job Status Summary report can be grouped by either job or report code, depending on which 

Report option you select before running the report. The report sorts jobs and report codes 

alphabetically with running totals for each report codes group or a running total of all jobs.  

The report header includes the report name as well as any filters applied to the report. 

The columns shown from left to right on the page include: 

• 
Report code: This is the report code value. 

• 
Job name: This is the name of the job. 

• 
Description: This is the description of the job. 

• 
Original budget: This amount varies depending on the job status. If the job status is 
Pending or Active, then this is the current amount of the cost code budget. If the job status 
is Active (budget locked), Complete (not closed), or Closed, then this is the amount of the cost 
code budget when the job status changed to Active (budget locked). 

• 
Budget changes: This is the total amount of changes to the cost code budget from 
approved change orders. 

The system only includes change orders whose Effective date is on or before the As of date. 

• 
Revised budget: This is the original cost code budget plus approved budget changes. The 
calculation is: Original budget ± Budget changes. 

• 
Budget changes pending: This is the total amount of change orders awaiting approval for 
the cost code. 

The system only includes change orders whose Effective date is on or before the As of date. 

• 
Projected revised budget: This is the original cost code budget plus approved and pending 
budget changes. This calculation is: Original budget ± Budget changes ± Budget changes 
pending. 

• 
Commitments pending approval: This is the total amount of commitments awaiting 
approval for the cost code. 

• 
Approved commitments: This is the total amount of approved commitments for the cost 
code. 

• 
Open commitments: This is the total amount of open commitments for the cost code. 

If you entered a Prior commitments offset amount when adding a budget for a cost code, 
then the Prior commitments offset amount reduces the Open commitments amount for 
that cost code. 

• 
External commitments: This is the total amount of external commitments for the cost code. 
External commitments are commitments that come from external sources, such as 
OpsTechnology. 

---


<!-- Page 479 -->
Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

This column appears only if you do not enter a Start date for the report.  

• 
Cost to date: This is the total amount of costs entered for the cost code. 

• 
Remaining budget: This is the amount of budget remaining for the cost code. This 
calculation is Revised budget – Approved commitments – Costs. 

• 
Cost to complete: This is the amount of estimated costs remaining for the cost code. This 
calculation is Projected revised budget – Costs. 

If you have not entered a budget or your budget is less than the Cost to date, then the 
report will display a negative value in the Cost to complete column. However, you can select 
the Prevent negative cost to complete option when running the report to display “0.00 ” 
instead of the negative value. 

• 
Cost at completion: This amount varies depending on the job status. If the job is closed, 
then this is the total amount of costs entered for applicable cost codes in the division when 
the job was closed. If the job is still open, then this is the Cost to date amount. 

• 
Variance to revised budget: This is the difference between the revised budget amount and 
the final cost for the code. This calculation is Revised budget - Cost at completion. 

• 
Variance to original budget: This is the difference between the original budget amount and 
the final cost for the code. This calculation is Original budget - Cost at completion. 

• 
Percent complete: This is the cost code completion percentage, based on the costs entered 
for the cost code. This calculation is (Cost at completion ÷ Revised budget) × 100. 

• 
Paid to date: This is the total amount paid. 

• 
Remaining to pay: This is the remaining amount owed to the vendor. 

• 
Retention held: This is the amount held back until the job is completed. 

• 
Begin date: This is the date that the job began. 

• 
Completion estimated: This is the date on which the job is estimated to be completed. 

• 
Completion required: This is the date by which the job must be completed. 

• 
Completion actual: This is the date on which the job was completed. If a job is still in 
progress, this column will be blank. 

Any columns that you selected in the Columns to hide drop-down list before running the report 
are excluded from the report. See Job Status Summary Report Options (on page 466 ) for more 
information. 

The Total rows in the summary report depend on the Report option setting: 

• 
If you grouped the report by job, then a Total all jobs row appears at the bottom of the 

report with totals for each column. 

• 
If you grouped the report by report code, then a separate Total row appears for each report 

code group with totals for each column. The totals only apply to jobs that are associated 

with the report code.

##### Job Cost Status by Month Report Options
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 483*

Chapter 2: Using Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Job Cost Status by Month Report Options 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Status with Projected Budget 
by Month`


To run the Job Cost Status by Month report: 

1. 
In the Actual activity start date and Actual activity end date fields, type or select a date 

range of job activity to cover in the report. 

The start date is optional but the end date is required. If you specify a start date, then the 

report displays only the cost expensed for each cost code within the date range. If you do 

not specify a start date, then the report displays the total cost expensed for each cost code 

through the end date. Adjust the start date to narrow or broaden the scope of the report. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

2. 
Optionally, in the Budget projection end date field, type or select the date through which 

to display projected budget amounts. This date determines how many of the remaining 

monthly budget periods to include in the report.  

For example, if you are running the report on July 31st to view the remaining projected 

budget for a job that ends on December 31st, then by default the report includes projected 

monthly budget amounts for August through December. However, if you set the Budget 

projection end date to October 31st, then the report will display only the projected budgets 

for August, September, and October. 

3. 
In the Job drop-down list, select the job for which you are running the report. 

4. 
By default, the report displays monthly actuals through the end of report date range. 

However, if you want to summarize all actual costs in one column, then you can select the 

Summarize actual cost check box. 

5. 
When finished, choose an action: 

• 
To view the report in your browser, click View.  

• 
To view the report in a printable format, click Print. 

• 
To memorize the report, click Memorize. 

• 
To view the report in an Excel spreadsheet, click Export, and then select Excel.

Job Cost Status by Month Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Job Status with Projected Budget

The Job Cost Status by Month report includes the following columns: 

• 
Cost code: This is the cost code level. 

• 
(Monthly actuals): This is the actual cost expensed for each cost code for all months 

through the Actual activity end date you specified in the report options. If you also 

specified an Actual activity start date, then only the months from the start date to the end 

date will appear in the report. 

• 
(Actual thru end date): This is the total cost for each cost code as of the Actual activity end 

date you specified in the report options. If you also specified an Actual activity start date, 

then this column will display only the cost that has accumulated since the start date. 

• 
(Projected monthly budgets): These are the projected budgets for each cost code for all 

remaining months until the job is completed. If you specified a Budget projection end date, 

then the report displays only the months remaining until that date. 

• 
Remaining budget: This is the total remaining budget for each cost code. 

• 
Total budget: This is the total budget for each cost code. 

• 
Total cost: This is the total actual cost associated with each cost code.  

• 
Variance: This is the budget variance of each cost code, i.e., the difference between the 

Total budget and the Total cost.

##### Customizing and Running the Retainage Register Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 492*

Using Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Customizing and Running the Retainage Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Reports > Retainage Register`


To customize and run the Retainage Register report: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Retainage register option. 

The report configuration page opens. 

Defining the Report Period 

In the Time period section, type or select the date from which to run the report in the As of date 

field. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 
Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. 

Filtering the Report 

In the Filters section, select one or more filter options: 

• 
Property: Select one or more properties to run the report for. This is a required field. 

• 
Job: Select one or more jobs to run the report for. 

• 
From vendor / To vendor: Select a range of vendor IDs to run the report for those vendors. 

Labeling the Report 

In the Titles section, define the report title, subtitle, and footer text: 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type a title for the report. The system assigns a report name by 

default, but you can customize it as needed. The report title displays in large typeface at the 

top of the page directly beneath your company’s name.  

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, type the text that you want to appear below the title of the report. 

This subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In the Footer text field, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get 
the PDF version). You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each field. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.  

• 
Print: Exports the report to a printable PDF file.

##### Configuring Job Cost
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 498*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide

Configuring Job Cost 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Applications > Configure (Job Cost)`


To configure job cost settings: 

1. 
In the Journal ID for cost code reclass drop-down list, select which journal to use for 

reclassified cost codes. 

As a best practice, set up a unique journal for this purpose. 

2. 
Optionally, you can prevent accrual journal entries from being included in replacement 

reserve draws. In the Journal ID for omitting accrual entries from replacement reserve 

draws drop-down list, select the accrual journal whose activity you want to omit from 

replacement reserve draws. No journal entries from that journal will be available to be 

included in a replacement reserve draw.  

3. 
In the A/P account for job cost items drop-down list, select the A/P account for job cost 

transactions.  

This field appears only if you flagged a G/L A/P account as an alternate. To do this, edit the 
G/L account, and then use the G/L account alternative drop-down list to assign this as a 
“Payables account.” 

4. 
Optionally, you can include user-defined books when calculating the escrow balance for 

replacement reserves. To do this, select one or more user-defined books from the 

User-defined books to include when calculating escrow balances drop-down list. The 

journals for these books will be included when calculating the Escrow balance on the Draw 

information page (on page 65). 

The escrow balance calculation exactly matches the Closing balance that appears in the 

Trial Balance report for the G/L account or account group defined as the Escrow 

account/account group in the replacement reserve’s funding source (on page 599). 

5. 
If you are licensed to integrate with Procore, then select the Procore integration check box 

to configure the integration details and synchronize the data between the RealPage 

---


<!-- Page 499 -->
Chapter 3: Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Financial Suite and Procore systems. See Integrating Job Cost with Procore (on page 489) for 

more information.  

6. 
If you want to post draws into the A/R system, use the Loans payable account (credit) 

drop-down list to select the G/L account to use when generating the A/R invoice. 

7. 
If you configured multiple A/R accounts and want to use an account other than the default 

A/R account, use the A/R override account (debit) drop-down list to select the account. 

8. 
In the Cash account drop-down list, select the G/L account you want to use when posting 

draw receipts. 

9. 
In the Journal for draw drop-down list, select the journal you want to use when a draw is 

posted and the system needs to create an entry in the General Ledger. 

As a best practice, define one journal for posted draws in the journal ID. 

10. 
Select the Allow on hold invoices to be included on a draw check box to allow users to 

include invoices on a draw even if they have been placed on hold. 

11. 
In the Job Cost retention account drop-down list, select the G/L account you want to use 

when generating invoices from purchase orders and subcontracts. 

12. 
When you complete your changes, click Save.

##### Integrating Job Cost with Procore
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 500*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Integrating Job Cost with Procore 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Configuration > Procore Integration`


If your company is licensed to integrate with Procore’s construction management software, then 

you can sync job data between RealPage Financial Suite and Procore. This integration benefits a 

couple types of users:  

• 
Companies who are already subscribed to Job Cost in RealPage Financial Suite but want to 

export and sync their jobs to Procore. 

• 
Companies who are using Procore but want to import and sync their jobs to RealPage 

Financial Suite. 

After you import or export jobs, any changes you make to the job record are automatically 

pushed out to Procore (and vice versa). In addition, any payments made to invoices that 

originated in Procore are automatically pushed out to Procore. 

If a job is synced to Procore, then any A/P invoices entered in RealPage Financial Suite with job 
cost line items for that job will automatically generate Direct Cost invoice entries in Procore. 
Likewise, any G/L journal entries entered in RealPage Financial Suite will generate Direct Cost 
expense entries in Procore. 

Importing Jobs from Procore 

To import jobs from Procore into RealPage Financial Suite: 

1. 
In the Job Cost & Reserves menu, click the Setup tab, and then select Configuration. 

2. 
The Configure Job Cost & Reserves page opens. 

3. 
In the Job Cost configuration information section, select the Procore integration check box. 

4. 
In the Procore company ID field, type your company ID number in Procore.  

5. 
In the Procore cost structure drop-down list, select the cost code structure that you defined 

in RealPage Financial Suite for the jobs you want to synchronize between the two systems.  

In RealPage Financial Suite, the cost code structure determines the number of levels and 
maximum number of characters for each cost code associated with a job type. You must 
create a cost code structure (on page 516 ) that matches the one in Procore to be able to 
sync jobs. 

6. 
In the Default work-in-process account drop-down list, select the default WIP account to 

assign to each cost code. The system charges this account when a job cost transaction is 

entered using one of these cost codes.    

7. 
In the Procore URL drop-down list, select a sandbox or production URL. 

Procore has two production servers, app.procore.com and us02.procore.com; the 

sandboxes for these servers are api-sandbox-monthly.procore.com and 

---


<!-- Page 501 -->
Chapter 3: Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

sandbox-monthly-us02.procore.com, respectively. The sandbox.procore.com URL is strictly 

for development purposes. 

8. 
Click the Select Procore projects to import button. 

A list of Procore projects appears. 

9. 
Select the projects you want to import, and then click the Import selected Procore projects 

button. 

The system adds the import to an offline queue for processing. You will receive a 

confirmation email when the import is complete, and the imported jobs will appear in the 

Jobs list (on page 17). If the import fails, a log entry appears in the External queue 

exceptions (on page 163) log with a description of the error. 

10. 
When you first import jobs from Procore, there’s no way for RealPage Financial Suite to 

know which property or entity to assign to each job record. Instead, you’ll need to manually 

edit each imported job to assign the appropriate property or entity, and then re-import the 

jobs to sync the data back to Procore. 

• 
In the Job Cost & Reserves menu, click the All tab, and then select Jobs. 

• 
Click Edit next to the job record. 

• 
On the Job information tab, select a property or entity from the Property drop-down 

list to associate with the job. 

• 
Click Save. 

• 
Repeat the steps for each job you imported from Procore. 

11. 
Return to the Configure Job Cost & Reserves page to import the jobs a second time. 

• 
In the Job Cost & Reserves menu, click the Setup tab, and then select Configuration. 

• 
Make sure that all of the jobs you initially imported from Procore are selected, and 

then click the Import selected Procore projects button to import the jobs again and 

re-sync the job information. 

Exporting Jobs to Procore 

To export jobs from RealPage Financial Suite to Procore: 

1. 
In the Job Cost & Reserves menu, click the Setup tab, and then select Configuration. 

2. 
The Configure Job Cost & Reserves page opens. 

3. 
In the Job Cost configuration information section, select the Procore integration check box. 

4. 
In the Procore company ID field, type your company ID number in Procore.  

5. 
In the Procore cost structure drop-down list, select the cost code structure that you defined 

in RealPage Financial Suite for the jobs you want to synchronize between the two systems.  

---

In RealPage Financial Suite, the cost code structure determines the number of levels and 
maximum number of characters for each cost code associated with a job type. You must 
create a cost code structure (on page 516 ) that matches the one in Procore to be able to 
sync jobs. 

6. 
In the Default work-in-process account drop-down list, select the default WIP account to 

assign to each cost code. The system charges this account when a job cost transaction is 

entered using one of these cost codes.    

7. 
In the Procore URL drop-down list, select a sandbox or production URL. 

Procore has two production servers, app.procore.com and us02.procore.com; the 

sandboxes for these servers are api-sandbox-monthly.procore.com and 

sandbox-monthly-us02.procore.com, respectively. The sandbox.procore.com URL is strictly 

for development purposes. 

8. 
Click Save to save the configuration and establish the API connection.  

9. 
Flag the job records that you want to include in the export: 

• 
In the Job Cost & Reserves menu, click the All tab, and then select Jobs. 

• 
Click Edit next to the job record. 

• 
On the Job information tab, select the Include this job when syncing to Procore 

check box. 

• 
Click Save. 

• 
Repeat the steps for each job you want to export. 

10. 
Return to the Configure Job Cost & Reserves page. 

11. 
Click the Export jobs to Procore button. 

The system adds the export to an offline queue for processing. You will receive a 

confirmation email when the export is complete. Going forward, any changes you make to 

these job records will automatically sync to Procore (and vice versa). 

Syncing Vendors with Procore 

After you configure the Procore integration in Job Cost, an additional field appears in each vendor 

record in RealPage Financial Suite to sync the vendor information with Procore. 

To sync a vendor record: 

1. 
In the Accounts Payable menu, click the All or Setup tab, and then select Vendors. 

The Vendors list opens. 

2. 
Click Edit next to the vendor record you want to sync. 

The Vendor information page opens. 

3. 
In the Vendor section of the Vendor tab, select the Sync to external system check box.

##### Defining Job Segments for a Job
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 514*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Defining Job Segments for a Job 

In order to define job segments (units) for a job and use them for budgeting and reporting 

purposes, the following conditions must be met: 

• 
Job segments must be enabled in the job type. 

• 
Cost codes must be marked as a segment code. 

• 
Units must be assigned to the job location. 

After you add units to the job, they will appear in the Job segments list. See Editing a Job (on 

page 22) for instructions on adding units to a job. 

We recommend that you set up the job, add or import the job budget, and then add units to the 
job, in that order. When you add units to a job with an existing budget, the system automatically 
creates budgets per cost code per unit in the Job segment budgets list. This way, you don’t have 
to manually add job segment budgets. 

Enabling Segments in the Job Type 

To enable segments in the job type: 

1. 
In the Job Cost & Reserves menu, select the Setup tab, and then click the Job types menu 

option. 

The Job types list opens. 

2. 
Find the desired job type, and then click the Edit link. 

The Job type information page opens. 

3. 
If the job type uses segments to track budgets and costs, select the Segments enabled 

check box. If you select this check box, complete the additional fields. 

• 
Use the Segment type drop-down list to select the segment type of the job type. 

• 
If you budget the job type to the segment level, select the Budget by segment type? 

check box.  

4. 
When your changes are complete, click Save. 

---


<!-- Page 515 -->
Chapter 3: Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

The system saves the job type and opens the (Job type) – Cost codes page. For more 

information, see Cost Codes (on page 528). 

Setting Cost Codes as Segment Codes 

Cost codes must be marked as segment codes when adding or importing them. The Segment 

code check box appears only if segments are enabled in the job type. See Adding a Cost Code (on 

page 530) for instructions. 

Assigning Units to the Job Location 

Before you can add units to a job, the units must be assigned to the property associated with the 

job. This is done via the Units list in the Company application. See Adding Units for instructions. 

---


<!-- Page 516 -->
Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

After you create units for the job location, you can edit the job record and add units to the job via 

the Units tab. 

When you save the job, the units will appear in the Job segments list and any budgets that you 

already created for the job will instead be divided into segment-level budgets by cost code in the 

Job segment budgets list.

This section lists one row per division that has at least one segment-level budget for the unit. 

Each row totals all budgets and costs for all cost codes in that division. 

This tab appears only when viewing a job segment. 

(Order) 
This is the order number of the cost code. The system sorts cost codes 

alphanumerically by division, from the lowest division number to the highest

<!-- Page 520 -->
Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Budget 
This is the total budget for applicable cost codes in the division. This amount 

varies depending on the job status: 

• 
If the job status is Pending or Active, then this is the current amount 

of the cost code budget. 

• 
If the job status is Active (budget locked), Complete (not closed), or 

Closed, then this is the amount of the cost code budget when the 

job status changed to Active (budget locked). 

Budget change 

orders 

This is the total amount of approved budget change orders for applicable 

cost codes in the division. 

Revised budget 
This is the original cost code budget plus approved budget changes for 

applicable cost codes in the division. This calculation is: 

Original budget ± Budget changes  

Cost to date 
This is the total amount of costs entered for applicable cost codes in the 

division. 

Remaining 

budget 

This is the amount of budget remaining for applicable cost codes in the 

division. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Costs 

Cost to complete This is the amount of estimated costs remaining for applicable cost codes in 

the division. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Costs 

Cost at 

completion 

This amount varies depending on the job status: 

• 
If the job is closed, this is the total amount of costs entered for 

applicable cost codes in the division when the job was closed. 

• 
If the job is still open, this is the Cost to date amount. 

Variance 
This is the difference between the budgeted amount and the final cost for 

applicable cost codes in the division. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Cost at completion 

Percent complete This is the cost code completion percentage, based on the costs entered for 

the cost code. This calculation is: 

(Cost at completion ÷ Revised budget) × 100 

Total 
This row is the total of all columns, except (Order), Division, and 

Description.

This is the total amount of costs entered for applicable cost codes in the 

phase. 

Remaining 

budget 

This is the amount of budget remaining for applicable cost codes in the 

phase. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Costs 

Cost to complete This is the amount of estimated costs remaining for applicable cost codes in 

the phase. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Costs 

Cost at 

completion 

This amount varies depending on the job status: 

• 
If the job is closed, this is the total amount of costs entered for 

applicable cost codes in the phase when the job was closed. 

• 
If the job is still open, this is the Cost to date amount. 

Variance 
This is the difference between the budgeted amount and the final cost for 

applicable cost codes in the phase. This calculation is: 

Revised budget – Cost at completion 

Percent complete This is the cost code completion percentage, based on the costs entered for 

the cost code. This calculation is: 

(Cost at completion ÷ Revised budget) × 100

##### Adding, Duplicating, or Editing a Cost Structure
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 526*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding, Duplicating, or Editing a Cost Structure 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > 
 Cost Structure Definition`


To add, duplicate, or edit a cost structure: 

• 
To add a cost structure, click Add. 

• 
To duplicate a cost structure, locate the cost structure you want to duplicate, click the 

View link, and then click Duplicate. 

When you duplicate a cost structure, the system pre -fills all fields to match the 
original cost structure, except for Cost structure name. 

• 
To edit a cost structure, locate the cost structure you want to edit, and then click the 

Edit link. 

You can only edit cost structures that are not assigned to any job types. 

1. 
In the Cost structure name field, enter the cost structure name. 

As a best practice, enter a name that reflects the number of levels included in the cost 

structure. For example, if a cost structure includes divisions, phases, and subphases, enter 

“Div-Phase-Subphase.” 

This field is read-only when editing a cost structure. 

2. 
Use the Cost structure level drop-down list to select the number of levels included in the 

cost structure. 

The Cost structure levels section shows a row for each level included in the cost structure. 

3. 
In the Name field, accept or update the cost structure level name. 

By default, the system assigns Division to the first level, Phase to the second level, and 

Subphase to the third level. You can change these names as needed. The system supports 

up to two additional custom cost levels. 

When viewing the Job Status Inquiry (on page 166) page, the job name shows as level one, 

the division shows as level two, the phase shows as level three, the subphase shows as level 

four, and the remaining two custom levels show as level five and level six, respectively. 

4. 
Use the Type drop-down list to select how each level is named. 

• 
Numeric: The level name can include only numbers, such as “100.” 

• 
Text: The level name can include letters and numbers, such as “A101.” 

5. 
In the Limit field, enter the maximum number of characters used to define a level, up to 

eight. 

For example, if you had a division named “1000,” you would set the limit to “4.” 

---

This field does not apply to levels of the “Text” Type. 

6. 
For each level in the cost structure, repeat steps 4-5. 

7. 
When your changes are complete: 

• 
Click Save to save the cost structure and close the Cost structure information page. 

• 
Alternatively, click More actions, and then click Save and new to save the cost 

structure and open a new Cost structure information page. 

The system saves the cost structure and adds it to the Cost structures list. 

Viewing a Cost Structure 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Cost Structure Definition > View`


To view a cost structure: 

1. 
In the Cost structures list, locate the cost structure you want to view. 

2. 
Click the View link to the left of the cost structure. 

The system opens the Cost structure information page. 

Deleting a Cost Structure 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Cost Structure Definition > Delete`


You can only delete cost structures that are not used by any job type. 

To delete a cost structure: 

1. 
In the Cost structures list, locate the cost structure you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete link to the right of the cost structure. 

3. 
Click OK in the confirmation box. 

The system removes the cost structure from the Cost structures list.

Cost Structure Information Page 

Use the Cost structure information page to manage cost structures. From this page, you can: 

• 
View cost structures. 

• 
Add cost structures. 

• 
Duplicate cost structures. 

• 
Edit cost structures. 

When you create cost structures, you decide the number of levels in the cost structure. Each cost 

structure level should match a level in the work breakdown structure of the overall job. For each 

level, you enter the name, type (numeric or text), and character limit. 

As a best practice, name each cost structure based on the included structure levels. For example, 

assume you need three cost structures for divisions, phases, and subphases. The names you can 

assign to each cost code structure include: 

• 
Div: This cost structure has only one level, for divisions.  

• 
Div-Phase: This cost structure has two levels, for divisions and phases. 

• 
Div-Phase-Subphase: This cost structure has three levels, for divisions, phases, and 

subphases. 

What’s Next? 

Set up job types. For more information, see Job Types (on page 522).

Job Types 

This section shows you how to add job types, which provide the cost codes for all jobs that use 

that job type. Job types inherit cost code structure from the cost structure definition assigned to 

the job type.

#### Job Types List

Job Types List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Job Types`


Use the Job types list to set up job types. Job types provide the account numbers you can use for 

journal entries or job invoices and control the billing, segment, and cost code settings of jobs.  

From this list, you can: 

• 
View job types. 

• 
Add job types. 

• 
Delete job types. 

• 
Edit job types. 

• 
Export job types. 

• 
Manage cost codes for a job type. 

A single job type can apply to multiple jobs, but you may require multiple job types to 

accommodate different construction scenarios. For example, a new construction job typically has 

different cost code requirements than a unit renovation. 

Typical job types include: 

• 
Tenant improvement 

• 
Unit renovation 

• 
New development 

• 
Repairs and maintenance 

• 
Capital cost 

• 
Building rehabilitation

Cost Codes List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost > Setup > Configuration – Job Types > Cost Codes`


Use the Cost codes page to manage and view cost codes. Cost codes, also known as the Work 

Breakdown Structure (WBS) or coding block or job cost chart detail, track a job’s budget, costs, 

and progress at a detailed level. From this page, you can: 

• 
View cost codes. 

• 
Add cost codes. 

• 
Delete cost codes. 

• 
Edit cost codes. 

• 
Export cost codes. 

• 
Import cost codes. 

Cost codes use the same levels as the cost structure assigned to the job type. For example, if the 

assigned cost structure includes divisions, phases, and subphases, you can assign cost codes 

down to the subphase level. 

During cost code setup, you assign an appropriate G/L account to each non-header cost code. 

This indicates which control account updates when a cost is assigned to the cost code. 

A single job can use only one job type and cost code structure.

of levels used.

• 
You must set up the G/L account(s) that you will assign to cost codes.

Adding a Cost Code 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Job Types > Cost Codes > Add`


You can add cost code details manually or import a group of cost codes (on page 532) from a 

CSV template. 

The cost structure assigned to a job determines the types of cost codes you can enter, including 
the number of levels and characters in the code. As a best practice, you should capitalize the 
name of any header-level cost codes and enter “0” for all levels after Division. This creates a 
cleaner view on reports such as the Job status inquiry. 

To manually add a cost code detail: 

1. 
In the Job types list, select the Cost codes link next to the job type for which you are 

entering cost codes. 

The Cost codes list opens. 

2. 
Click the Add button to open the Cost code information page. 

3. 
When you are adding a new cost code, the Name is initially unassigned. The system will 

automatically update the name after you save the cost code details. The name is the job 

---


<!-- Page 541 -->
Chapter 3: Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

type plus any levels, separated by hyphens. For example, a cost code with “Renovation” as 

the job type, “30” as the division, and “2” as the phase would be named “Renovation-30-2”. 

4. 
Verify that the Job type is correct. You can click the link to view the job type’s details. 

5. 
In the Cost code description field, type a description for the cost code. Remember to 

capitalize any header-level cost codes. 

6. 
In the Division field, type the division, or level 1, of the cost code. 

7. 
In the Phase field, type the phase, or level 2, of the cost code. 

8. 
In the Sub-phase field, type the subphase, or level 3, of the cost code. 

9. 
In the Segment 1 field, type the first segment, or level 4, of the cost code. 

10. 
In the Segment 2 field, type the second segment, or level 5, of the cost code. 

For the Phase, Sub-phase, Segment 1, and Segment 2 fields, keep in mind to: 

• 
Complete these fields only when the job type’s cost structure includes that level. 

Otherwise, leave the unused levels blank. 

• 
Enter “0” in these fields when creating a heading cost code. 

For example, assume your cost codes have three levels. To enter a division heading, 

both Phase and Sub-phase should be “0.” To enter a phase heading, only Sub-phase 

should be “0.” 

• 
Not enter any leading zeros. The system automatically applies leading zeros based on 

the level limit in the job type’s cost structure. 

For example, if Phase has a Limit of “3” in the cost structure and you enter 20, the 

system will automatically format that portion of the cost code as “020”. 

11. 
If you need to track the cost code budget at the segment or unit level, then select the 

Segment code check box. 

12. 
In the WIP account drop-down list, select the G/L account into which the system 

summarizes the costs for this cost code on the G/L. If your company set up a default 

Balance sheet A/R account (debit) account for Job Cost, then that selection shows here; 

you can change it as needed. 

Do not assign WIP accounts to header-level cost codes. 

13. 
In the Close account drop-down list, select the G/L account the system uses when closing 

this cost code before closing the entire job. If your company set up a default Revenue 

account (credit) account for Job Cost, then that selection shows here; you can change it as 

needed.

Viewing or Editing a Cost Code 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Job Types > Cost Codes > View or Edit`


To view or edit a cost code: 

1. 
In the Cost codes list, click the View or Edit link next to the cost code. 

The Cost code information page opens. 

2. 
View or edit the cost code details, and then click Done or Save. 

Importing Cost Codes 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Job Types > Cost Codes`


There are two methods for importing cost codes: 

• 
Download and fill in a blank CSV template. 

• 
Export the existing list of cost codes and then re-import it with your changes. 

The cost structure assigned to a job determines the types of cost codes you can enter, including 

the number of levels and characters in the code. As a best practice, you should capitalize the 

name of any header-level cost codes and enter “0” for all levels after Division. This creates a 

cleaner view on reports such as the Job status inquiry. 

To import cost codes: 

1. 
In the Cost codes list, click the Template button to download a blank CSV template.  

If you are updating an existing list of cost codes, then you can Export the current list to a 
CSV file and re-import the file with your changes. When importing, you can add or edit cost 
codes, but you can’t delete them. 

2. 
Open the downloaded file. 

3. 
For each cost code you want to add, enter the required information: 

• 
JOBTYPE: Enter the name of the job type to which you are adding the cost codes. 

Include any spaces. 

• 
DIVISION: Enter the division name or number. 

• 
PHASE: Enter the phase name or number. 

• 
SUBPHASE: Enter the subphase name or number. 

---


<!-- Page 543 -->
Chapter 3: Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

• 
CUSTSEGMENT1: Enter the custom phase (level 4) name or number. 

• 
CUSTSEGMENT2: Enter the custom phase (level 5) name or number. 

• 
COSTCODEDESCRIPTION: Enter a description of the cost code. 

As a best practice, enter any heading cost codes, such as land, in all capital letters. 

• 
WIPACCNO: Enter the account number of the G/L account you want to use as the WIP 

account. This must match the account number exactly. 

For example, to use the “1555.000--Construction in Process” account, you must enter 

1555.000 with all decimal points included. 

• 
CLOSEACCNO: Enter the account number of the G/L account you want to use as the 

close account. This must match the account number exactly. 

• 
In most cases, this should be blank. You can input an account here, typically a 

fixed asset account, if you need to close a single cost code earlier than you need 

to close the job. Contact your implementation consultant for more information. 

• 
For example, to use the “1555.000--Construction in Process” account, you must 

enter 1555.000 with all decimal points included. 

• 
SEGMENTCODE: If you need to budget the cost code to a segment or unit level, enter 

TRUE. 

If the cost code is not tracked or budgeted to a segment level, leave this column 

blank. 

For the PHASE, SUBPHASE, CUSTSEGMENT1, and CUSTSEGMENT2 fields, keep in mind to: 

• 
Complete these fields only when the job type’s cost structure includes that level. 

Otherwise, leave the unused levels blank. 

• 
Enter “0” in these fields when creating a heading cost code. 

For example, assume your cost codes have three levels. To enter a division heading, 

both Phase and Sub-phase should be “0.” To enter a phase heading, only Sub-phase 

should be “0.” 

• 
Not enter any leading zeros. The system automatically applies leading zeros based on 

the level limit in the job type’s cost structure. 

For example, if Phase has a Limit of “3” in the cost structure and you enter 20, the 

system will automatically format that portion of the cost code as “020”. 

---

4. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as. 

5. 
In the Save as box, use the Save as type drop-down list to select CSV (comma delimited) 

(*.csv). 

6. 
Change the File name or location as needed, and then click Save. 

7. 
On the Cost codes page, click Import. The system opens the Import cost code information 

box. 

8. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

9. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

10. 
Click Done.

Continue adding or removing rows as needed:

Click the 
 Add button to add another row. 

• 
Click the 
 Delete button to delete a row. 

3. 
Click Save. 

Importing Reserve Accounts 

To import accounts in bulk: 

1. 
Click the Download schedule template link. 

A CSV file is exported to your local Downloads folder with a list of existing reserve accounts. 

2. 
Add additional account numbers to the Reserve account column. 

3. 
Save the CSV file. 

4. 
In the Import account schedule (CSV) field, click the Choose file button. 

5. 
Upload the CSV file back into the system. 

The reserve accounts are added to the list. 

6. 
Click Save.

Job Reporting Codes List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Job Reporting Codes`


Use the Job reporting codes list to view and manage attributes of a job for the purpose of 

selecting and reporting based on job-identifying criteria. From this page, you can: 

• 
View reporting codes. 

• 
Add reporting codes. 

• 
Edit reporting codes. 

• 
Delete reporting codes. 

• 
Export reporting codes. 

You can assign reporting codes to a job to serve as additional filters when running Job Cost 

reports. Use reporting codes to sort and select jobs by the attributes assigned to them. For 

example, you can sort by “Regional manager” or “State” to pull reports based on all jobs that are 

managed by a specific manager in a specific state.  

For more information on assigning job reporting codes to a job, see Adding a Job (on page 18) or 

Editing a Job (on page 22). The reports that allow filtering by report codes include: 

• 
Job Cost Activity (on page 439) 

• 
Job Setup Summary (on page 435) 

• 
Job Status Summary (on page 465) 

• 
Job Status Inquiry (on page 166)

Draw Models 

This section shows you how to: 

• 
Manage job cost draw models, which organize cost codes into draw model details or lender 

categories. These are typically budget categories provided by your funding sources. 

• 
Manage replacement reserve draw models, which organize reserve accounts into draw 

model details or lender categories.

#### Draw Models List - Job Cost
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 564*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Draw Models List - Job Cost 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Draw Models > Job Cost`


Use the Draw models list for job costs to manage and view draw models, which represent the 

agreed-upon lender categories used to request funds from a lender. Draw models allow you to 

map cost codes to draw model details or lender categories. You can associate a single draw 

model with any number of lenders. You can set up a standard draw model for your lenders to 

adopt. However, the lenders may require you to use their provided categories, resulting in several 

unique models. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
View draw models. 

• 
Add draw models. 

• 
Delete draw models. 

• 
Edit draw models. 

• 
Export draw models. 

• 
Manage draw model details for a draw model. 

From a setup perspective, the workflow steps include: 

1. 
Create a job type cost code structure. 

2. 
Create a draw model or lender structure (lender categories). 

3. 
Map your structure to the lender categories. 

4. 
Add your lender as a customer to RealPage. 

5. 
Assign the mapped structure to any or all lenders (funding sources) who will accept this 

structure when requesting funds. 

6. 
Assign the funding source to a job.

Deleting or Inactivating a Job Cost Draw Model 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Draw Models > Job Cost > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Draw Models > Job Cost > Edit`


You can delete or inactivate a job cost draw model, depending on whether you want to retain its 

settings. 

Deleting a Draw Model 

If you no longer use a draw model, then you can delete it permanently. After you delete the draw 

model, it can’t be restored. If you’re unsure whether you want to delete it, you can set its status to 

Inactive instead. 

You can’t delete draw models that have one or more draw model details; you’ll have to delete the 
draw model details (on page 565 ) first. 

To delete a draw model: 

1. 
In the Draw models list, find the draw model you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete link next to the draw model. 

3. 
Click OK in the confirmation box. 

The system removes the draw model from the Draw models list. 

Inactivating a Draw Model 

Inactivating a draw model retains the settings and draw model details you’ve defined but hides 

the draw model from the Draw models list. You can reactivate the draw model at any time. 

To inactivate a draw model: 

1. 
In the Draw models list, find the draw model you want to inactivate. 

2. 
Click the Edit link next to the draw model. 

The Draw model page opens.

##### Adding Job Cost Draw Model Details - Job Cost
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 572*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Draw 

Adding Job Cost Draw Model Details - Job Cost 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Draw Models > Job Cost > Draw Model 
Details > Add`


Use this process to add, duplicate, or edit draw model details one at a time. To add a group of 

draw model details, see Importing Draw Model Details - Job Cost (on page 563). 

1. 
Verify the Draw model name. This identifies which draw model the new line belongs to and 

determines where the line appears when the draw is generated. 

2. 
In the Description field, type a description for the line detail. This label appears on the draw 

for this line (for example, a section name, cost category, or total description). 

3. 
In the Sequence field, type the sequence number of the line detail. This controls the order in 
which lines appear on the draw. Lower numbers display first. 

4. 
In the Total level drop-down list, select a level number (0–5). This determines the 
indentation and grouping of the line. Lines with the same level appear on the same tier and 
are grouped together on the draw. 

5. 
In the Record type drop-down list, define how the line should behave on the draw:  

• 
Title: Displays a header used to organize related lines. This type of line does not carry 
amounts. 

• 
Detail: Represents cost activity. Amounts associated with the line are included based 
on assigned cost codes or mapped reserve accounts. 

• 
Total: Calculates the sum of related detail lines within a section. 

Cost codes and reserve accounts can only be assigned to Detail lines. Title and Total lines 
are used for structure and calculations only. 

6. 
Click Save.

the drawmodeldetail.xls file, depending on your browser’s settings.

• 
For detail-level draw model details, leave the field blank. 

• 
For title-level draw model details, type “title”. 

• 
For total-level draw model details, type “total”. 

• 
Total Level: Type the level number (0–5) of the draw model detail. 

• 
Sequence: Type the sequence number of the draw model detail.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Draw Models

 Replacement Reserves`


Create a draw model to define how replacement reserve expenses are organized when requesting 

funds from a lender. A draw model acts as the framework for grouping costs into lender-required 

categories. After creating the model, you can add and configure draw model details to define 

specific sections and totals. 

To add a replacement reserve draw model: 

1. 
In the Draw model name field, assign a descriptive name to your draw model. 

2. 
In the Reserve account schedule drop-down list, select the reserve account schedule you 

want to assign to the draw model. 

3. 
Use the Status drop-down list to select the draw model’s status. The options include: 

• 
Active: The draw model is active and available. 

• 
Inactive: The draw model is inactive and not available. 

4. 
If you want to restrict the draw model to a specific entity or location, then select the 

Restricted check box. In the Restricted locations drop-down list, select one or more entities 

or locations to which to restrict the draw model. 

This option is necessary only if you do not already restrict your users by entity . 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save.

##### Deleting a Replacement Reserve Draw Model
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 586*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Deleting a Replacement Reserve Draw Model 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Replacement 
Reserves > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Replacement 
Reserves > Edit`


You can delete or inactivate a replacement reserve draw model, depending on whether you want 

to retain its settings. 

Deleting a Draw Model 

If you no longer use a draw model, then you can delete it permanently. After you delete the draw 

model, it can’t be restored. If you’re unsure whether you want to delete it, you can set its status to 

Inactive instead. 

You can’t delete draw models that have one or more draw model details; you’ll have to delete the 
draw model details (on page 565 ) first. 

To delete a draw model: 

1. 
In the Draw models list, find the draw model you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete link next to the draw model. 

3. 
Click OK in the confirmation box. 

The system removes the draw model from the Draw models list. 

Inactivating a Draw Model 

Inactivating a draw model retains the settings and draw model details you’ve defined but hides 

the draw model from the Draw models list. You can reactivate the draw model at any time. 

To inactivate a draw model: 

1. 
In the Draw models list, find the draw model you want to inactivate. 

2. 
Click the Edit link next to the draw model. 

The Draw model page opens. 

3. 
Set the Status to “Inactive”. 

4. 
Click Save. 

The system hides the draw model from the Draw models list and removes it from any 

system drop-down lists. 

Select the Include inactive check box in the Draw models list to see any inactive draw 
models.

##### Adding Replacement Reserve Draw Model Details
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 591*

Chapter 3: Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Adding Replacement Reserve Draw Model Details 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Draw Models 
> Replacement Reserves > Draw Model Details > Add`


Add draw model details to define how replacement reserve costs are structured and displayed on 

a draw. Each detail represents a line on the draw—such as a section header, cost line, or 

total—and controls how costs are grouped, ordered, and rolled up into totals. 

To create multiple draw model details at once, see Importing Draw Model Details (on page 563 ). 

To add or edit draw model details for a replacement reserve draw model: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the 

Setup tab. 

If you do not have a subscription to Job Cost, select the standalone Replacement Reserves 
application instead. 

2. 
In the Draw models section, select the Replacement reserves menu option. 

The Draw models list opens. 

3. 
Click the Draw model details link next to the desired draw model. 

The Draw model details list opens. 

4. 
Click the Add button at the top of the page. 

The Draw model detail page opens. 

5. 
Verify the Draw model name. This identifies which draw model the new line belongs to and 

determines where the line appears when the draw is generated. 

6. 
In the Description field, type a description for the line detail. This label appears on the draw 

for this line (for example, a section name, cost category, or total description). 

7. 
In the Sequence field, type the sequence number of the line detail. This controls the order in 

which lines appear on the draw. Lower numbers display first. 

8. 
In the Total level drop-down list, select a level number (0–5). This determines the 

indentation and grouping of the line. Lines with the same level appear on the same tier and 

are grouped together on the draw. 

9. 
In the Record type drop-down list, define how the line should behave on the draw:  

• 
Title: Displays a header used to organize related lines. This type of line does not carry 

amounts. 

• 
Detail: Represents cost activity. Amounts associated with the line are included based 

on assigned cost codes or mapped reserve accounts. 

• 
Total: Calculates the sum of related detail lines within a section. 

---

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 592*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Cost codes and reserve accounts can only be assigned to Detail lines. Title and Total lines 
are used for structure and calculations only. 

10. 
Click Save. 

Importing Replacement Reserve Draw Model Details 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Draw Models 
> Replacement Reserves > Draw Model Details > Template/Import`


Add draw model details to define how replacement reserve costs are structured and displayed on 

a draw. Each detail represents a line on the draw—such as a section header, cost line, or 

total—and controls how costs are grouped, ordered, and rolled up into totals. 

This topic explains how to import draw model details in bulk. To add lines one at a time, see 
Adding Replacement Reserve Draw Model Details (on page 580 ). 

To import draw model details: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the 

Setup tab. 

If you do not have a subscription to Job Cost, select the standalone Replacement Reserves 
application instead. 

2. 
In the Draw models section, select the Replacement reserves menu option. 

The Draw models list opens. 

3. 
Click the Draw model details link next to the desired draw model. 

The Draw model details list opens. 

4. 
Click the Template button. 

The system either downloads the drawmodeldetail.xls file or prompts you to open or save 

the drawmodeldetail.xls file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

5. 
Open the drawmodeldetail.xls file.  

6. 
For each draw model you want to add, enter the required information: 

• 
DRAWMODELNAME: Enter the draw model Name, including any spaces. 

• 
DRAWMODELDETAILNAME: Enter the name of the draw model detail. 

• 
RECORDTYPE: Complete this field based on the draw model detail level: 

• 
For detail-level draw model details, leave this field blank. 

• 
For title-level draw model details, enter “title”. 

• 
For total-level draw model details, enter “total”. 

• 
TOTALLEVEL: Enter the level number (0–5) of the draw model detail. 

---


<!-- Page 593 -->
Chapter 3: Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

• 
SEQUENCE: Enter the sequence number of the draw model detail.  

• 
STATUS: Complete this field based on the draw model detail status: 

• 
For active draw model details, leave this field blank. 

• 
For inactive draw model details, enter “inactive”. 

The example below shows a draw model detail list. 

7. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as.  

8. 
In the Save as box, use the Save as type drop-down list to select “CSV (comma delimited) 

(*.csv).” 

9. 
Change the File name or location as needed, and then click Save. 

10. 
On the Draw model details page, click Import. The system opens the Import draw model 

detail information box. 

11. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

12. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

13. 
Click Done.

Assigning Reserve Accounts to Draw Model Details 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Draw Models 
> Replacement Reserves > Draw Model Details > Assign Reserve Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Draw 
Workbench > Replacement Reserves > View > Category Mapping`


Assign reserve accounts to draw model lines so that activity is included in the appropriate 

categories on a draw. 

Changes to reserve account assignments apply only to draws that have not yet been posted. 

Before You Begin 

Before you get started, review the Reserve accounts list. This list includes all available reserve 

accounts, even ones that are not currently assigned to a draw model line. The Assign reserve 

accounts page displays only reserve accounts that haven’t been mapped to a lender category. 

Procedures 

To assign reserve accounts: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the 

Setup tab. 

If you do not have a Job Cost subscription, select the standalone Replacement Reserves 
application instead. 

2. 
In the Draw models section, select the Replacement reserves menu option. 

The Draw models list opens. 

3. 
Click the Draw model details link next to the desired draw model. 

The Draw model details list opens. 

4. 
Click the Assign reserve accounts button at the top of the page. 

The Assign reserve accounts page opens. 

5. 
Drag a reserve account to the appropriate line in the Draw model details list. 

• 
Repeat as needed. Each reserve account can be assigned to only one line. 

• 
To remove an assignment, drag the reserve account back to the Reserve accounts list. 

6. 
Click Save.

Funding Sources 

This section shows you how to manage funding sources, which are lenders for your jobs. 

---



#### Funding Source List - Job Cost
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 602*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Funding Source List - Job Cost 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > Setup > Funding Sources > Job Cost`


Use the Funding source list to manage funding sources, which are lenders for your jobs. For each 

funding source, you provide the name and assign the draw model to which the funding source 

applies. From this list, you can: 

• 
View funding sources. 

• 
Add funding sources. 

• 
Delete funding sources. 

• 
Edit funding sources. 

• 
Export funding sources. 

Funding Sources and Draw Schedules 

A job can have one or more funding sources, each of which is associated with a draw model. Draw 

models organize cost codes to draw categories provided by the funding source. 

For example, one job may have one funding source for land development costs, another for soft 

costs (architect fees, interest, insurance), and a third for hard costs (cement, framing, roofing).

##### Adding a Replacement Reserve Funding Source
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 610*

Setting Up Job Cost & Reserves 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding a Replacement Reserve Funding Source 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Funding 
Sources > 
 Replacement Reserves`


To add a replacement reserve funding source: 

1. 
In the Name field, enter the name of the funding source. 

2. 
Use the Draw model name drop-down list to select the draw model to map to the funding 

source. This determines the format of the draw schedule when generating a new draw. 

3. 
If you want to generate invoices in the A/R module when posting draws for this funding 

source, use the Customer for A/R invoice drop-down list to select a customer.  

4. 
In the Escrow reserve account/account group drop-down list, select an account or account 

group so the system knows the funding source balance. 

5. 
In the Reserve funds receivable account drop-down list, select an account to override the 

existing receivable account selected when configuring Accounts Receivable. 

6. 
If you want to be able to add unpaid A/P invoices to a draw, then select the Allow unpaid 

items on draw check box. 

7. 
If you want to restrict the funding source to a specific entity or location, then select the 

Restricted check box. In the Restricted locations drop-down list, select one or more entities 

or locations to which to restrict the funding source. 

This option is necessary only if you do not already restrict your users by entity . 

8. 
When your changes are complete, click Save.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

A/P batch 

A group of A/P transactions—such as invoices or 

credits—entered and posted together. 

A/P configuration 

The collection of settings that define how A/P 

functions behave, including approval rules, 

numbering formats, tolerances, and posting 

options. 

A/P workflow 

The routing and approval structure that 

determines how invoices move through review 

and approval before posting. 

A/R Batch 

A group of A/R transactions—such as charges, 

receipts, or adjustments—entered and posted 

together. 

Account balance 

The total amount recorded in a G/L account for a 

given period, including beginning balance, 

activity, and ending balance. 

Account grouping 

A structure used in financial reports to organize 

G/L accounts into meaningful categories such as 

assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. 

Predefined or custom groupings of G/L accounts 

used for reporting, dashboards, and financial 

analysis. 

Account type 

A classification that determines how an account 

behaves in financial statements (Asset, Liability, 

Equity, Revenue, Expense). 

Accounting period 

Transactions are recorded and separated into 

different reporting periods such as months, 

quarters, and years. The use of reporting periods 

lets you compare past and present performance. 

Accounting reviewer 

A designated role responsible for reviewing and 

approving accounting-related transactions 

before they are posted. 

Accounts 

An account keeps track of what your company 

owns, owes, spends, or receives. Separate 

accounts let you keep separate records for each 

type of asset, liability, equity, revenue, and 

expense. 

Each account can contain several subaccounts, 

which helps organize and manage your finances. 

Each account tracks the activity of its category. 

For example, the Receivables account tracks 

money coming in and the Payables account 

tracks money going out. Each of these accounts 

typically has many subaccounts. For example, the 

Receivables account may have a subaccount for 

each property: 

1201.001 - Accounts Receivable - Fair Haven 

1201.002 - Accounts Receivable - Coconut Grove 

Glossary of Terms
