Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Each account has a beginning balance. You 

record the increases and decreases for a period, 

and at the end of the period, you have the 

resulting ending balance. 

Accrual accounting 

The accrual method of accounting recognizes 

income in the period earned, and expenses in 

the period incurred. The accrual method is a 

better measure of profit and loss. 

Accrued Expenses report 

A report showing expenses that have been 

incurred but not yet paid, used during close to 

validate balances. 

Accumulated depreciation account 

The G/L account credited when depreciation is 

posted. It offsets the asset’s cost on the balance 

sheet. 

Action card 

A dashboard component that provides quick 

access buttons for common tasks or navigation 

shortcuts. 

Actuals 

Financial results of activity in the general ledger 

and used as the baseline for forecasts and 

budgets. 

Adjustment 

A manual increase or decrease to a customer’s or 

vendor’s balance, used to correct errors or apply 

special credits/charges. 

Adjustment codes 

Predefined codes used to categorize manual 

increases or decreases to a customer’s balance. 

Aging buckets 

Time based categories (e.g., 0–30, 31–60 days) 

used to group outstanding receivables or 

payables for reporting. 

Aging report 

A report that groups outstanding balances (A/P 

or A/R) by how long they have been unpaid (e.g., 

0–30, 31–60 days). 

Allocation 

A process that distributes amounts from one 

account or entity to others based on predefined 

rules or percentages. 

Allocation (Expense Reports) 

A method of distributing an expense across 

multiple projects, tasks, or locations. 

Approval levels 

The hierarchy of users or roles authorized to 

approve invoices based on amount, vendor, or 

other criteria.  

The number of approvers required for a role 

(1–4) when that role is assigned to an approval 

policy. 

Approval policy 

A rule that determines which users or roles are 

authorized to approve a transaction based on 

criteria such as amount, vendor, G/L account, 

job, or payment method.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Approval policy manager 

The page in the Company application used to 

create, edit, and organize approval policies. 

Approval queue 

The list of transactions awaiting approval, 

displayed in the Approval Workbench. 

Approval workbench 

An approval workbench is where users review, 

approve, and decline pending transactions. 

Approval workflow 

The routing process that determines who must 

review and approve a transaction before it can 

be posted or paid. A collection of approval 

policies are applied to specific transaction types 

and properties. 

Approver 

An approver is a person responsible for deciding 

to approve or decline a transaction. There are 

three types of approvers: 

• 
General approvers can approve or decline 

only transactions assigned to them or their 

role. 

• 
Unrestricted approvers can approve or 

decline any transaction. 

• 
Delegate approvers can approve or decline 

transactions assigned to another approver. 

Approver permissions 

The system permissions required to create 

approval policies or approve transactions. 

Asset account 

The G/L account representing the asset’s cost. 

Used when posting depreciation and disposal 

entries. 

Asset Activity report 

A report showing additions, disposals, transfers, 

and depreciation activity for selected assets. 

Asset class 

A category of assets that share the same 

depreciation rules and G/L account structure. 

Determines how depreciation is calculated and 

posted. 

Asset Disposal report 

A report showing assets that have been disposed 

of, including gain/loss calculations. 

Asset List report 

A report showing basic asset details such as cost, 

location, class, and placed in service date. 

Asset Reconciliation report 

A report comparing fixed asset balances to G/L 

balances to identify discrepancies. 

Assets 

The tangible and intangible items used in the 

operation of a business. Tangible assets include 

buildings, equipment, and vehicles. Intangible 

assets include the company’s bank account 

balance and A/R invoices representing future 

income from customers. Assets are tracked 

through acquisition, depreciation, transfer, and 

disposal.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Assumptions 

User defined variables—such as inflation rates, 

occupancy targets, or expense growth—that 

drive forecast calculations. 

Attachments 

An attachment is a bundle of one or more 

supporting documents, such as spreadsheets, 

scanned images, or word processor documents. 

Audit trail 

A system record showing changes made to 

transactions or records, including who made the 

change and when. 

Bank account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on the bank account used. 

Bank accounts 

Financial accounts set up in the system for 

issuing payments, recording deposits, 

withdrawals, and performing reconciliations. 

Bank feed 

An automated connection that imports bank 

transactions into reconciliation for matching and 

reconciliation. 

Bank reconciliation 

The process of matching bank activity to general 

ledger transactions to ensure the bank balance 

and book balance agree. 

Bank register 

A chronological list of all transactions recorded 

in a bank account within the system. 

Baseline forecast 

The initial forecast generated from actuals and 

default assumptions before adjustments or 

scenario modeling. 

Batch 

A group of journal entries entered and posted 

together as a single unit. 

Batch report 

A report that displays all transactions included in 

a specific batch, such as A/P invoices or journal 

entries. 

Beginning balance 

The starting balance of a G/L account at the 

beginning of a fiscal period. 

Billable time 

Hours worked on a project that can be invoiced 

to a customer. The Billable Time page allows 

users to generate invoices for approved billable 

hours. 

Book balance 

The balance of a bank account according to the 

general ledger. It can also be the balance from 

the general ledger of a default general ledger 

account set on the bank account. 

Bookmarks / favorites 

User-defined shortcuts to frequently accessed 

pages or modules. 

Books closed 

The state indicating that the accounting period 

has been finalized for a property.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Budget 

A financial plan for a future period that outlines 

expected revenue, expenses, and cash flow. In 

Job Cost, a budget is an estimate of expected 

costs for a job. 

Budget version 

A saved iteration of a budget or forecast, 

allowing comparison between drafts, scenarios, 

or approval stages. 

BVA 

Budget Variance Analysis is an analysis of the 

difference between the amount that you 

budgeted for and the actual amount that you 

spent. 

Calculation model 

The logic used to compute forecasted values, 

such as percentage growth, fixed amounts, or 

driver based formulas. 

Cash accounting 

The cash method of accounting recognizes 

revenue in the same reporting period as the cash 

is received, and expenses in the period in which 

cash payments are made. 

Cash flow forecast 

A projection of expected cash inflows and 

outflows over a defined period. 

Certification / skill 

A credential, license, or skill tracked for an 

employee. Users can add, edit, or delete 

certifications and skills in their profile. 

Charge 

A receivable posted to a customer or tenant 

account for rent, fees, utilities, or other billable 

items. 

Charge schedule 

A configuration that defines when recurring 

charges generate, such as monthly rent cycles. 

Chart of accounts (COA) 

The structured list of G/L accounts used to 

categorize financial transactions. 

Check layout 

The format and design used when printing 

checks, including alignment, fields, and MICR line 

settings. 

Check run 

A batch process that selects, reviews, and prints 

multiple vendor payments at once. 

Child location 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, properties are 

called locations. Subproperties are called child 

locations. 

An entity represents the corporate office of one 

or more locations, responsible for locations’ 

taxes. Every location is associated with an entity. 

An entity can be responsible for one location or 

a large group of locations and child locations.  

A company can be composed of one entity or 

multiple entities. See also Multi-entity companies 

(on page 619).

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Cleared transaction 

A payment or deposit that has been matched to 

bank activity during reconciliation. 

Cloned dashboard 

A duplicate of an existing dashboard that can be 

edited independently. 

Close account 

A close account is a G/L account used to track 

job completion. 

Close checklist 

A list of tasks required to complete the financial 

close for a period. Can be generated 

automatically or manually. 

Close console 

A centralized page for managing close activities, 

including generating checklists, opening/closing 

books, and viewing charts. 

Close workbench 

A workspace that displays close tasks, checklists, 

and work paper actions for selected properties. 

Closing period 

The process of finalizing a fiscal period so no 

additional transactions can be posted. 

Coding 

Assigning G/L accounts, properties, entities, and 

other classifications to an invoice or credit. 

Commitment 

A commitment, or purchase order, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount. 

Component 

An individual element displayed on a dashboard, 

such as a chart, list, report, performance card, 

calendar, or smartlink. 

Component controls 

The actions available on each dashboard 

component, such as edit, delete, expand, 

collapse, or move. 

Component group 

A collection of dashboard components grouped 

together for organization or layout purposes. 

Component permissions 

Permissions required to view the underlying data 

of a dashboard component. Users must have 

access to the data source (e.g., A/P invoices, G/L 

accounts) to see the component. 

Concession 

A concession is a negative charge awarded to 

the customer as a short-term incentive. Examples 

of concessions include waived fees, reduced rent, 

nuisance discounts, and renovation credits.  

Console page 

A dashboard style page showing close status, 

charts, and tools for generating checklists and 

managing books.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Consolidation 

Combining financial data from multiple entities 

into a single set of financial statements. 

Contra accounts 

A contra account is an account which offsets and 

reduces or offsets the balance of another 

account. You can have contra accounts for both 

assets and liabilities. 

A contra asset account has a credit balance and 

offsets and decreases the debit balance of the 

related asset account. An example of a 

contra-asset account is Accumulated 

Depreciation Autos & Vehicles account, which 

reduces the Automobiles & Vehicles account to 

arrive at the net value. 

A contra-liability account has a debit balance 

and offsets and decreases the credit balance of 

the related liability account. 

Cost code 

A cost code is a way to track a specific cost 

based on nature or function. 

Cost code policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific cost code. 

Cost coding 

Cost coding is a method of grouping individual 

costs based on their nature, function, or work 

phase. 

Credit memo 

A credit memo increases the overall amount you 

owe a vendor. It is typically a vendor-issued 

document that reduces the amount owed on an 

invoice. 

Custom field 

A user-defined field added to records or 

transactions to capture additional data not 

included in standard RealPage fields. 

Custom field wizard 

The guided tool used to create new custom 

fields, define field types, and configure visibility. 

Custom report 

A user built report that pulls data from Financial 

Suite records, transactions, and custom fields, 

allowing flexible filtering, grouping, and 

calculations. 

Custom report wizard 

A step-by-step tool for building custom reports, 

including selecting data sources, defining 

columns, adding filters, grouping, and setting 

prompts. 

Custom view 

A personalized list view that displays selected 

columns, filters, and sorting for any application’s 

list pages. 

Customer / tenant ledger 

A detailed record of all charges, payments, 

adjustments, and balances for a specific 

customer or tenant. 

Dashboard 

A workspace where users can pin frequently 

used reports for quick access, and display

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

business insights using components such as 

charts, KPIs, lists, and reports. 

Dashboard library 

A collection of prebuilt dashboards available for 

installation, typically provided when a company 

is created using a QuickStart template. 

Data import wizard 

A tool used to import data such as vendors, 

customers, G/L accounts, or transactions into the 

Financial Suite. 

Data mapping 

The process of aligning fields in your import file 

with the corresponding fields in the Financial 

Suite so the system knows where each value 

belongs. 

Data source (primary data source) 

The record or transaction type selected as the 

foundation for a report (e.g., Customer, A/P 

Invoice Detail, G/L entry). 

Data template 

A predefined spreadsheet or CSV layout 

provided by RealPage that specifies the required 

columns and formatting for a successful import. 

Debit memo 

A debit memo decreases the overall amount you 

owe that vendor. 

For example, if you receive a credit memo from a 

vendor, enter it as a debit memo to reduce the 

amount you owe that vendor. 

Debits and credits 

In common use, credit generally has positive 

associations; in accounting, credit is associated 

with decreases in asset, expense, and equity 

accounts. 

Debits increase balances in asset and expense 

accounts and decrease balances in liability 

accounts, revenue accounts, and capital 

accounts. 

Credits increase balances in liability, revenue, 

and capital accounts, and decrease balances in 

asset and expense accounts. 

Debit accounts are asset and expense accounts 

that usually have debit balances; the total debits 

usually exceed the total credits in each debit 

account. 

Credit accounts are revenue (income, gains) 

accounts and liability accounts that usually have 

credit balances. 

Declining balance (100/150/200) 

A depreciation method that accelerates 

depreciation by applying a percentage to the 

asset’s remaining book value. 

Default dashboard 

The dashboard automatically displayed when a 

user logs in. 

Default settings 

Predefined values that automatically populate 

fields when creating records, such as default G/L 

accounts or payment terms (A/P), or default 

charge codes or payment application rules (A/R).

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Delegate 

The approver who assumes your responsibility 

for approving transactions while you are out of 

the office. Any approvals that have been 

delegated while you are out of the office remain 

with your delegate, even if you turn off the 

out-of-office notification before the delegate has 

approved or declined the transaction. 

Deposit 

Funds received and recorded in a bank account, 

often grouped into a deposit batch for posting. 

Deposit batch 

A group of deposits entered and posted 

together. 

Depreciation batch 

A batch of depreciation journal entries generated 

for a period. Can be posted, viewed, or deleted. 

Depreciation expense account 

The G/L account debited when depreciation is 

posted. 

Depreciation journal entry 

The G/L entry created when depreciation is 

posted, debiting expense and crediting 

accumulated depreciation. 

Depreciation schedule 

The system generated schedule showing 

depreciation amounts for each period over the 

asset’s useful life. 

Depreciation schedules (financial vs. 
tax) 

Separate schedules that allow different 

depreciation rules for GAAP and tax reporting. 

Detail data source 

A data source option that includes both header 

and line item information for transactions (e.g., 

A/P Invoice Detail). 

Detail ledger 

A record showing all transactions posted to a 

specific G/L account. 

Detail report 

A report that includes line item or transaction 

level information rather than summarized totals. 

Dimension report structures 

Dimension report structures are named 

structures that you can create for the purpose of 

adding custom analysis to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. You can add dimension 

structures for any dimension that you have in 

your company. 

Disbursement 

Any outgoing cash transaction, such as checks, 

ACH payments, or manual payments. 

Document template 

A customizable Word-based template used for 

printed documents such as invoices, statements, 

sales orders, and purchase orders.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Document type 

The category of document associated with a 

report, such as invoices, statements, or purchase 

orders. 

Draft asset 

An asset imported from an external system that 

has not yet been activated. 

Draft expense report 

An expense report that has been created but not 

yet submitted for approval. 

Draw 

In Job Cost & Reserves, a draw summarizes 

invoiced costs by combining job activity into 

predetermined categories. After it’s summarized, 

you can provide the draw to the funding sources 

of the job. 

Draw model 

A draw model is an agreement between a lender 

and your company that lists the budgeted items 

approved for funds. 

Driver 

A variable that influences forecasted values (e.g., 

occupancy, rent growth, utility usage). 

Due date 

The date by which a vendor invoice must be 

paid. 

eInvoice 

A system-generated A/P invoice created by 

Spend Management Storefront. 

Entity 

An entity record contains a property’s or 

location’s accounting and legal details, such as 

the business name and address as they should 

appear on A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and tax 

forms. An entity contains the accounting 

information of a location/property or property 

management company. 

In a multi-entity environment, entities are 

distinct—but nearly identical—companies or 

business units that are fully owned by a 

corporate or headquarters entity. Entities can 

represent divisions managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized 

payables and receivables and a common chart of 

accounts. 

Exception 

A transaction that does not match bank activity 

during reconciliation and requires review or 

correction. 

Expense report 

A form used to record reimbursable expenses. 

Users can add receipts, allocate expenses, and 

submit for approval. 

FAS 

A final account statement (FAS) is a document 

that provides a detailed record of a transaction’s 

activity. 

Filter 

Criteria applied to limit which records appear in 

a report.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Final work paper package 

The completed, approved set of work papers for 

a period, locked after approval. 

Fiscal calendar 

The structure of accounting periods and fiscal 

years used for reporting and posting. 

Forecast 

A forward looking projection of financial 

performance based on actuals, assumptions, and 

drivers. 

Forecast cycle 

The defined period for creating, reviewing, and 

finalizing forecasts (monthly, quarterly, annually). 

Funding source 

A funding source is a lender for a job. 

G/L account (general ledger account) 

A financial account used to categorize 

transactions for reporting and posting. A G/L 

account is associated with each charge or 

payment. 

G/L account group 

A predefined group of G/L accounts that can be 

selected instead of individual account ranges. 

G/L account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific G/L account or 

account range. 

G/L group 

A collection of G/L accounts grouped for 

reporting, allocations, or approval routing. 

Global (top level) setup 

Configuration performed at the top level that 

applies to all entities in the portfolio. 

Home page 

The landing page provides quick access to 

dashboards, tasks, and frequently used modules. 

Import log 

A system-generated record that shows which 

rows were imported successfully and which 

failed, including error messages. 

Initial posting date 

Revaluation reports help you manage 

unrecognized gains and losses from the 

fluctuation in exchange rates. Set the initial 

posting date on this report as the end of the 

month. 

Injection (smart rules / smart events) 

A dynamic value inserted into a rule or event 

action, such as a field value, date, or user 

information. 

Interim financing 

Interim financing, or construction loan, is a 

deployment of capital for short-term 

development, such as the acquisition and 

renovation of properties. This capital is typically 

provided by a lender.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

When the project is complete, owners pay the 

construction loan and replace it with permanent 

financing. 

In-transit item 

A transaction recorded in the system but not yet 

reflected on the bank statement (e.g., 

outstanding checks, deposits in transit). 

Invoice (A/P) 

A vendor’s bill for goods or services received. 

Invoice (A/R) 

A document generated to bill a customer for 

charges owed. In A/R, invoices may be created 

manually or automatically. 

Invoice entry 

The process of entering vendor invoices into the 

A/P module for approval and posting. 

Invoice matching 

The process of comparing an invoice to purchase 

orders, receipts, or expected amounts before 

approval. 

Invoice numbering rules 

Settings that determine how invoice numbers are 

validated, formatted, or restricted. 

Job 

A job is a method of tracking the work and 

expenses related to construction at a property. 

Jobs are used for job costing and approval 

routing. 

Job policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific job. 

Job type 

A classification of jobs used for approval policies 

and reporting. 

Job type policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a job type. 

Journal entry 

A journal entry documents the movement of 

money. When you add a journal entry, you enter 

an accounting transaction into the records. Every 

journal entry must include at least two equal and 

offsetting entries. This is because every 

transaction involves a change in at least two 

places in the accounting records, and the total of 

all debits and credits must balance. 

Key performance indicator (KPI) 

A measurable metric used to evaluate financial 

or operational performance (e.g., NOI, occupancy 

rate). KPIs can be displayed on performance 

cards on a dashboard to show financial or 

operational performance. 

Late fee 

A charge applied when a customer fails to pay by 

the due date, based on configured rules. 

Late fee rules 

Configuration that determines when late fees 

apply, how they are calculated, and which charge 

codes they use.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Ledger 

The complete set of financial accounts used to 

record all transactions for an entity or portfolio. 

Line item 

An individual revenue or expense entry within a 

transaction such as an invoice, purchase order, 

budget or forecast. 

Loan schedule 

A loan schedule is a list of all payments 

previously paid (historical purposes only) or due 

to the lender for the loan. 

Lookup values 

Reference lists—such as vendors, charge codes, 

or account types—that must exist in the system 

before certain imports can succeed. 

Manual entry 

A bank transaction entered directly into the 

system rather than imported through a bank 

feed or processed by AI. 

Manual journal entry 

A journal entry created directly by a user rather 

than generated by a subsystem such as A/P or 

A/R. 

Matching 

The process of pairing bank activity with 

corresponding G/L transactions during 

reconciliation.  

M-console 

The M-console is the management console used 

by administrators to create and manage multiple 

RealPage Accounting Suite environments. 

M-console access is different from RealPage 

Accounting Suite system access. To access the 

M-console, you must have a separate account in 

the M-console. 

Most implementations of RealPage Accounting 

Suite do not need the M-console. 

Memorized report 

A saved version of a report with preset filters, 

parameters, and formatting for quick reuse. 

Merge field 

A placeholder inserted into a Word document 

template that pulls data from the Financial Suite 

when the document is generated. 

Monthly checklist 

A checklist used for monthly close activities. 

Multi year forecast 

A projection that spans multiple fiscal years, 

often used for long term planning. 

Multi-entity companies 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, a parent property 

is called a location, and a subproperty is called a 

child location. A location must have an entity 

associated with it. The entity handles the 

accounting and tax activities for its location and 

any child locations. 

In a multi-entity shared corporation, entities 

represent a separate tax identification or a 

separately secured, fully balancing set of books. 

Entities typically represent properties, or 

locations, which are managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Performance card 

A dashboard component that displays KPIs, 

trends, or financial metrics in a compact visual 

format. 

Period activity 

The total debits and credits posted to an account 

within a specific accounting period. 

Period close 

The workflow used to review, adjust, and finalize 

financial activity before closing an accounting 

period. 

Periodic tasks 

Recurring A/P activities performed on a regular 

schedule, such as check runs, recurring invoice 

generation, or reconciliation. 

Permission 

The rights required to view and work with data 

and access pages. 

A permission allows you to access a single 

function. When RealPage adds a new feature to a 

product, the feature often comes with new 

permissions that you must enable before users 

can use the new feature. The word “Right” and 

the word “Permission” refer to the same thing. 

When you use the Unified Platform, they are 

referred to as rights. When you set up access to 

functions in the Financial Suite, they are referred 

to as permissions.  

Permit 

A permit is a category that organizes job 

attachments by type or function. 

Placed in service date 

The date the asset begins being used. 

Depreciation starts based on this date. 

PO 

An abbreviation for purchase order (on page 

622). 

Policy type 

The category of rule used to determine approval 

routing (User, Amount, Tiered Amount, Vendor, 

Vendor Type, G/L Account, Job, Job Type, Cost 

Code, Accounting Reviewer, Journal Type, 

Payment Method, Bank Account). 

Positive Pay 

Positive pay is an automated service that the 

bank offers to help detect fraud by matching a 

company’s check with the check presented for 

payment.  

You can use the RealPage Financial Suite Positive 

Pay feature to generate a Positive Pay file and 

transmit the list of checks to the bank for review. 

The bank compares the amount, check number, 

and account number to ensure that they match. 

Non-matching checks are flagged and sent back 

to the check issuer for review. 

You can also configure the system to submit 

Positive Pay files on a schedule. When a schedule 

is configured, the system generates the Positive 

Pay files containing a list of checks on the 

scheduled dates and automatically sends them 

to the bank. 

Posting 

The action that finalizes a transaction and 

records it in the general ledger.

When you post a transaction, you are

behavior and posting dates.

reporting and setup. 

Prompts

allow filtering at runtime.

financial activity is tracked separately.

application. 

PTO approvals

decline PTO requests. 

PTO request

time off. 

PTO types

vacation, sick leave, or personal time. 

Punchout vendor

vendor allows customers to browse his product 

catalogs online and then purchase goods or 

services within the client’s e-procurement 

system. 

Purchase order

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount.

Sequences

automatic document numbering feature used to 

assign unique identifiers to new records. This 

helps ensure consistency and avoids duplication.

sequencing, is available only for select 

transactions and records in RealPage 

Accounting. Document sequencing uses 

pre-defined numbering plans to assign 

sequential identifiers to new records or 

transactions, such as customer records or A/R 

invoices. Document sequencing is a two-step 

process. First, you configure the numbering 

scheme, then you assign the scheme to the type 

of record or transaction.  

Service charge 

A bank fee recorded during reconciliation to 

adjust the book balance.

Site Experience 

The Site Experience is a scaled-down version of 

Spend Management in a simplified interface. 

While the Spend Management application in the 

RealPage Financial Suite offers more robust 

functionality, most users can accomplish their 

procurement-to-payment processes from the 

Site Experience. 

The Site View option opens Site Experience. The 

Site View menu option is available in the Spend 

Management, General Ledger, and Accounts 

Payable application menus. 

Smart event 

An automation that triggers an action—such as 

sending an email, making an API call, or posting 

an HTTP request—when conditions are met. 

Smart rule 

A rule that triggers warnings or errors to guide 

user behavior when certain conditions are met. 

Smartlink 

A dashboard component that provides a 

clickable link to another page, report, or 

application. 

Source entity 

The paying entity. The entity that is the source of 

the money in a transaction between two or more 

entities. 

Splits 

A line within a transaction that records the 

account and amount of money involved is called 

a split. 

Spread method (budgeting) 

The rule used to distribute annual amounts 

across months (e.g., evenly, seasonally, 

driver-based). 

Staff expenses

members by administrators or managers. 

Staff timesheets 

Timesheets created or managed by supervisors 

for their staff. 

Standard report 

A pre-built Financial Suite report that cannot be 

modified but can be exported or memorized. 

Statement 

A statement, or Statement of Account, is 

essentially a report. It’s a snapshot that includes 

all open and unapplied transactions at the time 

the snapshot was taken—usually at the end of a 

period. 

Statement balance 

The ending balance shown on the bank 

statement for the reconciliation period. 

Straight line depreciation 

A depreciation method that spreads the asset’s 

cost evenly over its useful life.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Subledger 

A subledger is a ledger containing all of one kind 

of transaction. For example, a subledger may 

contain all accounts receivable transactions, or 

accounts payable transactions, or fixed asset 

transactions. All transactions in all subledgers roll 

up into the general ledger. 

Submitted (timesheet status) 

Indicates that a timesheet has been submitted 

and is awaiting approval. 

Sum of years digits (SYD) 

An accelerated depreciation method that applies 

a decreasing fraction of the asset’s cost each 

year. 

Summary 

Summaries are collections of the same type of 

transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, 

no line items appear in the Summaries list. 

Summaries can be either open or closed. When 

summaries are open in Accounts Receivable, you 

can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits. In 

designing an accounts receivable process, the 

system administrator can give access to the 

pages involved with managing invoices but not 

opening or closing summaries. 

Summary report 

A high level report that aggregates data without 

showing line item detail. 

Suspense account 

A temporary account used to hold transactions 

that require review or correction. 

System journal 

A system journal is a journal that is used by the 

system. Users can designate a journal as a 

system journal. Users cannot add journal entries 

to system journals, and system journals are 

excluded from appearing in manual journals 

drop-down lists. 

Target (budgeting) 

A predefined financial goal used to guide 

budgeting or forecasting (e.g., NOI target, 

expense cap). 

Task (Financial Close Management) 

An individual close activity, such as reconciling a 

subledger or reviewing a report. 

Task (Time & Resources application) 

A specific activity within a project. Tasks must be 

created before they can be selected on 

timesheets. 

Template version (importing) 

The specific RealPage-approved layout for an 

import file. Using an outdated version can cause 

errors. 

Tenant / customer 

The individual or organization responsible for 

paying charges recorded in A/R. 

Three-way tie 

A reconciliation requirement ensuring that the 

bank balance, book balance, and cleared balance 

all match.

RealPage® Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide 

Tiered amount policy

through multiple approval tiers based on 

increasing amount ranges. 

TIH 

Trust Interest Holder

The list where approvers review and approve or

Timesheet 

A weekly record of hours worked on projects and 

tasks. Users can add comments, submit for 

approval, and track status. 

Timesheet periods 

Defined weekly or biweekly periods used for 

time entry. Administrators open and close 

periods as needed. 

Tolerance percentage 

The allowable variance between an invoice and 

the expected amount before manual approval is 

required. 

Transaction date

reporting. 

Transaction detail 

Line-level information associated with a 

transaction, such as invoice items or journal 

entry lines. 

Transaction type 

The category of transaction, such as invoices, 

journal entries, or payments. 

Transactions 

A transaction represents money flowing from 

one account to another. Whenever you spend or 

receive money, or transfer money from one 

account to another, it is represented as a 

transaction. 

In double-entry accounting, transactions always 

involve at least two accounts—a source account 

and a destination account. 

Transfer 

A movement of funds between two bank 

accounts within the system. 

Transfer (asset transfer) 

Moving an asset from one location, entity, or 

department to another. 

Trial balance 

A report showing all G/L accounts with 

beginning balances, period activity, and ending 

balances. 

Unapplied payment 

A payment that has been received but not yet 

applied to specific charges. 

Unapplied payment handling 

Rules that determine how payments are stored 

when they cannot be matched to specific 

charges.

About Job Cost

Job costs are expenses associated with property improvements
and new developments, such as capital improvement projects,
renovations, and new constructions. With the job cost features
in RealPage Financial Suite, you can track and manage every
phase of a project through completion, from budget estimates
to revisions to final costs.

Adding a Cost Structure

Set up at least one cost structure per set of cost codes that use
different levels.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.

2. Select 
 Cost structure definition.
3. Type a Cost structure name (e.g., "Div-Phase-Subphase").
4. Select the number of Cost structure levels.
5. Type or select a Name, Type, and Limit for each cost structure
level.
6. Click Save.

Adding a Job Type

Add job types to record account numbers that you can use for
journal entries or job invoices and to control the billing,
segment, and cost code settings of jobs.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.

2. Select 
 Job types.
3. Type a Name for the job type.
4. Select the Cost structure name that applies to the job type.
5. If the job type is billable, select Billable.
6. If the job type uses segments to track budgets and costs, select
Segments enabled.

▪
Select the Segment type.
▪
Select Budget by segment type if you want to budget the
job type to the segment level.

7. If you want to restrict the job type to specific entities or
locations, select Restricted.

▪
Select one or more Restricted locations.

8. Click Save.

Adding a Cost Code

Add a cost code to track a job's budget, costs, and progress at
a detailed level.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.
2. Select Job types.
3. Click the Cost codes link next to a job type.
4. Click Add.

5. Type a Cost code description.
6. Depending on the number of levels in the cost code structure, fill
in the following fields:

▪
Division (Level 1)
▪
Phase ((Level 2)
▪
Sub-phase (Level 3)
▪
Segment 1 (Level 4)
▪
Segment 2 (Level 5)

7. Select a WIP account and Close account.
8. Click Save.

Adding a Job Cost Draw Model

Add a draw model to map cost codes to draw model details or
lender categories.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.

2. In the Draw models section, select 
 Job cost.
3. Type a Draw model name.
4. Select one or more Job types.
5. If you want to restrict the draw model to specific entities or
locations, select Restricted.

▪
Select one or more Restricted locations.

6. Click Save.

Adding Draw Model Details

Add draw model details to map your cost codes to draw
categories provided by your funding sources.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.
2. In the Draw models section, select Job cost.
3. Click the Draw model details link next to the draw model.
4. Click Add.
5. Type a Description of the draw model detail.
6. Type the Sequence number of the draw model detail.
Draw model details are listed from lowest to highest on draws.
7. Select the draw model detail level (0–5) from the Total level
drop-down list.
8. Select a Record type for the draw model detail:

▪
Title: Title lines show as category headers on draws.
▪
Detail: Job costs apply to detail lines based on the cost
codes assigned to the draw model detail.
▪
Total: Total lines calculate the totals of all detail lines
between the total line and the most recent title line in the
draw model detail sequence.

9. Click Save.

Assigning Cost Codes to Draw Model Details

Assign cost codes to the draw model detail folders.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.
2. In the Draw models section, select Job cost.
3. Click the Draw model details link next to the draw model.
4. Click Assign cost codes.
5. Drag the Chart cost code to the appropriate Draw model
details folder.

You can't assign a cost code to more than one draw model
detail.

6. Click Save.

Adding a Job Cost Funding Source

Add details about your funding sources or lenders.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.

2. In the Funding sources section, select 
 Job cost.
3. Type a Name for the funding source.
4. Select a Draw model name to map to the funding source.
5. Select a Customer for A/R invoice to generate A/R invoices
for that customer when posting draws.
6. If you want to restrict the funding source to specific entities or
locations, select Restricted.

▪
Select one or more Restricted locations.

7. Click Save.

Adding a Job

Enter details about a job to help manage job status and
budgets.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Jobs.
3. Fill in basic job information.
4. Type or select the job start and completion dates.
5. If the job type is billable, fill in the customer or internal billing
information.
6. Add permits and attachments.
7. Assign job reporting codes.
8. Add authorized users who can view and manage the job.
9. Click Save.

Viewing the Job Status

Customize a job status inquiry to review budgets and
commitments for jobs.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.
2. Select Job status inquiry.
3. Set your filters:

▪
As of date: Type or select the date from which to calculate
balances.
▪
Select report codes: Select one or more report codes.
▪
Parent job: Select a parent job to filter the inquiry by all
child jobs under a parent job.
▪
Job: Select one or more jobs to filter the inquiry by a single
job or multiple jobs.
▪
Job type: Select a job type to filter the inquiry by all jobs
within a specific job type.

4. If you selected multiple jobs, select Consolidated to
consolidate budget and cost information.
5. Select the Cost structure level for which you want to view
budgets.
6. Select the Level of detail (cost structure levels) to show.
7. To hide cost code numbers from the report, select Hide cost
code.
8. To show the job cost description next to the job name, select
Include job description.
9. To display "0.00" when the Cost to complete amount is a
negative value, select Prevent negative cost to complete.
10. Click Apply filters.

Approving or Declining a Budget Change Order

Update the approval status of submitted budget change orders.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.
2. Select Approve budget change orders.
3. Set filters to display transactions pending approval.
4. Click Apply.
5. Select the transaction(s) that you want to approve or decline.
6. In the Comments field, type the reason you are approving or
denying the change order.
7. Click Approve or Decline.

Adding a Job Budget

Add a budget for jobs in the Pending or Active status.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Budgets.
3. Select the Job and Cost Code to which the budget applies.
4. Type the budget Amount.

5. In the Prior commitments offset field, type the amount by
which to offset the Open commitments amount for the cost
code.
6. Select Billable to track costs to this budget with A/P invoices.
7. Click Save.

Adding a Budget Change Order

Add a budget change order for jobs in the Active (budget
locked) status.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.
2. Select Budgets.
3. Click Change order for the budget you want to adjust.
4. Click Add.
5. Type or select the Effective date of the change order.
6. Type the Amount of the change order.
7. In the Prior commitments offset field, type the amount by
which to offset the Open commitments amount for the cost
code.
8. In the Comment field, type the reason for the adjustment.
9. Select any Attachments to include in the change order.
10. Click Save.

Closing a Job

Use this option sparingly. Closing a job creates a credit to the
selected cost codes, effectively zeroing them out on the job
status view.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.
2. Select Close job.
3. Select the Job you want to close.
4. Select a Close option:

▪
Completed job: Closes the entire job.
▪
Selected cost codes: Closes the selected Cost codes.

5. Type or select a G/L posting date for the closing journal entry.
6. Optionally, enable additional settings:

▪
Exclude job history: Exclude the job cost history from the
journal entry.
▪
Create fixed assets: Create fixed assets for any cost code
whose Close account matches an asset account on a
fixed asset class.
▪
Summarize by account: Group cost codes that use the
same WIP account and Close account in one closing
journal entry.

7. Click Preview close.
8. Review the preview, and then click Proceed.

Adding a Permit

Create permits to categorize job attachments.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the Setup tab.

2. Select 
 Permits.
3. Type a Name and Description for the permit.
4. Click Save.

Adding a Job Segment Budget

Use this feature to add a job segment budget if your job
involves segment levels.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.

2. Slect 
 Job segment budgets.
3. Select the Job name, Cost code, and Unit (or Segment) to
which the budget applies.
4. Type the budget Amount.
5. Click Save.

Adding a Job Segment Budget Change Order

Add a job segment budget change order if the job status is
Active (budget locked).

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.
2. Select Job segment budgets.
3. Click Change order for the segment budget you want to adjust.
4. Click Add.
5. Type or select the Effective date of the change order.
6. Type the Amount of the change order.
7. In the Comment field, type the reason for the adjustment.
8. Select any Attachments to include in the change order.
9. Click Save.

Adding a Job Cost Draw

A draw summarizes invoiced costs by combining job activity
into predetermined categories.

1. In Job Cost & Reserves, click the All tab.
2. Select Draw workbench.
3. Select the Job cost filter.
4. Click Add.
5. On the Draw schedule tab, enter the draw and funding source
details.
6. On the Cover page tab, type any text you want to include on
the draw's cover page.
7. On the Attachments tab, select a file to attach to the draw
package.
8. Click Save.

## Replacement Reserves
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 5*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 

Replacement Reserves 

Replacement reserves are funds that are set aside to periodically replace or repair building components during the 

building’s economic life, such as roofs, parking lots, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems. 

With the application’s Replacement Reserves features, you can track replacement and repair expenses and then 

organize and package them as reimbursement requests to your lender(s). 

Additionally, you can: 

• 
Generate draw request packages with supporting documents to present to the lender for reimbursement. 

• 
Maintain lender information in corporate Accounts Receivable. 

• 
Apply receipts after funds are received. 

• 
View a status inquiry report for reserve accounts. 

The Replacement Reserves documentation is divided into three chapters: 

• 
Introduction to Replacement Reserves: (on page 3) This chapter introduces the application’s permissions, 

home page, and menu options. 

• 
Using Replacement Reserves: (on page 9) This chapter describes how to use the application to track and 

manage your reserves. 

• 
Setting Up Replacement Reserves: (on page 105) This chapter describes how to configure draw posting 

information, reserve account schedules, draw models, and funding sources.

Draw Workbench Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench`


Use the Draw workbench page to manage draws for job cost construction lending and for 

replacement reserve escrow requests. A draw summarizes invoiced costs by combining job activity 

into predetermined categories. When it’s summarized, you can provide the draw to the funding 

sources of the job. Draws include invoices as proof of service and material costs from vendors and 

subcontractors.  

From this page, you can: 

• 
Filter draws. 

• 
Add draws. 

• 
View and edit draws. 

• 
Add and reverse draw activities. 

• 
Export the draws list. 

• 
Create and save a custom workbench view. 

If you subscribed to the standalone Replacement Reserves application without Job Cost, then 
the Draw workbench will include only replacement reserve draws.

##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 16*

Using Replacement Reserves 

RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Subscriptions 

You must be subscribed to the Job Cost & Reserves application to manage job cost draws in the 

draw workbench. If you are subscribed to the standalone Replacement Reserves application, then 

you will see only replacement reserve draws in the workbench. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage draws: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Job Cost & Reserves 

or 

Replacement Reserves 

Draw Workbench 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete, Add Activity 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

##### Adding a Replacement Reserve Draw
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 17*

Chapter 2: Using Replacement Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 

Adding a Replacement Reserve Draw 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > Replacement Reserve > Add`


You can add replacement reserve draws individually or import multiple draws using a CSV 

template. 

To add a replacement reserve draw: 

1. 
On the Draw workbench page, select the Replacement reserves option. 

2. 
Click the Add button. 

A blank Draw information page opens. 

3. 
On the Draw schedule tab, fill in the following fields: 

• 
Reserve name: Select a reserve from the drop-down list. 

• 
Draw name: Type a name for the draw. 

• 
Draw number: Type the draw number. 

• 
Draw date: Type or select the date of the draw. 

4. 
On the Cover page tab, use the text editor to create and format a cover page for the draw. 

5. 
On the Attachments tab, select an attachment to include in the draw package. Attachments 

in RealPage Financial Suite can include multiple files. 

6. 
When finished, click Save. 

---



##### Filtering the Draw Workbench
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Using Replacement Reserves 

RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Filtering the Draw Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench`


You can filter the Draw workbench list to display specific job cost draws or replacement reserve 

draws and then save the filtered view for future use. Filters are retained even after you view or 

edit a draw so that you don’t have to reapply the same filters when you return to the workbench. 

If you subscribed to the standalone Replacement Reserves application without Job Cost, then 
the Draw workbench will include only replacement reserve draws. 

Filtering the Draw Workbench 

To filter by job cost draws: 

1. 
Select the Job cost option. 

2. 
If you want to filter draws for a particular property, select the property from the Property 

name drop-down list. 

3. 
If you want to filter draws for a particular job, select the job from the Job name drop-down 

list.  

4. 
Use the Status drop-down list to filter for open or posted draws. 

The list of draws automatically refreshes with your filter selections. 

To filter by replacement reserve draws: 

1. 
Select the Replacement reserves option. 

2. 
If you want to filter draws for a particular reserve, select the reserve from the Reserve name 

drop-down list. 

3. 
Use the Status drop-down list to filter for open or posted draws. 

The list of draws automatically refreshes with your filter selections. 

Saving and Applying a Custom View 

You can save your filter settings to reapply the same workbench view in the future. 

To save a custom view: 

1. 
After you apply your filters, click the Save view as button in the upper-right corner. 

The Save view as box opens. 

2. 
In the View name field, type a name for the custom view. 

3. 
Select the Default view check box if you want to set the view as your default view. 

4. 
Select the Make public check box if you want to share the view with other users. 

---

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find >

To add activity to multiple funding sources allocated by percent type draw: 

1. 
In the Draw workbench list, find the desired draw, and then click the Add activity link in the 

Actions column. 

The Draw information page opens with two lists: 

• 
Items included in this draw: This lists all transaction line items included in the draw. 

• 
Items not yet included on a draw: This lists all of the job’s transaction line items that 

are not included in any draw. 

You can also access this page by clicking the View link next to the draw, and then selecting 
the Add activity link on the Activity tab. 

2. 
To add a single line item to the draw, click the Include link for the desired line item. 

Alternatively, to add all open items to the draw, click the Include all items link.  

To remove a line item from the draw, click the Exclude link for the desired line item. 

3. 
Click the Allocate link for a line item on the draw. 

The Allocate item to multiple funding sources box opens. Each line item is automatically 

allocated to the funding sources assigned to the job, based on the percentages entered on 

the Funding sources tab. 

For example, assume you are allocating a $500.00 line item that is 75% funded by Hartford 

Savings and 25% funded by F&D Trust. When you view the Allocate item to multiple 

funding sources box, the system automatically allocates $375.00 to Hartford Savings and 

$125.00 to F&D Trust. 

4. 
To manually change any funding allocation, in the Amount field, enter the amount that this 

funding source is paying the line item. 

You must also update any additional line items so that the total allocation equals the line 

item amount. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Apply allocation. 

6. 
Repeat steps 5 – 7 for each line item included on the draw.  

7. 
When your changes are complete, click Save. 

If you print the draw schedule, the allocation split shows at the top of the schedule.

Posting a Draw Schedule 

As a best practice, before you post a draw schedule, print the draw schedule and verify that it is 

accurate. For more information, see Printing a Draw Schedule (on page 23). 

Posting a draw schedule moves the draw amounts from the current draw column of the view and 

the report to the previously drawn column.  

You can no longer make adjustments to a draw after posting. We recommend waiting to post the 
draw until after you receive funding.  

To post a draw schedule: 

1. 
Locate the draw you want to post, and then click the View link. 

2. 
Click Post draw schedule. 

A confirmation message shows when the draw posts.  

If you selected the Balance sheet A/R account (debit) check box during Job Cost 

configuration, the system generates an A/R invoice for each applicable funding source that 

has a customer assigned to it in Job Cost setup.

Printing or Exporting a Draw Schedule Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Draw Workbench > View 
> Print/Export Draw Schedule`


To print or export a Draw Schedule report: 

1. 
In the Draw workbench list, click the View link next to the draw whose draw schedule you 

want to print or export. 

The Draw information page opens on the Draw schedule tab. 

2. 
In the Draw schedule section, click the Show reporting and packaging options link. 

A series of reporting and packaging options appears. 

3. 
In the Draw schedule report options section, select which funding sources to include in the 

report: 

• 
Include all sources: Includes all funding sources in the report.  

• 
Include used sources: Includes used funding sources in the report. 

• 
Include no sources: Excludes all funding sources from the report. 

4. 
Click the Print draw schedule or Export draw schedule button. 

• 
If you are printing, a new window opens with the Draw Schedule report in a printable 

format. 

• 
If you are exporting, the Draw Schedule report exports to an Excel file. 

Columns showing previous draws are included when you export the draw schedule so you 
can use them for operational analysis. The printed version of the draw schedule does not 
include these columns.

Before You Begin 

Before you get started, review the Reserve accounts list. This list includes all available reserve 

accounts, even ones that are not currently assigned to a draw model line. The Assign reserve 

accounts page displays only reserve accounts that haven’t been mapped to a lender category.

Setup tab.

application instead.

In the Draw models section, select the Replacement reserves menu option. 

The Draw models list opens. 

3. 
Click the Draw model details link next to the desired draw model. 

The Draw model details list opens. 

4. 
Click the Assign reserve accounts button at the top of the page. 

The Assign reserve accounts page opens.

Drag a reserve account to the appropriate line in the Draw model details list.

Receiving and Posting Draw Receipts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > View > Receive Draw`


After you receive funds for a draw, you can post your draw receipt(s) to the General Ledger. 

To post your draw receipt(s): 

1. 
On the Draw information page, go to the Draw schedule tab, and then click the Receive 

draw button in the Draw schedule section. 

This button appears only after you have posted the draw schedule. 

2. 
In the Draw receipts box, fill in the draw source receipt details: 

• 
In the Amount received field, type the amount received from the funding source. 

Select the Receive all check box to receive the full amount. 

• 
In the Date received field, type or select the date on which you received the funds. 

• 
Select a payment method from the drop-down list. See Payment Methods Overview 

for more information. 

• 
In the Document number field, type the number on the draw receipt. 

3. 
When finished, click the Post receipts button. 

The system creates a deposit in A/R and records the details in the G/L. 

If you receive an error message that the cash account for draws is not defined, then this 
means that you have not defined a Cash account on the Configure Job Cost & Reserves 
page. For multi-entity shared companies, this setting applies to the top level; however, you 
can override it at the entity level.

#### Replacement Reserve Status Inquiry Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 50*

Using Replacement Reserves 

RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Replacement Reserve Status Inquiry Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Daily Tasks > 
Replacement Reserve Status Inquiry Page`


This page lets you summarize the reserves and show the reserve account breakdown.  

By default, the system displays the replacement reserve status based on the system date. 

Replacement Reserve Status Inquiry columns include: 

• 
Reserve name: Lists the reserves 

• 
Reserve accounts: Lists all accounts associated with each reserve 

• 
Category maximum: Lists maximum amount assigned to each account 

• 
Requested to date: Lists the total draw amount requested up to the current date 

• 
Remaining available: The difference between the category maximum date and draw 

amount requested to date

Create an A/P Invoice 

This section shows you how to add job cost A/P invoices. The Create an A/P invoice link in the 

Job Cost & Reserves application menu takes you to the same A/P Invoice page as the one in the 

Accounts Payable application. From this page, you can add standard invoice line items, job cost 

line items, or both. 

See the A/P Invoices section in Accounts Payable for a comprehensive set of topics related to 
A/P invoices. 

---



#### A/P Invoice Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 54*

Using Replacement Reserves 

RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

A/P Invoice Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > All > Search & Find > A/P Invoices`


Use the A/P invoice page to add a new A/P invoice and view and edit an existing A/P invoice. 

After creating the invoice, you can: 

• 
Duplicate the invoice. Click the Duplicate button. 

• 
Print the invoice. Click the Print button. 

• 
Pay the invoice. Click the Pay button. 

• 
Reclassify the invoice. Click the Reclassify button.  

If the button does not appear at the top left, then you cannot reclassify this transaction. 

• 
Post the invoice to the General ledger. Click the Post button. 

• 
Create a recurring transaction based on the invoice. Click the More actions button and then 

select Create recurring transaction. 

• 
View the invoice’s audit trail. Click the More actions button and then select View audit trail. 

• 
View a breakdown of the total balance due to the vendor. Click the Vendor ID balance link 

at the top of the page. 

• 
Associate documents with this invoice and view the attached documents. 

• 
In the OPS section, you can view the approval workflow of an invoice when your system is 

integrated with OPSTechnology. 

• 
In the OPS Attachments section, you can click the URL to view the eInvoice and any 

attachments associated with the eInvoice. This section appears when the invoice type is 

eInvoice or oInvoice. 

In the Invoice Entries section, you can: 

• 
View the available budget for the property. Click the Spend control button. 

• 
Add default values for the invoice entries list. Click the Show defaults link. 

• 
Apply A/P allocations to the invoice. Click the Apply A/P allocation button.  

• 
Save the A/P allocations. Click the Save A/P allocation button. 

• 
Define an allocation split. Click Show details. 

• 
Customize the allocation. Click Show details and then click the Customize allocation 

button. 

• 
Select one or more segment type and segment values to associate with the A/P invoice. 

• 
Use fields shared by Spend Management to help you match the A/P invoice to a purchase 

order. The shared fields include Account code description, Qty, UOM, Price, and Extended 

price.  

The A/P Invoice page can have up to eight sections: 

---


<!-- Page 55 -->
Chapter 2: Using Replacement Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 

• 
At the top is the vendor name, vendor ID in parentheses, and the vendor’s balance, the total 

amount that you owe to the vendor. This section appears only after you have saved the 

invoice. 

• 
The banner section shows basic information about the A/P invoice so that you can find it 

quickly. This section appears only after you have saved the invoice. 

• 
The Date section (so-called because the first field in the section is the Date field) contains 

most of the important information about the A/P invoice.  

• 
The Term section contains further details about the invoice. 

• 
The next section can contain custom fields requested by your company. Consult your 

System Administrator for details. 

• 
The Documents section contains documents related to this A/P invoice. Use this section to 

attach documents, scan documents and to view the attached documents. 

• 
The Currency section appears if your system is multi-currency enabled.  

• 
The Invoice entries section contains the line items that are covered by this A/P invoice.  

The A/P Invoice record can have up to three tabs: 

• 
A/P invoice: This tab contains the essential components of the invoice,  

• 
Messaging: This tab allows you to send a message about this invoice to another system 

user, to an external email address, or to the vendor associated with the A/P invoice. 

• 
Header: This tab contains any custom fields that the property management company wants 

to track. 

---

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf`, Page 58*

Adding an A/P Invoice Manually 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 
 A/P Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > Add`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open 
Invoices and Adjustments > Accounts Payable Invoices > Create`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Search & Find > 
 AP Invoice`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost > Daily Tasks > Create an AP Invoice`


This topic describes how to create an A/P invoice as if every possible feature is enabled. Your 

experience of this page will differ depending on the features that your system has enabled. 

Variations occur due to system configuration, your permissions, and your company’s installation 

of other RealPage Financial Suite applications. 

Applications that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
Spend Management 

• 
Job Cost  

Configuration Differences that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
When your system is configured to use multiple currencies, additional currency fields appear 

in this record. See the multi-currency systems section on the General Ledger configuration 

page. 

• 
When the Intercompany billing option is enabled (Accounts Receivable configuration), the 

A/R Invoice Dimensions section appears. 

• 
When your system is integrated with OpsTechnology, it allows RealPage Accounting to 

receive eInvoices. 

• 
Accounts Payable configuration:  

• 
When the Enable bank account selection in A/P invoice option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Bank account field to appear on the A/P invoice 

record. 

• 
When the Enable invoice entry control validation option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Total invoice amount field to appear on the A/P 

invoice record. 

• 
When Spend management is enabled, then the Match Order button appears, allowing you 

to match a purchase order to the A/P invoice. Additional fields appear on the record such as 

QTY, Price, Extended Price, UOM, and Account code description. 

---

• 
When Job Cost is enabled, the Line Entry Type section appears. When you select Include Job 

cost, the system adds Job cost-specific columns in the Invoice Entries list such as Job name, 

Cost code, and Job unit.  

• 
When scanning is enabled, the Attachments field is replaced with the Documents section, 

affecting the way that you attach documents.  

• 
If the Please complete one-time setup scanner prompt appears, follow the 

instructions in Downloading the Scanning Software. If you do not plan to scan 

supporting documents at this time, you can skip the download by clicking the X in 

upper-right corner of the box.  

• 
If you enabled the Single scan upload feature in your preferences and have previously 

downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the 

software when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, 

purchase order, or service contract, or scan a document into the document dashboard. 

When this occurs, download the new software. There is no need to uninstall the 

previous version. 

• 
Clicking the Scan button in the Documents section redisplays the scanner prompt. 

Related Permissions 

• 
Permissions for attachments 

• 
Permissions for adding assets 

To create an A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the Date field, type the date of the invoice, or leave it set to today’s date.  

Any date entered here is automatically filled in the G/L posting date field (and to the 

Exchange rate date field if you’re a multi-currency company). You can change either date as 

needed; for example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different 

date. 

2. 
In the G/L posting date field, type the date that you want the A/P invoice to post on the 

general ledger.  

3. 
In the Total invoice amount field, type the amount of the invoice.  

This field appears only when the Enable invoice entry control validation check box is 

selected on the configuration page of Accounts Payable. When enabled, this is a required 

field.  

---


<!-- Page 60 -->

4. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select an existing vendor or add a new vendor, as required. 

The system completes the Pay to and Return to fields automatically based on the vendor 

record that you select. This is a required field. 

To add a new vendor, you must be at the top level. You can use the field-level controls to 

add a new vendor, view a vendor’s record, or find a vendor’s record. 

The system fills in the Pay to field automatically. If you need to change the Pay to contact, 

you can do that here. In the Pay to drop-down list, select the name of the person to whom 

the payment should be sent. 

The system fills in the Return to field automatically. If you need to change the Return to 

contact, you can do that here. In the Return to drop-down list, select the name of the 

person to whom returns should be addressed.  

5. 
To fill in the A/P invoice form with data from the last A/P invoice from this vendor, click the 

Populate from last A/P invoice button.  

6. 
In the Invoice number field, type the invoice number. This is a required field. 

7. 
Type a Reference number. Reference numbers can be a vendor’s number that they use to 

track the payment.  

8. 
Type a Description of the transaction.  

You can also use the Reference number and Description fields to enter specific 
information that a vendor requires. Sometimes, a vendor requires a specific piece of 
information to reconcile your payments, such as a customer account number or a pin 
number. 

9. 
Select the Corporate invoice check box if you want to prevent this invoice from appearing 

in Spend Management’s Site Experience. 

10. 
If your company uses the Spend Management application for purchase orders: 

• 
Click the Match order button. 

• 
In the Match orders box, click the View details link. 

• 
In the Contract details section that appears below, select the service order for which 

you want to create an A/P invoice.

Make the Invoice Recurring 

1. 
Select the Make recurring check box to turn this invoice into a recurring invoice. When you 

submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a recurring A/P invoice based on the current 

invoice. When you select this check box, the Schedules section appears.  

2. 
In the Schedules section, fill in the A/P invoice start date field with the date that you want 

the system to start creating the recurring A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select the sequence number scheme from the AP invoice sequence number drop-down list. 

4. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select: 

• 
Never: To keep the invoice perpetually running, select Never. This is common for A/P 

invoices for ongoing services that have a set price. 

• 
Number of occurrences: The End after field appears. To have the invoice run for a 

limited number of times, type the number of times you want the invoice to recur in the 

End after field. This setting is often used for debts that are being paid over time. 

Setting the number of occurrences eliminates the possibility of making payments after 

the debt is paid off. 

• 
End date: To have the invoice recur until a specific date, select End date and then, in 

the End on field, type the date on which the last invoice is to recur.  

5. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, select the frequency that you want the system to 

generate the recurring A/P invoices. The options are: 

• 
None 

• 
Days 

• 
Weeks 

• 
Months 

• 
Years

If you selected Months, then you can select the End of month check box to have the invoice 

created at the end of the month.

The system sends you an email as a reminder on the day before the future draft invoice 
date is to be automatically posted.

 Calendar button and then select the 

date by which to pay the invoice.

In the Attachments field, you can attach any documents related to the invoice. The system

• 
Select the segments that your company uses, and then assign the segment value to each as 

needed. You can also add segments to specific line items in the standard Invoice Entries 

section as needed.  

Saving the A/P Invoice 

When entering the transaction information, save it as a draft or post it. The system validates 

transactions only when they are posted. For example, required departments or locations are not 

validated until posting. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction without affecting the 

subledger or G/L. Later, you or another user can review and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the transaction. 

System Checks for Budget Exceeded  

If you try to post an A/P invoice that exceeds the default budget, and your company uses the A/P 

invoice approval process with the budget exceeded feature, the system displays a warning. The 

system may also prevent you from posting the A/P invoice. If you want to be able to bypass this 

budget check, ask your system administrator to grant you the desired bypass permission. Bypass 

permissions are available for A/P invoices and purchase orders. 

When the budget exceeded feature is enabled, the system checks the A/P invoice amount against 

the budgeted number for the G/L account. When the amount exceeds the budget, then the 

system either displays a warning or prevents you from saving the A/P invoice, depending on how 

your company configured the feature. When preventing an A/P invoice from being posted, the 

system also displays a warning to let you know why you cannot post. 

To enable or disable the budget exceeded feature, see Setting a system action when an A/P 

invoice or purchase order exceeds the budget.  

---


<!-- Page 75 -->
Chapter 2: Using Replacement Reserves 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 

System Checks for Attachments 

Your company may require that you attach a document to support the A/P invoice before you can 

save it as a draft, post, or submit it. If you need to save an A/P invoice without an attachment, 

contact your system administrator and ask them to remove the Require attachment permission 

(on page 51) from your role or account. 

What’s Next? 

When your company uses approvals, A/P invoices first go through the payment approval 

workflow. After payments are approved, you can make the payments.  

Go to the Pay A/P invoices page to select the invoice for payment. When you select Add to 

outbox or Pay now: 

• 
The invoice becomes a payment request. 

• 
The system notifies approvers that a payment is waiting for their approval. 

• 
You can view the status of the payment request in the Payment request list. 

• 
When an approver approves the invoice, the system pays the invoice. 

• 
If the payment method is Check, the system allows the payment to be included in a check 

run.

This column contains the current part of the processing cycle for the A/P

• 
Posted: The A/P invoice was posted to the G/L. 

• 
Selected: The A/P invoice is now selected for payment. 

• 
Paid: Vendor payment was made. 

• 
Partially Paid: Only a partial payment was made. There is a 

remaining amount to be paid. 

• 
Reversed: The A/P invoice was reversed by a second transaction, 

which essentially zeroed out the balance in the GL. Your 

company retains a record of the reversed A/P invoice and the 

reversal transaction for audit trail purposes. 

• 
Reversal: This transaction is created when you reverse a 

transaction and causes the balance to zero out. 

• 
No value: This transaction is posted but has not affected the 

General ledger.

#### Reserves List

RealPage Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide 

Reserves List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > 
Reserves`


Use the Reserves list to view and manage reserve accounts. Replacement reserves simplify how 

you track replacement or repair expenses and then organize and package them as reimbursement 

requests to the lender.  

You can use replacement reserves to: 

• 
Track expenses for reimbursable replacement or repair expenses. 

• 
Generate draw request packages with supporting documents for presentation to the lender 

for reimbursement. 

• 
Apply receipts after receiving funds. 

• 
Run a Reserve Status Inquiry. 

• 
Integrate with the RealPage Accounting Security model. 

From this page, you can: 

• 
View reserve accounts. 

• 
Add reserve accounts. 

• 
Edit reserve accounts. 

• 
Delete reserve accounts. 

---

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage reserves: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Job Cost & Reserves 

or 

Replacement Reserves 

Reserves

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Adding a Reserve 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks >`


 Reserves 

To add a reserve: 

1. 
In the Property drop-down list, select the property you want to associate with the reserve. 

The system auto-populates the Reserve name field with the property name. 

2. 
If you want to override the default name, enter your preferred reserve name. 

3. 
In the Funding source drop-down list, select the funding source for this reserve. 

You can no longer change the funding source after saving. 

4. 
In the Minimum reserve balance field, enter a value that you want to maintain for the 

reserve. The system warns you when the value exceeds the minimum when creating draws 

against this reserve. 

5. 
In the Past months activity allowed on draws field, enter a value to limit the A/P invoice 

records available for selection while creating draws. 

The system auto-populates the Reserve accounts list with all of the reserve accounts 

associated with the selected funding source.  

6. 
In the Maximum amount to be drawn column, enter the maximum withdrawal amount that 

you want to set for each reserve account.

#### Configure Replacement Reserves Page

##### Before You Begin
